title.zh: 卷九十二 列傳第八十: 恩幸
title.raw: 卷九十二 列傳第八十: 恩幸 Volume 92 Biographies 80: Noble Favorites

sentences.zh: 王睿 王仲興 寇猛 趙修 茹皓 趙邕 侯剛 徐紇 宗愛 仇洛齊 段霸 王琚 趙默 孫小 張宗之 劇鵬 張祐 抱嶷 王遇 苻承祖 王質 李堅 秦松 白整 劉騰 賈粲 楊范 成軌 王溫 孟欒 平季 封津 劉思逸 張景嵩 毛暢 郭秀 和士開 穆提婆 高阿那肱 韓鳳齊 諸宦者

translations.literal: Wang Rui, Wang Zhongxing, Kou Meng, Zhao Xiu, Ru Hao, Zhao Yong, Hou Gang, Xu He, Zong Ai, Qiu Luoqi, Duan Ba, Wang Ju, Zhao Mo, Sun Xiao, Zhang Zongzhi, Ju Peng, Zhang You, Bao Ni, Wang Yu, Fu Chengzu, Wang Zhi, Li Jian, Qin Song, Bai Zheng, Liu Teng, Jia Can, Yang Fan, Cheng Gui, Wang Wen, Meng Luan, Ping Ji, Feng Jin, Liu Siyi, Zhang Jingsong, Mao Chang, Guo Xiu, He Shikai, Mu Tipo, Gao Anagong, Han Fengqi, and various eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui, Wang Zhongxing, Kou Meng, Zhao Xiu, Ru Hao, Zhao Yong, Hou Gang, Xu He, Zong Ai, Qiu Luoqi, Duan Ba, Wang Ju, Zhao Mo, Sun Xiao, Zhang Zongzhi, Ju Peng, Zhang You, Bao Ni, Wang Yu, Fu Chengzu, Wang Zhi, Li Jian, Qin Song, Bai Zheng, Liu Teng, Jia Can, Yang Fan, Cheng Gui, Wang Wen, Meng Luan, Ping Ji, Feng Jin, Liu Siyi, Zhang Jingsong, Mao Chang, Guo Xiu, He Shikai, Mu Tipo, Gao Anagong, Han Fengqi, and various eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 夫令色巧言，矯情飾貌，邀眄睞之利，射咳唾之私，乃苟進之常道也。

translations.literal: Flattering looks and clever speech, feigning emotion and adorning one's appearance, seeking the profit of a sidelong glance and aiming at the private favor of a cough or spittle—such is the usual path of unscrupulous advancement.
translations.idiomatic: To put on a pleasing face and honeyed words, to fake feeling and polish one's looks, to court the advantage of a lingering glance and to angle for the intimacy granted in a whispered confidence—these are the ordinary ways by which men claw their way forward.

sentences.zh: 況乃親由褻狎，恩生趨走，便僻俯仰，當寵擅權。

translations.literal: How much more when intimacy arises from indecent familiarity, favor grows from running to and fro, and by fawning and cringing one comes to hold exclusive favor and usurp power.
translations.idiomatic: All the more so when favor springs from vulgar intimacy, when grace is won by scurrying at one's master's heels, and when by obsequious posturing a man comes to monopolize the ruler's affection and wield power unchecked.

sentences.zh: 斯乃夏桀、殷紂所以喪兩代，石顯、張讓所以翦二京焉。

translations.literal: This is why Jie of Xia and Zhou of Yin lost their two dynasties, and why Shi Xian and Zhang Rang brought ruin upon the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: It was by such means that Jie of Xia and Zhou of Yin lost their dynasties, and that Shi Xian and Zhang Rang laid waste to the two imperial capitals.

sentences.zh: 魏世王睿幸於太和之初，鄭儼寵於孝昌之季，宗愛之弑帝害王，劉騰之廢後戮相，此蓋其甚者爾。

translations.literal: In Wei times Wang Rui was favored at the beginning of the Taihe era, Zheng Yan was petted in the closing years of Xiaochang, Zong Ai murdered the emperor and harmed princes, and Liu Teng deposed the empress and killed the chief minister—these were among the most extreme cases.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wei, Wang Rui won favor early in the Taihe reign; in the late Xiaochang years Zheng Yan was doted upon; Zong Ai assassinated the emperor and harmed princes; Liu Teng deposed an empress and executed a chief minister—these were the most flagrant examples.

sentences.zh: 其間盜宮賣爵，污辱宮闈者多矣，亦何可枚舉哉？

translations.literal: In between, those who plundered the palace, sold offices, and defiled the inner quarters were many—how could they all be enumerated?
translations.idiomatic: Between them were countless men who looted the palace treasuries, sold rank, and debased the inner apartments—far too many to list one by one.

sentences.zh: 斯乃王者所宜深誡。

translations.literal: This is what rulers ought to take as a grave warning.
translations.idiomatic: Such conduct is what kings and emperors should heed as a solemn warning.

sentences.zh: 而齊末又有甚焉。

translations.literal: Yet at the end of Qi it was still worse.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the close of Northern Qi the abuse went further still.

sentences.zh: 乃自書契以降，未之有也。

translations.literal: Since the age of written records began, nothing like it had existed.
translations.idiomatic: From the invention of writing down to that time, nothing comparable had ever been seen.

sentences.zh: 若乃心利錐刀，居台鼎之任；

translations.literal: Some whose hearts coveted profit sharp as an awl yet held the burden of the highest offices;
translations.idiomatic: Some men whose hearts were as sharp as awls for gain yet held the highest offices of state;

sentences.zh: 智昏菽麥，當機衡之重。

translations.literal: some whose minds were duller than beans and millet yet bore the weight of the scales of power.
translations.idiomatic: others whose wits could scarcely tell beans from millet yet bore the weight of the empire's balances of power.

sentences.zh: 亦有西域醜胡，龜茲雜伎，封王開府，接武比肩。

translations.literal: There were also ugly barbarians from the Western Regions and miscellaneous performers from Kucha who were enfeoffed as kings, opened their own bureaus, and marched shoulder to shoulder with the great.
translations.idiomatic: There were even hideous barbarians from the Western Regions and variety players from Kucha who were enfeoffed as kings, given their own administrative offices, and ranked shoulder to shoulder with the mighty.

sentences.zh: 非直獨守幸臣，且復多幹朝政。

translations.literal: Not only did they alone monopolize favor; many also meddled in court politics.
translations.idiomatic: They did not merely hoard the ruler's favor; many also meddled directly in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 賜予之費，帑藏以虛；

translations.literal: The cost of bestowals emptied the treasury;
translations.idiomatic: The cost of their largesse emptied the state coffers;

sentences.zh: 杼柚之資，剝掠將盡。

translations.literal: the resources of loom and spindle were stripped almost bare.
translations.idiomatic: and the wealth drawn from every household was stripped nearly to the bone.

sentences.zh: 齊運短促，固其宜哉！

translations.literal: That Qi's fortune was brief was only to be expected!
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder that Northern Qi's reign proved so brief!

sentences.zh: 神武、文襄，情存庶政，文武任寄，多貞幹之臣，唯郭秀小人，有累明德。

translations.literal: Shenwu and Wenxiang still cared for ordinary governance; in civil and military appointments they relied mostly on upright ministers—only the petty man Guo Xiu was a stain on their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan and Gao Cheng still took some interest in ordinary governance; for civil and military posts they chiefly entrusted upright men—only the petty Guo Xiu marred their reputation.

sentences.zh: 天保五年之後，雖罔念作狂，所幸有通州刺史梁伯和、陸芃兒之徒，唯左右驅馳，內外褻狎，其朝廷之事，一不與聞，故不入此傳。

translations.literal: After the fifth year of Tianbao, though the ruler grew heedless and wild, he was fortunate in having men such as Liang Bohe, prefect of Tongzhou, and Lu Peng'er, who merely ran about at his side in private intimacy within and without and heard nothing of court affairs; therefore they are not entered in this biography.
translations.idiomatic: After the fifth year of Tianbao the ruler grew reckless and dissolute, yet he had the likes of Liang Bohe, prefect of Tongzhou, and Lu Peng'er, who merely hurried to and fro at his side in private dalliance and took no part in court business; for that reason they are omitted from this account.

sentences.zh: 大寧之後，奸佞浸繁，盛業鴻基，以之顛覆，生靈厄夫左衽，非不幸也！

translations.literal: After Daning, wicked flatterers grew ever more numerous; the great foundation was overturned thereby, and the people suffered the calamity of having their coats buttoned on the left—no small misfortune!
translations.idiomatic: After the Daning era flatterers multiplied without cease; the splendid foundation of the state was overturned, and the people suffered the disaster of foreign conquest—no small calamity indeed!

sentences.zh: 《魏書》有《恩幸傳》及《閹官傳》，《齊書》有《佞幸傳》。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei has a "Biographies of Favored Favorites" and a "Biographies of Eunuchs"; the Book of Qi has a "Biographies of Flatterers."
translations.idiomatic: The History of the Northern Wei contains accounts of favored favorites and of eunuchs; the History of Northern Qi has an account of flatterers.

sentences.zh: 今用比次，以為《恩幸》篇云。

translations.literal: The present work arranges them by comparison and makes of them this chapter on "Favored Favorites."
translations.idiomatic: Here they are arranged comparatively to form this chapter on favored favorites.

sentences.zh: 舊書鄭儼在《恩幸》中，今從例附其家傳，其餘並編於此。

translations.literal: In the older books Zheng Yan stood among the favored favorites; following precedent his family biography is appended separately, while the rest are compiled here.
translations.idiomatic: In the earlier histories Zheng Yan appeared among the favored favorites; by precedent his family account is attached elsewhere, and the remainder are gathered in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 其宦者之徒，尤是亡齊之一物，醜聲穢跡，千端萬緒，其事闕而不書，乃略存姓名，附之此傳之末。

translations.literal: As for the eunuchs, they were above all an instrument of Qi's destruction; their foul reputations and filthy tracks ran in a thousand strands—since the events are omitted from the text, only their names are briefly preserved and appended at the end of this account.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs were among the chief agents of Qi's fall; their shameful deeds and sordid traces were beyond numbering—because the particulars are passed over in silence, only their names are briefly recorded here at the end of the chapter.

sentences.zh: 其帝家諸奴及胡人樂工叨竊貴幸者，亦附出焉。

translations.literal: Imperial household slaves and barbarian musicians who presumptuously seized high favor are also appended.
translations.idiomatic: Household slaves of the imperial clan and barbarian musicians who presumptuously won high favor are likewise appended.

sentences.zh: 王睿，字洛誠，自雲太原晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Rui, styled Luocheng, claimed for himself that his family was from Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rui, courtesy name Luocheng, claimed descent from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 六世祖橫，張軌參軍。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Heng was a staff officer under Zhang Gui.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Heng had served Zhang Gui as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 晉亂，子孫因居於武威姑臧。

translations.literal: When the Jin fell into disorder, his descendants accordingly settled at Guzang in Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin realm collapsed into chaos, the family settled at Guzang in Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 父橋，字法生，解天文卜筮。

translations.literal: His father Qiao, styled Fasheng, was skilled in astronomy and divination.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiao, courtesy name Fasheng, was versed in astronomy and divination.

sentences.zh: 涼州平，入京。

translations.literal: When Liangzhou was pacified, he entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Liangzhou was pacified, he entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 家貧，以術自給，歷位終於侍御中散。

translations.literal: The family was poor and supported itself by these arts; he rose through office to end as Palace Attendant and Central Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The household was poor and lived by these arts; Qiao rose through office to Palace Attendant and Central Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 天安初，卒，贈平遠將軍、涼州刺史、顯美侯，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Tianan he died; posthumously he was given General Who Pacifies the Distant, Governor of Liangzhou, and Marquis of Xianmei, with the posthumous title Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianan era he died and was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distant, Governor of Liangzhou, and Marquis of Xianmei, with the posthumous title Respectful.

sentences.zh: 睿少傳父業，而姿貌偉麗，景穆之在東宮，見而奇之。

translations.literal: Rui in his youth inherited his father's craft, yet his bearing was imposing and handsome; when Jingmu was in the Eastern Palace he saw him and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Rui in youth learned his father's craft, but his person was imposing and handsome; when Emperor Jingmu was crown prince he saw him and was struck by him.

sentences.zh: 興安初，擢為太卜中散，稍遷為令，領太史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xing'an he was promoted to Central Regular Attendant of the Grand Diviner, and gradually advanced to director, concurrently heading the Astronomical Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Xing'an era he was promoted to Central Regular Attendant of the Grand Diviner, then gradually advanced to director while heading the Astronomical Bureau.

sentences.zh: 承明元年，文明太后臨朝，睿因緣見幸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengming the Empress Dowager Wenming held court; Rui by circumstance won her favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chengming, when Empress Dowager Wenming held court, Rui won her favor through circumstance.

sentences.zh: 超遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was abruptly promoted to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was abruptly promoted to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 俄為散騎常侍、侍令，領太史。

translations.literal: Soon he became Regular Attendant of the Scatterers, Palace Attendant, and concurrently headed the Astronomical Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Regular Attendant of the Scatterers and Palace Attendant, while still heading the Astronomical Bureau.

sentences.zh: 承明元年，文明太后臨朝，睿因緣見幸，超遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengming the Empress Dowager Wenming held court; Rui by circumstance won her favor and was abruptly promoted to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chengming, when Empress Dowager Wenming held court, Rui won her favor and was abruptly promoted to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 俄為散騎常侍、侍中、吏部尚書，賜爵太原公。

translations.literal: Soon he became Regular Attendant of the Scatterers, Palace Attendant, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and was granted the title Duke of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Regular Attendant of the Scatterers, Palace Attendant, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and was ennobled Duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 於是內參機密，外豫政事，愛寵日隆，朝士懾憚焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon within he shared in secrets, without he took part in government; favor grew daily, and court officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he shared in confidential counsel within and took part in government without; his favor grew daily, and court officials stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，孝文及文明太后率百僚與諸方客臨獸圈，有猛獸逸，登門閣道，幾至御坐。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming led the hundred officials and guests from various regions to visit the animal park; a fierce beast broke loose, climbed the gate-tower passage, and nearly reached the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe, Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming led the hundred officials and foreign guests to the animal park when a fierce beast broke loose, climbed the gate-tower passage, and nearly reached the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 左右侍衛皆驚靡，睿獨執戟禦之，猛獸乃退。

translations.literal: The attendants and guards on left and right were all struck down in terror; Rui alone took a halberd to repel it, and the beast then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants and guards on either side were all struck down in terror; Rui alone seized a halberd to drive it back, and the beast withdrew.

sentences.zh: 故親任轉重。

translations.literal: Therefore his intimate trust grew still heavier.
translations.idiomatic: From that time his intimate trust grew still heavier.

sentences.zh: 三年春，詔睿與東陽王丕同入八議，永受復除。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year an edict placed Rui together with the Prince of Dongyang, Pi, among the eight categories of privileged offenders, with perpetual exemption from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year an edict placed Rui together with Prince Pi of Dongyang among the eight categories of privileged offenders, granting perpetual exemption from punishment.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷尚書令，進爵中山王，加鎮東大將軍，置王官二十二人，中書侍郎鄭羲為傅，郎中令以下，皆當時名士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Director of the Department of State Affairs, advanced to Prince of Zhongshan, and given the additional post of Great General Who Pacifies the East; twenty-two officials of the princely household were appointed, with Zheng Xi of the Secretariat as tutor, and the Director of Palace Affairs and those below were all famous men of the day.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Director of the Department of State Affairs, advanced to Prince of Zhongshan, and given the additional title Great General Who Pacifies the East; twenty-two officials of the princely household were appointed, with Secretariat Attendant Zheng Xi as tutor, while the Director of Palace Affairs and those below were all eminent men of the day.

sentences.zh: 又拜睿妻丁氏為妃。

translations.literal: Rui's wife, the Lady Ding, was also ennobled as a princess consort.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's wife, Lady Ding, was also ennobled as a princess consort.

sentences.zh: 及沙門法秀謀逆事發，多所牽引。

translations.literal: When the Buddhist monk Faxiu's plot of treason broke out, many were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: When the Buddhist monk Faxiu's treasonous plot came to light, many were implicated.

sentences.zh: 睿曰：「與殺不辜，寧赦有罪，宜梟斬首惡，余從原赦，不亦善乎！」

translations.literal: Rui said: "Better to spare the guilty than to kill the innocent; the chief culprits ought to be beheaded and displayed, while the rest should be pardoned—would that not be good!
translations.idiomatic: Rui said, "Better to spare the guilty than to kill the innocent. The ringleaders should be beheaded and displayed, while the rest are pardoned—would that not be best?

sentences.zh: 考文從之，得免者千餘人。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this; more than a thousand persons were spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this counsel, and more than a thousand persons were spared.

sentences.zh: 睿出入帷幄，太后密賜珍玩繒彩，人莫能知。

translations.literal: Rui went in and out of the inner curtains; the empress dowager secretly bestowed on him precious objects and silks that no one could know of.
translations.idiomatic: Rui passed in and out of the inner curtains; the empress dowager secretly bestowed precious objects and silks on him that no one else could know of.

sentences.zh: 率常以夜帷載閹官防致，前後钜萬，不可勝數。

translations.literal: He regularly had eunuchs carry them at night in curtained carts; in all, tens of thousands before and after—beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He regularly had eunuchs bring them at night in curtained carts; over time the total ran to tens of thousands, beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 加以田園、奴婢、牛馬雜畜，並盡良美。

translations.literal: Added to this were estates, slaves, cattle, horses, and miscellaneous livestock, all of the finest quality.
translations.idiomatic: To this were added estates, slaves, cattle, horses, and other livestock, all of the finest quality.

sentences.zh: 大臣及左右因是以受賚賜，外示不私，所費又以萬計。

translations.literal: Great ministers and those close to him accordingly received gifts and rewards; outwardly he showed no partiality, yet the sums spent again ran to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers and those around him accordingly received gifts and rewards; outwardly he showed no favoritism, yet the sums spent again ran to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 及疾病、孝文、太后每親視疾，侍官省問，相望於道。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, Emperor Xiaowen and the empress dowager each personally visited his sickness; attendants sent to inquire after him lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, Emperor Xiaowen and the empress dowager each personally visited him; attendants sent to inquire lined the road.

sentences.zh: 及疾篤，上疏陳刑政之宜。

translations.literal: When his illness grew grave, he submitted a memorial setting forth what was fitting in punishments and government.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave, he submitted a memorial on what was fitting in punishments and government.

sentences.zh: 尋薨，孝文、文明太后親臨哀慟。

translations.literal: Soon he died; Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming personally came to mourn in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died; Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming came in person to mourn him in grief.

sentences.zh: 賜溫明秘器，宕昌公王遇監護喪事。

translations.literal: He was granted the warm-bright secret coffin, and Wang Yu, Duke of Dangchang, supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the warm-bright secret coffin, and Wang Yu, Duke of Dangchang, supervised the funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈衛大將軍、太宰、并州牧，諡曰宣王。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand General of the Guard, Grand Tutor, and Governor of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title King Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Grand General of the Guard, Grand Tutor, and Governor of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title King Xuan.

sentences.zh: 內侍長董醜奴營墳墓。

translations.literal: Dong Chounu, chief of the inner attendants, arranged the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chounu, chief of the inner attendants, arranged the tomb.

sentences.zh: 將葬於城東，孝文登城樓以望之。

translations.literal: When he was to be buried east of the city, Emperor Xiaowen ascended the city tower to look upon it.
translations.idiomatic: When he was to be buried east of the city, Emperor Xiaowen ascended the city tower to look on.

sentences.zh: 京都文士為作哀詩及誄者百餘人。

translations.literal: Literary men of the capital composed more than a hundred elegies and dirges for him.
translations.idiomatic: Literary men of the capital composed more than a hundred elegies and dirges for him.

sentences.zh: 乃立睿祀于都南二十里大道右，起廟，以時祭薦，並立碑銘，置守祀五家。

translations.literal: A shrine to Rui was then established twenty li south of the capital on the right of the great road; a temple was raised, sacrifices offered at the proper seasons, an inscription set up, and five households appointed to guard the cult.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine to Rui was established twenty li south of the capital on the right of the great road; a temple was raised, seasonal sacrifices offered, an inscription set up, and five households appointed to guard the cult.

sentences.zh: 又詔褒揚睿，圖其捍猛獸狀于諸殿，令高允為之贊。

translations.literal: An edict also praised Rui and had painted in the halls his image repelling the fierce beast; Gao Yun was ordered to compose the encomium.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also praised Rui and had painted in the halls his image repelling the fierce beast; Gao Yun was ordered to compose the encomium.

sentences.zh: 京邑士女，諂稱睿美，造新聲而弦歌之，名曰《中山王》。

translations.literal: Men and women of the capital flattered him as beautiful, composed a new tune, and sang it to strings; it was called "The Prince of Zhongshan."
translations.idiomatic: Men and women of the capital flattered his beauty, composed a new tune, and sang it to strings under the title "The Prince of Zhongshan."

sentences.zh: 詔班樂府，合樂奏之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it distributed to the Music Office and performed with full orchestra.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered it sent to the Music Office and performed with full orchestra.

sentences.zh: 初，睿女妻李沖兄子蕤，次女以適趙國李恢子華。

translations.literal: Earlier, Rui's elder daughter had married Rui, son of Li Chong's elder brother; the younger daughter was given in marriage to Li Hua, son of Li Hui of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Rui's elder daughter had married Rui, son of Li Chong's elder brother; the younger was given in marriage to Li Hua, son of Li Hui of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 女之將行，先入宮中，其禮略如公主、王女之儀。

translations.literal: When the daughters were to depart, they first entered the palace; the rites were much like those for an imperial princess or a king's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: When the daughters were to depart, they first entered the palace; the rites were much like those for an imperial princess or a king's daughter.

sentences.zh: 太后親禦太華殿，寢其女於帳中，睿與張祐侍坐。

translations.literal: The empress dowager personally presided in the Taihua Hall, laid the daughter to rest in the curtained bed, and Rui and Zhang You sat in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager personally presided in the Taihua Hall, laid the daughter to rest in the curtained bed, while Rui and Zhang You sat in attendance.

sentences.zh: 睿所親及兩李家丈夫、婦人列於東西廊。

translations.literal: Rui's intimates and the husbands and wives of the two Li families were arrayed in the eastern and western corridors.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's intimates and the husbands and wives of the two Li families were arrayed in the eastern and western corridors.

sentences.zh: 及女子登車，太后送過中路。

translations.literal: When the girl mounted the carriage, the empress dowager escorted her beyond the middle of the road.
translations.idiomatic: When the girl mounted the carriage, the empress dowager escorted her beyond the middle of the road.

sentences.zh: 時人竊謂天子、太后嫁女。

translations.literal: People at the time privately said the Son of Heaven and the empress dowager were marrying off a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time whispered that the Son of Heaven and the empress dowager were marrying off a daughter.

sentences.zh: 睿之葬也，假親姻義舊衰絰縞冠送喪者千餘人，皆舉聲慟泣，以要榮利，時謂之義孝。

translations.literal: At Rui's burial, more than a thousand persons in mourning dress and white caps who pretended kinship or old friendship came to escort the funeral; all raised their voices in loud weeping to seek glory and profit—men of the time called this "righteous mourning."
translations.idiomatic: At Rui's burial more than a thousand persons in mourning dress and white caps, feigning kinship or old friendship, came to escort the funeral; all wailed loudly to win glory and profit—contemporaries called this "righteous mourning."

sentences.zh: 睿既貴，乃言家本太原晉陽，遂移屬焉。

translations.literal: Once Rui was exalted, he declared that his family was originally from Jinyang in Taiyuan and moved his registration there.
translations.idiomatic: Once Rui had risen high, he declared that his family was originally from Jinyang in Taiyuan and moved his household registration there.

sentences.zh: 故其兄弟封爵，多以并州郡縣。

translations.literal: Therefore when his brothers received fiefs, it was mostly in the commanderies and counties of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when his brothers received fiefs, it was mostly in the commanderies and counties of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 薨後，重贈睿父橋侍中、征西將軍、左光祿大夫、儀同三司、武威王，諡曰定。

translations.literal: After his death Rui's father Qiao was again posthumously given Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the West, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left, Director with the Three Departments, Prince of Wuwei, with the posthumous title Settled.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Rui's father Qiao was again posthumously made Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers the West, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left, Director with the Three Departments, and Prince of Wuwei, with the posthumous title Settled.

sentences.zh: 追策睿母賈氏為妃，立碑于墓左。

translations.literal: Rui's mother, the Lady Jia, was posthumously ennobled as a princess consort, and a stele was set up to the left of the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's mother, Lady Jia, was posthumously ennobled as a princess consort, and a stele was set up to the left of the tomb.

sentences.zh: 父子並葬城東，相去里餘。

translations.literal: Father and son were both buried east of the city, a little more than a li apart.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son were both buried east of the city, a little more than a li apart.

sentences.zh: 遷洛後，更徙葬太原晉陽故地。

translations.literal: After the move of the capital to Luoyang, they were reburied in the old lands of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was moved to Luoyang, they were reburied in the old lands of Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 子襲，字元孫。

translations.literal: His son Xi, styled Yuansun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi, courtesy name Yuansun.

sentences.zh: 睿薨，孝文詔襲代領都曹，為尚書令，領吏部曹。

translations.literal: When Rui died, Emperor Xiaowen ordered Xi to succeed him in heading the Departmental Section, made him Director of the Department of State Affairs, and had him head the Ministry of Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: When Rui died, Emperor Xiaowen ordered Xi to succeed him in heading the Departmental Section, made him Director of the Department of State Affairs, and had him head the Ministry of Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 後襲王爵，例降為公。

translations.literal: Later he inherited the princely title, which by precedent was reduced to a dukedom.
translations.idiomatic: Later he inherited the princely title, which by precedent was reduced to a dukedom.

sentences.zh: 太后崩後，襲禮遇稍薄，不復關與時事。

translations.literal: After the empress dowager's death, Xi's treatment grew somewhat thinner, and he no longer had a part in current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress dowager died, Xi's favor grew somewhat thinner and he no longer had a part in current affairs.

sentences.zh: 後出為并州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Governor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went out as Governor of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 輿駕詣洛，路幸其州，人庶多為立銘，置於大路，虛相稱美。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to Luoyang, the route passed through his province; the common people for the most part set up inscriptions along the great road, falsely praising him.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage went to Luoyang, the route passed through his province; the common people for the most part set up inscriptions along the great road with false praise.

sentences.zh: 或云襲所教也，尚書奏免其官，詔唯降號二等。

translations.literal: Some said Xi had instructed this; the Department of State Affairs memorialized to remove him from office, but an edict only reduced his rank by two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Some said Xi had instructed this; the Department of State Affairs memorialized to remove him from office, but an edict only reduced his rank by two grades.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈豫州刺史，諡曰質。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Governor of Yuzhou, with the posthumous title Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Yuzhou, with the posthumous title Simple.

sentences.zh: 襲弟椿，字元壽。

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother Chun, styled Yuanshou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's younger brother Chun, courtesy name Yuanshou.

sentences.zh: 正始中，拜太原太守，坐事免。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he was appointed Governor of Taiyuan and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era he was appointed Governor of Taiyuan and was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 椿僮僕千餘，園宅華廣，聲伎自適，無乏于時。

translations.literal: Chun had more than a thousand servants; his gardens and residence were splendid and broad, and he enjoyed music and performers without want in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Chun had more than a thousand servants; his gardens and residence were splendid and broad, and he enjoyed music and performers without want.

sentences.zh: 或有權椿仕者，椿笑而不答。

translations.literal: When some urged Chun to take office, he smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When some urged Chun to take office, he smiled and did not answer.

sentences.zh: 雅有巧思，凡所營制，可為後法。

translations.literal: He was by nature skilled in ingenious design; whatever he planned and built could serve later men as a model.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature skilled in ingenious design; whatever he planned and built could serve later men as a model.

sentences.zh: 由是正光中元叉將營明堂、辟雍，俗徵為將作大匠，椿聞而固辭。

translations.literal: Hence in the Zhengguang era, when Yuan Cha was about to build the Bright Hall and the Imperial Academy, he was popularly summoned to be Director of Palace Construction; Chun heard of it and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Hence in the Zhengguang era, when Yuan Cha was about to build the Bright Hall and the Imperial Academy, he was popularly summoned to be Director of Palace Construction; Chun heard of it and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，爾硃榮以汾州胡逆，表椿慰勞汾胡。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, Erzhu Rong, on account of rebellion by the Hu of Fenzhou, memorialized that Chun should comfort and reassure the Fen Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era, Erzhu Rong, on account of rebellion by the Hu of Fenzhou, memorialized that Chun should comfort and reassure the Fen Hu.

sentences.zh: 汾胡與椿比州，服其聲望，所至降下。

translations.literal: The Fen Hu were of the same province as Chun and respected his reputation; wherever he went they submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Fen Hu were of the same province as Chun and respected his reputation; wherever he went they submitted.

sentences.zh: 事甯，授太原太守。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was appointed Governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, he was appointed Governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 以預立莊帝功，封遼陽縣子，尋轉封真定縣。

translations.literal: For his merit in helping establish Emperor Zhuang, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Liaoyang and soon transferred to the county of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in helping establish Emperor Zhuang, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Liaoyang and soon transferred to the county of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，除瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was made Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he was made Governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時有風雹之變，詔書廣訪讜言，椿乃上疏言政事之宜。

translations.literal: At that time there were changes of wind and hail; an edict broadly sought forthright counsel, and Chun submitted a memorial on what was fitting in government.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there were storms of wind and hail; an edict broadly sought forthright counsel, and Chun submitted a memorial on what was fitting in government.

sentences.zh: 椿性嚴察，下不容奸，所在吏人畏之重足。

translations.literal: Chun's nature was stern and exacting; below him wickedness was not tolerated, and wherever he was posted officials and clerks feared him as though treading on thin ice.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's nature was stern and exacting; below him wickedness was not tolerated, and wherever he was posted officials and clerks feared him as though treading on thin ice.

sentences.zh: 天平末，更滿還鄉。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianping his term expired and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianping his term expired and he returned home.

sentences.zh: 初，椿於宅構起査事，極為高壯。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chun had built a lookout tower in his residence, extremely high and massive.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chun had built a lookout tower in his residence, extremely high and massive.

sentences.zh: 時人忽云：「此乃太原王宅，豈是王太原宅？」

translations.literal: People of the time suddenly said: "This is the mansion of the Prince of Taiyuan—how could it be the mansion of Wang of Taiyuan?"
translations.idiomatic: People of the time suddenly remarked, "This is the mansion of the Prince of Taiyuan—how could it be the mansion of Wang of Taiyuan?"

sentences.zh: 椿往為本郡，世皆呼為王太原。

translations.literal: Chun had formerly been governor of his native commandery, and the world all called him Wang of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chun had once governed his native commandery, and everyone called him Wang of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，爾硃榮居椿之宅，榮封太原王焉。

translations.literal: Before long Erzhu Rong occupied Chun's residence, and Rong was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Erzhu Rong took up residence in Chun's house, and Rong was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 到于齊神武之居晉陽，霸朝所在，人士輻湊。

translations.literal: When it came to Shenwu of Qi's dwelling in Jinyang, the seat of the hegemonic court, men of rank gathered like spokes to a hub.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan made his seat at Jinyang, the center of the hegemonic court, men of rank gathered there in crowds.

sentences.zh: 椿禮敬親知，多所拯接。

translations.literal: Chun treated kinsmen and acquaintances with courtesy and rescued many.
translations.idiomatic: Chun treated kinsmen and acquaintances with courtesy and rescued many from hardship.

sentences.zh: 後以老病辭疾，客居趙郡之西鯉魚祠山。

translations.literal: Later, citing old age and illness, he resigned on grounds of infirmity and lived as a guest on Carp Shrine Mountain west of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, citing old age and illness, he resigned and lived as a guest on Carp Shrine Mountain west of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書左僕射、太尉公、冀州刺史，諡曰文恭。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Duke of Grand Commandant, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Cultured and Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Duke of Grand Commandant, and Governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous title Cultured and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 及葬，齊神武親自吊送。

translations.literal: At his burial, Shenwu of Qi personally came to mourn and escort the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: At his burial Gao Huan came in person to mourn and escort the funeral.

sentences.zh: 椿妻巨鹿魏悅次女，明達有遠操，多識往行前言。

translations.literal: Chun's wife was the second daughter of Wei Yue of Julu; she was clear-sighted and far-seeing, and knew much of past conduct and earlier sayings.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's wife was the second daughter of Wei Yue of Julu; she was clear-sighted and far-seeing, and knew much of past conduct and earlier sayings.

sentences.zh: 隨夫在華州，兄子建在洛遇患，聞而馳赴，膚容虧損，親類歎尚之。

translations.literal: Following her husband in Huazhou, when her brother's son Jian fell ill in Luoyang she heard of it and rushed there; her complexion wasted away, and kin praised and admired her.
translations.idiomatic: While following her husband in Huazhou, she learned that her brother's son Jian had fallen ill in Luoyang; she rushed there at once, her complexion wasted with care, and her kin praised her devotion.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮妻鄉郡長公主深所禮敬。

translations.literal: The Princess of Xiangjun, wife of Erzhu Rong, deeply honored and respected her.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Xiangjun, Erzhu Rong's wife, deeply honored and respected her.

sentences.zh: 永安中，詔以為南和縣君。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era an edict made her Lady of Nanhe county.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongan era an edict made her Lady of Nanhe county.

sentences.zh: 內足於財，不以華飾為意。

translations.literal: Inwardly content with her wealth, she did not care for lavish adornment.
translations.idiomatic: Content with her means, she did not care for lavish adornment.

sentences.zh: 撫兄子收，情同己子。

translations.literal: She reared her brother's son Shou as though he were her own son.
translations.idiomatic: She reared her brother's son Shou as though he were her own child.

sentences.zh: 存拯親類，所在周給。

translations.literal: She preserved and aided her kin, everywhere providing for them.
translations.idiomatic: She preserved and aided her kin, providing for them wherever they were.

sentences.zh: 椿名位終始，魏有力焉。

translations.literal: Chun's fame and position from beginning to end owed much to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's rise in fame and position owed much to the Wei family.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈巨鹿郡君。

translations.literal: When she died she was posthumously given the title Lady of Julu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When she died she was posthumously made Lady of Julu commandery.

sentences.zh: 椿無子，以兄孫叔明為後。

translations.literal: Chun had no sons and took his elder brother's grandson Shuming as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Chun had no sons and took his elder brother's grandson Shuming as heir.

sentences.zh: 王仲興，趙郡南欒人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongxing was a man of Nanluan in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongxing was a native of Nanluan in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 父天德，起自細微，至殿中尚書。

translations.literal: His father Tiande rose from humble origins to reach Director of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tiande rose from humble origins to become Director of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 仲興幼而端謹，以父任，早給事左右，累遷越騎校尉。

translations.literal: Zhongxing in youth was proper and careful; through his father's position he early entered service at the ruler's side and rose through posts to Colonel of the Rapid-as-Leopards Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing in youth was proper and careful; through his father's position he entered service at the ruler's side while still young and rose to Colonel of the Rapid-as-Leopards Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 孝文在馬圈，自不豫、大漸迄于崩，仲興頗預侍護。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen was at the horse park, from his first illness through his grave decline until his death, Zhongxing took part in attending and guarding him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen was at the horse park, from his first illness through his grave decline until his death, Zhongxing took part in attending and guarding him.

sentences.zh: 宣武即位，轉左中郎將。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, he was transferred to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Zhongxing was transferred to General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 及帝親政，與趙脩並見寵任，遷光祿大夫，領武衛將軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally took power, he and Zhao Xiu alike were favored and entrusted; he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and concurrently Great General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally took power, he and Zhao Xiu alike were favored and entrusted; he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and concurrently Great General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 雖與脩並，而畏慎自退，不若脩倨傲無禮。

translations.literal: Although he stood with Xiu, he was fearful and cautious and held himself back, unlike Xiu's arrogance and lack of courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Although he stood with Xiu, he was fearful and cautious and held himself back, unlike Xiu's arrogance and lack of courtesy.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧之出奔也，當時上下微為震駭，帝遣仲興先馳入金墉安慰。

translations.literal: When Prince Xi of Xianyang fled, the court above and below were slightly shaken in alarm; the emperor sent Zhongxing ahead at full gallop into Jinyong to reassure the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xi of Xianyang fled, court and capital were slightly shaken; the emperor sent Zhongxing ahead at full gallop into Jinyong to reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 後與領軍於勁參機要，因自回馬圈侍疾及入金墉功，遂封上党郡開國公。

translations.literal: Later, together with the Commander-in-Chief Yu Jin he shared in confidential affairs; because of his merit in attending illness at the horse park and entering Jinyong, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shangdang with an open fief.
translations.idiomatic: Later, together with Commander-in-Chief Yu Jin he shared in confidential affairs; because of his merit in attending illness at the horse park and entering Jinyong, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shangdang with an open fief.

sentences.zh: 自拜武衛及受封日，車駕每臨饗其宅。

translations.literal: From the day he was appointed to the Martial Guard and received his fief, the imperial carriage each time came to feast at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he was appointed to the Martial Guard and received his fief, the imperial carriage each time came to feast at his residence.

sentences.zh: 宣武游幸，仲興常侍，不離左右，外事得徑以聞，百僚亦聳體而承望焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu went on excursions, Zhongxing constantly attended and never left his side; outside affairs could reach the emperor through him, and the hundred officials also stood in awe and looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu went on excursions, Zhongxing constantly attended and never left his side; outside affairs could reach the emperor through him, and the hundred officials stood in awe and looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 兄可久，以仲興故，自散爵為征虜府長史，帶彭城太守。

translations.literal: His elder brother Kejiu, because of Zhongxing, rose from a scattered noble title to Chief Clerk of the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians' headquarters, concurrently holding the post of Governor of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Kejiu, because of Zhongxing, rose from a scattered noble title to Chief Clerk of the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians' headquarters, concurrently holding the post of Governor of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 仲興世居趙郡，自以寒微，雲舊出京兆霸城，故為雍州大中正。

translations.literal: Zhongxing's family had long lived in Zhao commandery; considering himself of humble origin, he claimed his clan originally came from Bacheng in Jingzhao and therefore became Chief Rectifier of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing's family had long lived in Zhao commandery; considering himself of humble origin, he claimed his clan originally came from Bacheng in Jingzhao and therefore became Chief Rectifier of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 尚書後以仲興賞報過優，北海王詳嘗以面啟，奏請降減，事久不決。

translations.literal: The Department of State Affairs later held that Zhongxing's rewards were excessively generous; Prince Xiang of Beihai once spoke to him face to face and memorialized to request reduction, but the matter long went undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of State Affairs later held that Zhongxing's rewards were excessively generous; Prince Xiang of Beihai once spoke to him face to face and memorialized to request reduction, but the matter long went undecided.

sentences.zh: 可久在徐州，恃仲興寵勢，輕侮司馬梁郡太守李長壽，乃令僮僕邀毆長壽，遂折其脅。

translations.literal: Kejiu in Xuzhou relied on Zhongxing's favor and power and lightly insulted Li Changshou, Administrator of Liang commandery and acting Governor of Xuzhou; he had his servants waylay and beat Changshou and broke his ribs.
translations.idiomatic: Kejiu in Xuzhou relied on Zhongxing's favor and power and lightly insulted Li Changshou, Administrator of Liang commandery and acting Governor of Xuzhou; he had his servants waylay and beat Changshou and broke his ribs.

sentences.zh: 州以表聞，北海王詳因百僚朝集，厲色大言曰：「徐州名籓，先帝所重，朝廷云何簡用上佐，遂至此紛紜，以徹荒外，豈不為國醜辱！」

translations.literal: The province reported it to the throne; Prince Xiang of Beihai, at an assembly when the hundred officials paid court, spoke sternly in a loud voice: "Xuzhou is a famous frontier, heavily valued by the late emperor—how could the court so lightly appoint its chief administrator, with the result that such turmoil arose, to alarm the distant borderlands? Is this not a national disgrace!"
translations.idiomatic: The province reported it to the throne; at an assembly when the hundred officials paid court, Prince Xiang of Beihai spoke sternly in a loud voice: "Xuzhou is a famous frontier, heavily valued by the late emperor—how could the court so lightly appoint its chief administrator, with the result that such turmoil arose, to alarm the distant borderlands? Is this not a national disgrace!"

sentences.zh: 仲興是後漸疏。

translations.literal: After this Zhongxing was gradually estranged.
translations.idiomatic: After this Zhongxing was gradually estranged.

sentences.zh: 宣武乃下詔奪其封邑。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu then issued an edict stripping his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu then issued an edict stripping his fief.

sentences.zh: 後卒于并州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he died while Governor of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died while Governor of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，又有上穀寇猛，少以姿幹充武賁，稍遷至武衛將軍。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanwu's time there was also Kou Meng of Shanggu; in youth, for his looks and bearing, he filled a post in the Martial Guard and gradually rose to Great General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xuanwu's time there was also Kou Meng of Shanggu; in youth, for his looks and bearing, he filled a post in the Martial Guard and gradually rose to Great General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 出入禁中，無所拘忌。

translations.literal: He went in and out of the forbidden precincts without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: He went in and out of the forbidden precincts without restraint.

sentences.zh: 自以上穀寇氏，得補燕州大中正，而不能甄別士庶也。

translations.literal: Because his clan was the Kou of Shanggu, he was appointed Chief Rectifier of Yanzhou, yet he could not distinguish gentry from commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Because his clan was the Kou of Shanggu, he was appointed Chief Rectifier of Yanzhou, yet he could not distinguish gentry from commoners.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈燕州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 趙修，字景業，趙郡房子人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiu, styled Jingye, was a man of Fangzi in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiu, courtesy name Jingye, was a native of Fangzi in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 父謐，陽武令。

translations.literal: His father Mi was Magistrate of Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mi was Magistrate of Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 修本給事東宮，為白衣左右，頗有膂力。

translations.literal: Xiu had originally served in the Eastern Palace as a white-robed attendant at the ruler's side and was rather strong in physique.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had originally served in the Eastern Palace as a white-robed attendant at the ruler's side and was rather strong in physique.

sentences.zh: 宣武踐阼，愛遇日隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, his favor grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, his favor grew daily.

sentences.zh: 然天性暗塞，不親書疏。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was dull and obstructed and did not attend to documents.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was dull and obstructed and did not attend to documents.

sentences.zh: 宣武親政，旬月間頻有轉授。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu personally took power, within a month he received frequent promotions.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu personally took power, within a month he received frequent promotions.

sentences.zh: 每受除設宴，帝幸其宅，諸王公百僚悉從，帝親見其母。

translations.literal: Each time he received an appointment a feast was set; the emperor visited his residence, and all the princes, dukes, and hundred officials followed; the emperor personally saw his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he received an appointment a feast was set; the emperor visited his residence, and all the princes, dukes, and hundred officials followed; the emperor personally saw his mother.

sentences.zh: 修能劇飲，至於逼勸觴爵，雖北海王詳、廣陽王嘉等皆亦不免，必致困亂。

translations.literal: Xiu could drink heavily; when it came to pressing others to drink, even Prince Xiang of Beihai, Prince Jia of Guangyang, and the like could not escape, and he always reduced them to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu could drink heavily; when it came to pressing others to drink, even Prince Xiang of Beihai, Prince Jia of Guangyang, and the like could not escape, and he always reduced them to disorder.

sentences.zh: 每適郊廟，修常驂陪，出入華林，恆乘馬至禁內。

translations.literal: Whenever he went to the suburban altars or ancestral temples, Xiu regularly rode in the side carriage as escort; going in and out of the Flowery Grove, he always rode a horse into the inner forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went to the suburban altars or ancestral temples, Xiu regularly rode in the side carriage as escort; going in and out of the Flowery Grove, he always rode a horse into the inner forbidden precinct.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧誅，其家財貨多賜高肇及脩。

translations.literal: When Prince Xi of Xianyang was executed, much of his family's wealth and goods were bestowed on Gao Zhao and Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xi of Xianyang was executed, much of his family's wealth and goods were bestowed on Gao Zhao and Xiu.

sentences.zh: 修之葬父，百官自王公已下，無不弔祭，酒犢祭奠之具，填塞門街，。

translations.literal: At Xiu's burial of his father, from the princes and dukes downward no one failed to offer mourning sacrifices; wine, oxen, and offerings for the sacrifice filled the streets before the gate.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiu's burial of his father, from the princes and dukes downward no one failed to offer mourning sacrifices; wine, oxen, and offerings filled the streets before the gate.

sentences.zh: 于京師為制碑銘、石獸、石柱，皆發人車牛，傳致本縣，財用之費，悉自公家。

translations.literal: In the capital he had made for him regulated stele inscriptions, stone beasts, and stone pillars, all sent for by conscripting men and ox-carts and transported to his native county; the cost of materials was entirely from the public treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he had made regulated stele inscriptions, stone beasts, and stone pillars, all sent for by conscripting men and ox-carts and transported to his native county at public expense.

sentences.zh: 凶吉車乘將百兩，道路供給，皆出於官。

translations.literal: Funeral and auspicious carriages and teams numbered nearly a hundred; supplies along the road all came from the government.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral and auspicious carriages and teams numbered nearly a hundred; supplies along the road all came from the government.

sentences.zh: 時將馬射，宣武留修過之，帝如射宮，又驂乘，輅車旒竿觸東門折。

translations.literal: At that time there was to be horse archery; Emperor Xuanwu detained Xiu to pass the time with him; the emperor went to the archery park, and Xiu again rode in the side carriage; the tasselled pole of the imperial carriage struck the eastern gate and broke.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was to be horse archery; Emperor Xuanwu detained Xiu to pass the time with him; the emperor went to the archery park, and Xiu again rode in the side carriage; the tasselled pole of the imperial carriage struck the eastern gate and broke.

sentences.zh: 脩恐不逮葬日，驛赴窆期。

translations.literal: Xiu feared he would not reach the burial day and took post-horses to rush to the interment date.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu feared he would not reach the burial day and took post-horses to rush to the interment date.

sentences.zh: 左右求從及特遣者數十人，修道路嬉戲，殆無戚容，或與賓客奸掠婦女裸觀，從者噂栎遝喧嘩，詬詈無節，莫不畏而惡之。

translations.literal: Those at his side who sought to follow and special envoys numbered several tens; Xiu amused himself along the road, almost without a grieving countenance, and sometimes with guests seized and raped women for naked viewing; his followers' clamor and noise were heaped up without restraint or abuse without limit—none did not fear and detest him.
translations.idiomatic: Those at his side who sought to follow and special envoys numbered several tens; Xiu amused himself along the road, almost without a grieving countenance, and sometimes with guests seized and raped women for naked viewing; his followers clamored without restraint and abused passersby without limit—all fear and detest him.

sentences.zh: 是年，又為修廣增宅舍，多所並兼，洞門高堂，房廡周博，崇麗擬于諸王。

translations.literal: That year he again had Xiu's residence broadly enlarged; he annexed many neighboring properties; lofty gates and high halls, rooms and corridors broad all around, their splendor rivaling the princes.
translations.idiomatic: That year he again had Xiu's residence broadly enlarged; he annexed many neighboring properties; lofty gates and high halls, rooms and corridors broad all around, their splendor rivaling the princes.

sentences.zh: 其四面鄰居，賂入其地者侯天盛兄弟，越次出補長史大郡。

translations.literal: His neighbors on all four sides who bribed their way into his land were the brothers Hou Tiansheng, who leapfrogged others to be appointed Chief Clerk of great commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His neighbors on all four sides who bribed their way into his land were the brothers Hou Tiansheng, who leapfrogged others to be appointed Chief Clerk of great commanderies.

sentences.zh: 修起自賤伍，暴致富貴，奢傲無禮，物情所疾，困其在外，左右或諷糾其罪。

translations.literal: Xiu rose from base ranks and suddenly grew rich and noble; extravagant and arrogant without courtesy, he was detested by public sentiment; while he was away outside, those at his side sometimes admonished and reported his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu rose from base ranks and suddenly grew rich and noble; extravagant and arrogant without courtesy, he was detested by public sentiment; while he was away outside, those at his side sometimes admonished and reported his crimes.

sentences.zh: 自其葬父還也，舊寵小薄。

translations.literal: From the time he returned from burying his father, his old favor grew somewhat thin.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he returned from burying his father, his old favor grew somewhat thin.

sentences.zh: 初，王顯附修，後因忿鬩，密伺其過，列修葬父時，路中淫亂不軌。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Xian had attached himself to Xiu; later, because of a quarrel of resentment, he secretly watched for his faults and reported that on the road while burying his father Xiu had been licentious and disorderly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Xian had attached himself to Xiu; later, because of a quarrel of resentment, he secretly watched for his faults and reported that on the road while burying his father Xiu had been licentious and disorderly.

sentences.zh: 又云與長安人趙僧愔謀匿玉印事。

translations.literal: He also said that with Zhao Sengyin of Chang'an he plotted to conceal a jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that with Zhao Sengyin of Chang'an he plotted to conceal a jade seal.

sentences.zh: 高肇、甄琛等構成其罪，乃密以聞。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao, Zhen Chen, and others fabricated his crime and secretly reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, Zhen Chen, and others fabricated his crime and secretly reported it.

sentences.zh: 始琛及李憑等曲事修，無所不至，懼相連及，乃爭共糾扌適。

translations.literal: At first Chen and Li Ping and others had curried favor with Xiu without limit, fearing they would be implicated; therefore they all strove to accuse and impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Chen and Li Ping and others had curried favor with Xiu without limit, fearing they would be implicated; therefore they all strove to accuse and impeach him.

sentences.zh: 遂有詔按其罪惡，鞭之一百，徒敦煌為兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to investigate his crimes; he was flogged one hundred strokes and banished to Dunhuang as a soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict was issued to investigate his crimes; he was flogged one hundred strokes and banished to Dunhuang as a soldier.

sentences.zh: 其家宅作徒，即仰停罷，所親在內者，悉令出禁。

translations.literal: His family residence was made into convict labor and immediately stopped; those close to him within the palace were all ordered out of the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: His family residence was made into convict labor and immediately stopped; those close to him within the palace were all ordered out of the forbidden precinct.

sentences.zh: 是日，修詣領軍於勁第，與之樗蒱。

translations.literal: That day Xiu went to Commander-in-Chief Yu Jin's residence to play liubo with him.
translations.idiomatic: That day Xiu went to Commander-in-Chief Yu Jin's residence to play liubo with him.

sentences.zh: 籌未及畢，羽林數人，相續而至，稱詔呼之。

translations.literal: Before the game was finished, several men of the Imperial Guard came in succession, calling him by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Before the game was finished, several men of the Imperial Guard came in succession, calling him by edict.

sentences.zh: 脩驚起，隨出。

translations.literal: Xiu started up in alarm and followed them out.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu started up in alarm and followed them out.

sentences.zh: 路中執引脩馬詣領軍府。

translations.literal: On the road they seized Xiu's horse and led him to the Commander-in-Chief's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they seized Xiu's horse and led him to the Commander-in-Chief's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 琛與顯監決其罪，先具問事有力者五人，更迭鞭之，占令必死。

translations.literal: Chen and Xian supervised the execution of his punishment; they first prepared five strong men for questioning and had them take turns flogging him, calculating that he must die.
translations.idiomatic: Chen and Xian supervised the execution of his punishment; they first prepared five strong men for questioning and had them take turns flogging him, calculating that he must die.

sentences.zh: 旨決百靴，其實三百。

translations.literal: The edict decided on one hundred strokes, but in fact it was three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The edict decided on one hundred strokes, but in fact it was three hundred.

sentences.zh: 修素肥壯，腰腹博碩，堪忍楚毒，了不轉動。

translations.literal: Xiu had always been fat and robust; his waist and belly were broad and thick; he could endure the cruel blows and did not stir at all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had always been fat and robust; his waist and belly were broad and thick; he could endure the cruel blows and did not stir at all.

sentences.zh: 鞭訖，即召驛馬，促之令發。

translations.literal: When the flogging was finished they immediately summoned post-horses and urged him to set out.
translations.idiomatic: When the flogging was finished they immediately summoned post-horses and urged him to set out.

sentences.zh: 出城西門，不自勝舉，縛置鞍中，急驅馳之，其母妻追隨，不得與語，行八十里乃死。

translations.literal: Leaving the western city gate, he could no longer hold himself up; they bound him on the saddle and drove him hard; his mother and wife followed in pursuit but could not speak with him; after eighty li he died.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the western city gate, he could no longer hold himself up; they bound him on the saddle and drove him hard; his mother and wife followed in pursuit but could not speak with him; after eighty li he died.

sentences.zh: 初，於後之入，修之力也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Empress Yu entered the palace, it was through Xiu's effort.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Empress Yu entered the palace, it was through Xiu's effort.

sentences.zh: 修死後，領軍於勁猶追感舊意，經恤其家。

translations.literal: After Xiu died, Commander-in-Chief Yu Jin still recalled their old ties and looked after his family.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu died, Commander-in-Chief Yu Jin still recalled their old ties and looked after his family.

sentences.zh: 自余朝士昔相宗承者，悉棄絕之，以示己之疏遠焉。

translations.literal: The other court gentlemen who had formerly associated with him all cast him off, to show their own distance from him.
translations.idiomatic: The other court gentlemen who had formerly associated with him all cast him off, to show their own distance from him.

sentences.zh: 茹皓，字禽奇，舊吳人也。

translations.literal: Ru Hao, styled Qinqi, was formerly a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Hao, courtesy name Qinqi, was formerly a man of Wu.

sentences.zh: 父謙之，本名要，隨宋巴陵王休若為將，至彭城，遂寓居淮陽上黨。

translations.literal: His father Qianzhi, original name Yao, followed Prince Xiuling of Song as a general to Pengcheng and there settled in Shangdang in Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qianzhi, original name Yao, followed Prince Xiuling of Song as a general to Pengcheng and there settled in Shangdang in Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 皓年十五六，為縣金曹吏。

translations.literal: When Hao was fifteen or sixteen he was a metal-bureau clerk of the county.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was fifteen or sixteen he was a metal-bureau clerk of the county.

sentences.zh: 南徐州刺史沈陵見而善之，自隨入洛，舉充孝文白衣左右。

translations.literal: Shen Ling, Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, saw him and favored him, taking him along into Luoyang; he was recommended to fill a post as white-robed attendant at Emperor Xiaowen's side.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ling, Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, saw him and favored him, taking him along into Luoyang; he was recommended to fill a post as white-robed attendant at Emperor Xiaowen's side.

sentences.zh: 宣武踐阼，皓侍直禁中，稍被寵接。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Hao attended duty in the forbidden precinct and was gradually received in favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Hao attended duty in the forbidden precinct and was gradually received in favor.

sentences.zh: 宣武嘗拜山陵，路中欲引與同車，黃門侍郎元匡切諫乃止。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu once went to pay respects at the mountain tombs; on the road he wished to have Hao ride in the same carriage, but Attendant Within the Yellow Gates Yuan Kuang remonstrated sharply and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu once went to pay respects at the mountain tombs; on the road he wished to have Hao ride in the same carriage, but Attendant Within the Yellow Gates Yuan Kuang remonstrated sharply and stopped it.

sentences.zh: 乃帝親政，皓眷賚日隆。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally took power, Hao's favor and gifts grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally took power, Hao's favor and gifts grew daily.

sentences.zh: 時趙脩亦被幸，妒之，求出皓。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Xiu was also favored; jealous of him, he sought to have Hao sent out.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Xiu was also favored; jealous of him, he sought to have Hao sent out.

sentences.zh: 皓亦慮見危禍，不樂內官，遂超授濮陽太守，其父因皓，訟理舊勳，先除兗州陽平太守，賜以子爵。

translations.literal: Hao also feared he would meet with disaster and did not relish inner office; he was abruptly appointed Governor of Puyang; because of Hao his father pleaded the old merit of their clan and was first made Governor of Yangping in Yanzhou and granted a viscount's title.
translations.idiomatic: Hao also feared he would meet with disaster and did not relish inner office; he was abruptly appointed Governor of Puyang; because of Hao his father pleaded the old merit of their clan and was first made Governor of Yangping in Yanzhou and granted a viscount's title.

sentences.zh: 父子剖符名邦，郡境相接。

translations.literal: Father and son held separate credentials in famous commanderies with adjoining territories.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son held separate credentials in famous commanderies with adjoining territories.

sentences.zh: 皓忻於去內，不以疏外為戚。

translations.literal: Hao rejoiced at leaving the inner quarters and did not regard being sent outside as a sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Hao rejoiced at leaving the inner quarters and did not regard being sent outside as a sorrow.

sentences.zh: 及趙脩等敗，竟獲全。

translations.literal: When Zhao Xiu and the others fell, he in the end escaped unscathed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Xiu and the others fell, he in the end escaped unscathed.

sentences.zh: 雖起微細，為守乃清簡寡事。

translations.literal: Although he rose from the minute, as governor he was pure and simple and had few affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Although he rose from humble origins, as governor he was pure and simple and had few affairs.

sentences.zh: 後授左中郎將，領直閣，寵待如前。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General of the Left Guard and concurrently head of the Direct Attendance Office; favor and treatment were as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed General of the Left Guard and concurrently head of the Direct Attendance Office; favor and treatment were as before.

sentences.zh: 皓既宦達，自雲本出雁門，雁門人諂附者，乃因薦皓于司徒，請為肆州大中正，詔特依許。

translations.literal: Once Hao had risen in office he claimed for himself that his origin was Yanmen; men of Yanmen who flattered and attached themselves therefore recommended Hao to the Minister of State and requested him as Chief Rectifier of Sizhou; an edict specially approved it as requested.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hao had risen in office he claimed for himself that his origin was Yanmen; men of Yanmen who flattered and attached themselves therefore recommended Hao to the Minister of State and requested him as Chief Rectifier of Sizhou; an edict specially approved it as requested.

sentences.zh: 遷驍騎將軍，領華林諸作。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Valiant Cavalry and concurrently head of all works of the Flowery Grove.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of Valiant Cavalry and concurrently head of all works of the Flowery Grove.

sentences.zh: 皓性微工巧，多所興立，為山于天泉池西，採掘北芒及南山佳石，徙竹汝、潁，羅蒔其間。

translations.literal: Hao was by nature slightly skilled in ingenious craft and raised up many constructions; he made a mountain west of the Heavenly Spring Pool, quarrying fine stone from Northern Mang and the southern mountains, transplanting bamboo from the Ru and Ying, and planting them round about.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was by nature slightly skilled in ingenious craft and raised up many constructions; he made a mountain west of the Heavenly Spring Pool, quarrying fine stone from Northern Mang and the southern mountains, transplanting bamboo from the Ru and Ying, and planting them round about.

sentences.zh: 經構樓觀，列於上下，樹草栽木，頗有野致。

translations.literal: He planned towers and pavilions ranged above and below; trees, grass, and plantings had much of the flavor of the wild.
translations.idiomatic: He planned towers and pavilions ranged above and below; trees, grass, and plantings had much of the flavor of the wild.

sentences.zh: 帝心悅之，以時臨幸。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart was pleased and from time to time he visited.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's heart was pleased and from time to time he visited.

sentences.zh: 皓貴寵日升，關豫政事，太傅、北海王詳以下，咸祗憚之。

translations.literal: Hao's exalted favor rose daily; he took part in government affairs; from the Grand Tutor, Prince Xiang of Beihai, downward, all stood in awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's exalted favor rose daily; he took part in government affairs; from the Grand Tutor, Prince Xiang of Beihai, downward, all stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 皓娶僕射高肇從妹，于帝為從母，迎納之日，詳親詣之，禮以馬物，皓又為弟聘安豐王延明妹，延明恥非舊流，不許。

translations.literal: Hao married the younger cousin of Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Gao Zhao; to the emperor she was a maternal aunt; on the day of the welcome and reception Prince Xiang personally came to him and presented gifts of horses and goods; Hao also arranged a marriage for his younger brother with the younger sister of Prince Yanming of Anfeng, but Yanming was ashamed that she was not of an old lineage and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Hao married the younger cousin of Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Gao Zhao; to the emperor she was a maternal aunt; on the day of the welcome and reception Prince Xiang personally came to him and presented gifts of horses and goods; Hao also arranged a marriage for his younger brother with the younger sister of Prince Yanming of Anfeng, but Yanming was ashamed that she was not of an old lineage and did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 詳勸之云：「欲覓官職，如何不與茹皓婚姻也？」

translations.literal: Xiang earnestly urged him, saying: "If you wish to seek office, why not give your daughter in marriage to Ru Hao?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiang earnestly urged him, saying, "If you wish to seek office, why not give your daughter in marriage to Ru Hao?

sentences.zh: 延明乃從焉。

translations.literal: Yanming thereupon consented.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming thereupon consented.

sentences.zh: 皓頗敏慧，折節下人，潛自經營，陰有納受，貨產盈積，起宅宮西，朝貴弗及。

translations.literal: Hao was rather clever and quick-witted; he humbled himself before others and secretly managed affairs on his own; he secretly accepted bribes, his goods and wealth piled up, and he built a residence west of the palace—court nobles did not match it.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was rather clever and quick-witted; he humbled himself before others while secretly managing his own affairs; he secretly accepted bribes until his wealth piled up, and he built a residence west of the palace that court nobles could not match.

sentences.zh: 時帝雖親萬務，皓率常居內，留宿不還，傳可門下奏事。

translations.literal: Although the emperor then personally handled the myriad affairs of state, Hao regularly stayed within and did not return at night, transmitting and approving memorials at the Gate of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor then personally handled state affairs, Hao regularly stayed within and did not return at night, transmitting and approving memorials at the Gate of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 未幾，轉光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Director of the Chamberlain for Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Vice Director of the Chamberlain for Attendants.

sentences.zh: 意殊不已，方欲陳馬圈從先帝勞，更希榮舉。

translations.literal: His intent was by no means satisfied; he was about to report the horse park's service to the late emperor as meritorious labor and hoped still for further honors.
translations.idiomatic: His ambition was by no means satisfied; he was about to cite his service at the horse park to the late emperor and hoped for further honors.

sentences.zh: 初，脩、皓之寵，北海王詳皆附之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiu and Hao were favored, Prince Xiang of Beihai had attached himself to them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xiu and Hao were favored, Prince Xiang of Beihai had attached himself to them.

sentences.zh: 又直閣劉胄本為詳薦，常感恩。

translations.literal: Also, Direct Attendant Liu Zhou had originally been recommended by Xiang and constantly felt gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Also, Direct Attendant Liu Zhou had originally been recommended by Xiang and constantly felt gratitude toward him.

sentences.zh: 高肇素嫉諸王，常規陷害，既知詳與皓等交關相昵，乃構之，雲皓等將有異謀。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao had always resented the princes and regularly plotted to entrap them; knowing that Xiang was on intimate terms with Hao and the others, he fabricated charges that Hao and the rest were plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao had always resented the princes and regularly plotted to entrap them; learning that Xiang was on intimate terms with Hao and the others, he fabricated charges that they were plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 宣武乃召中尉崔亮，令奏皓、胄、常季賢、陳掃靜四人擅勢納賄及私亂諸事。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu then summoned the Chief Commandant Cui Liang and ordered him to memorialize that Hao, Zhou, Chang Jixian, and Chen Saojing four men had usurped power, accepted bribes, and privately committed various disorderly acts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu then summoned Chief Commandant Cui Liang and ordered him to memorialize that Hao, Zhou, Chang Jixian, and Chen Saojing had usurped power, accepted bribes, and privately committed various disorderly acts.

sentences.zh: 即日執皓等，皆詣南台，翌日，奏處殺之。

translations.literal: That very day Hao and the others were arrested and all sent to the Southern Terrace; the next day a memorial was submitted sentencing them to death.
translations.idiomatic: That very day Hao and the others were arrested and sent to the Southern Terrace; the next day a memorial was submitted sentencing them to death.

sentences.zh: 皓妻被髮出堂，哭而迎皓。

translations.literal: Hao's wife came out of the hall with her hair unbound, weeping as she went to meet Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's wife came out of the hall with her hair unbound, weeping as she went to meet him.

sentences.zh: 皓徑入哭別，食椒而死。

translations.literal: Hao went straight in to take leave in tears and ate pepper to die.
translations.idiomatic: Hao went straight in to take leave in tears and ate pepper to die.

sentences.zh: 胄字元孫，後位直閣將軍。

translations.literal: Zhou, styled Yuansun, later reached the post of Direct Attendant General.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou, courtesy name Yuansun, later reached the post of Direct Attendant General.

sentences.zh: 季賢起于主馬，宣武初好騎乘，因是獲寵。

translations.literal: Jixian rose from managing the imperial horses; when Emperor Xuanwu first loved riding, he thereby won favor.
translations.idiomatic: Jixian rose from managing the imperial horses; when Emperor Xuanwu first loved riding, he thereby won favor.

sentences.zh: 位司藥丞，仍主廄閑。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Director of the Pharmacy Bureau and still managed the stables.
translations.idiomatic: He reached the post of Director of the Pharmacy Bureau and still managed the stables.

sentences.zh: 掃靜、徐義恭，並彭城舊營人。

translations.literal: Saojing and Xu Yigong were both old camp followers from Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Saojing and Xu Yigong were both old camp followers from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 掃靜能為宣武典櫛梳，義恭善執衣服，並以巧便，旦夕居中，愛幸相侔，官敘不異。

translations.literal: Saojing could attend Emperor Xuanwu in combing and dressing; Yigong was skilled at holding garments; both were dexterous and from morning to evening were in the inner quarters; their favor was comparable, and their official ranks were not different.
translations.idiomatic: Saojing could attend Emperor Xuanwu in combing and dressing; Yigong was skilled at holding garments; both were dexterous and from morning to evening were in the inner quarters; their favor was comparable, and their official ranks were alike.

sentences.zh: 二人皆承皓，皓亦接眷。

translations.literal: Both men relied on Hao, and Hao also received them in favor.
translations.idiomatic: Both men relied on Hao, and Hao also received them in favor.

sentences.zh: 而掃靜偏為親密，與皓常在左右，略不歸休。

translations.literal: Yet Saojing was especially intimate; he and Hao were constantly at the ruler's side and scarcely returned home to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Saojing was especially intimate; he and Hao were constantly at the ruler's side and scarcely returned home to rest.

sentences.zh: 皓敗，掃靜亦死於家。

translations.literal: When Hao fell, Saojing also died at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao fell, Saojing also died at home.

sentences.zh: 義恭小心謹慎，皓等死後，彌見幸信。

translations.literal: Yigong was careful and cautious; after Hao and the others died, he was still more favored and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong was careful and cautious; after Hao and the others died, he was still more favored and trusted.

sentences.zh: 宣武不豫，義恭晝夜扶抱，崩於懷中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu was ill, Yigong supported and embraced him day and night; the emperor died in his arms.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu was ill, Yigong supported and embraced him day and night; the emperor died in his arms.

sentences.zh: 義恭諂附元叉，叉有淫宴，多在其宅。

translations.literal: Yigong flattered and attached himself to Yuan Cha; Cha's licentious feasts were often held at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong flattered and attached himself to Yuan Cha; Cha's licentious feasts were often held at his residence.

sentences.zh: 位終左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He ended as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness on the Left.

sentences.zh: 趙邕，字令和，自雲南陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Yong, styled Linghe, claimed for himself that his family was from Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yong, courtesy name Linghe, claimed descent from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 潔白美髭眉。

translations.literal: He was clean and white, with beautiful beard and eyebrows.
translations.idiomatic: He was fair-complexioned, with handsome beard and eyebrows.

sentences.zh: 司空李沖之貴寵也。

translations.literal: He was favored and exalted when Li Chong was Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose when Li Chong was Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 邕以少年端謹，出入其家，頗給桉磨奔走之役。

translations.literal: Yong in youth was proper and careful; he went in and out of Chong's household and often performed tasks of grinding ink and running errands.
translations.idiomatic: Yong in youth was proper and careful; he went in and out of Chong's household and often performed tasks of grinding ink and running errands.

sentences.zh: 沖令與諸子遊處，人有束帶謁沖者，時托之以自通。

translations.literal: Chong had him associate with his sons in their activities; when people came with girdles to call on Chong, they would entrust Yong to announce them.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had him associate with his sons; when visitors came formally to call on Chong, they would entrust Yong to announce them.

sentences.zh: 太和中，給事左右，至殿中監。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he served at the ruler's side and reached Director of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he served at the ruler's side and reached Director of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 宣武即位及親政，猶居本任。
