translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne and personally took power, he still held his original post.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne and personally took power, he still held his original post.

sentences.zh: 微與趙脩結為宗援，然亦不甚相附也。

translations.literal: He slightly joined Zhao Xiu in clan alliance, yet he did not attach himself very closely.
translations.idiomatic: He slightly joined Zhao Xiu in clan alliance, yet he did not attach himself very closely.

sentences.zh: 邕父怡，以邕寵，召拜太常少卿，尋為荊州大中正，出為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Yong's father Yi, because of Yong's favor, was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials; soon he became Chief Rectifier of Jingzhou and went out as Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's father Yi, because of Yong's favor, was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials; soon he became Chief Rectifier of Jingzhou and went out as Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 怡乃致其母喪，葬于宛城之南，趙氏舊墟。

translations.literal: Yi then brought his mother's coffin and buried her south of Wancheng on the old ruins of the Zhao clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yi then brought his mother's coffin and buried her south of Wancheng on the old ruins of the Zhao clan.

sentences.zh: 後拜金紫光祿大夫，卒，贈相州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Ornament; he died and was posthumously made Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Ornament; he died and was posthumously made Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣武每出入郊廟，脩恆以常侍兼侍中陪乘，而邕兼奉車都尉，執轡同載。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Xuanwu went in and out of the suburban altars and ancestral temples, Xiu regularly as Regular Attendant and concurrently Palace Attendant rode in the side carriage as escort, while Yong concurrently as Director of the Imperial Carriage held the reins in the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Xuanwu went to the suburban altars and ancestral temples, Xiu regularly rode in the side carriage as Regular Attendant and concurrently Palace Attendant, while Yong as Director of the Imperial Carriage held the reins in the same carriage.

sentences.zh: 時人竊論，號為二趙。

translations.literal: People of the time privately discussed them and called them the Two Zhaos.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time privately called them the Two Zhaos.

sentences.zh: 以趙出南陽，徙屬荊州。

translations.literal: Because the Zhao clan came from Nanyang, their registration was moved to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Zhao clan came from Nanyang, their registration was moved to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 邕轉給事中，南陽中正。

translations.literal: Yong was transferred to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Chief Rectifier of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was transferred to Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Chief Rectifier of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 以父為荊州大中正，罷。

translations.literal: Because his father was Chief Rectifier of Jingzhou, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father was Chief Rectifier of Jingzhou, he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 宣武崩，邕兼給事黃門。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu died, Yong concurrently served as Attendant of the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, Yong concurrently served as Attendant of the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 後為幽州刺史，貪與范陽盧氏為婚，女父早亡，其叔許之，而母不從。

translations.literal: Later he became Governor of Youzhou; greedy for a marriage with the Lu clan of Fanyang, the girl's father had died early and her uncle consented, but the mother did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Governor of Youzhou; greedy for a marriage with the Lu clan of Fanyang, the girl's father had died early and her uncle consented, but the mother did not agree.

sentences.zh: 母北平陽氏，攜女至家藏避，規免。

translations.literal: The mother was the Lady Yang of Beiping; she took the girl home to hide and avoid the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The mother was Lady Yang of Beiping; she took the girl home to hide and avoid the marriage.

sentences.zh: 邕乃考掠陽叔，遂至於死。

translations.literal: Yong then tortured and flogged Yang's uncle until he died.
translations.idiomatic: Yong then tortured and flogged Lady Yang's uncle until he died.

sentences.zh: 陽氏訴冤，邕坐處死。

translations.literal: The Lady Yang appealed her wrong; Yong was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang appealed her wrong; Yong was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 會赦，免。

translations.literal: An amnesty came and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty came and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，卒。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Xiaochang he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning of Xiaochang he died.

sentences.zh: 侯剛，字乾之，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Hou Gang, styled Qianzhi, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Gang, courtesy name Qianzhi, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 其先代人，本出寒微。

translations.literal: His ancestors for generations were commoners; the family originally came from humble origins.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors for generations were commoners; the family originally came from humble origins.

sentences.zh: 少以善於鼎俎，得進膳出入，積官至嘗食典禦。

translations.literal: As a youth, skilled at handling dishes and sacrificial vessels, he gained entry to serve meals and pass in and out of the palace; he rose through posts to become Director of Imperial Tasting.
translations.idiomatic: In youth his skill with dishes and sacrificial vessels won him entry to the imperial kitchens; rising through the ranks, he eventually became Director of Imperial Tasting.

sentences.zh: 宣武以其質直，賜名剛焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu, because of his plain forthrightness, bestowed upon him the name Gang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu gave him the name Gang in recognition of his plainspoken character.

sentences.zh: 稍遷左中郎將，領刀劍左右，後領太子中庶子。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Left Commandant of the Center, in charge of the sword bearers at the emperor's side, and later served as Grand Tutor Attendant to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to Left Commandant of the Center, commanding the emperor's sword bearers at court, and later served as Grand Tutor Attendant to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 宣武崩，剛與侍中崔光迎明帝於東宮，尋除衛尉卿，封武陽縣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu died, Gang together with Palace Attendant Cui Guang welcomed Emperor Ming at the Eastern Palace; shortly after he was appointed Commandant of the Guard and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, Gang and Palace Attendant Cui Guang went to the Eastern Palace to install Emperor Ming; he was soon made Commandant of the Guard and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang County.

sentences.zh: 俄為侍中、撫軍將軍、恆州大中正，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Soon he became Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Chief Rectifier of Heng Province, and was advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he held the posts of Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Chief Rectifier of Heng Province, and was raised to the rank of duke.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，侍中游肇出為相州，剛言于靈太后曰：「昔高氏擅權，遊肇抗衡不屈，而出牧一籓，未盡其美。

translations.literal: In the Xiping era, Palace Attendant You Zhao went out to serve as governor of Xiang Province. Gang said to Empress Dowager Ling: "In the past when the Gao clan monopolized power, You Zhao resisted them without yielding, yet he was sent out to govern a single frontier region—the full measure of his worth has not been employed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiping era, when Palace Attendant You Zhao was sent out as governor of Xiang Province, Gang told Empress Dowager Ling: "When the Gao clan once held unchecked power, You Zhao stood up to them without bending, yet he was posted to govern a single frontier province—surely he has not been given his full due.

sentences.zh: 宜還引入，以輔聖主。」

translations.literal: He should be recalled and brought back in to assist the sage sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: He ought to be recalled to court to aid the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 太后善之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager approved.

sentences.zh: 剛寵任既隆，江陽王繼、尚書長孫承業皆以女妻其子。

translations.literal: Once Gang's favor and appointment had risen high, Prince Jiangyang Ji and Minister of Works Changsun Chengye both gave their daughters in marriage to his sons.
translations.idiomatic: As Gang's favor rose ever higher, Prince Jiangyang Ji and Minister of Works Changsun Chengye married their daughters to his sons.

sentences.zh: 司空、任城王澄以其起由膳宰，頗竊侮之云：「此近為我舉食。」

translations.literal: The Minister of Works, Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng, because he had risen from the rank of meal server, secretly slighted him, saying: "This man not long ago was serving food for me.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cheng, Prince of Rencheng and Minister of Works, looked down on him for having come up from the kitchens and was heard to mutter: "Not long ago this fellow was waiting on me at table.

sentences.zh: 然公坐對集，敬遇不虧。

translations.literal: Yet at public gatherings, his respectful treatment did not fall short.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in public assemblies he still treated him with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 後剛坐掠殺試射羽林，為御史中尉元匡所彈，處剛大辟。

translations.literal: Later Gang was charged with plundering and killing at a trial archery session of the Imperial Guard; he was impeached by the Director of the Censorate Yuan Kuang and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gang was impeached by Director of the Censorate Yuan Kuang for plundering and killing during an Imperial Guard archery trial, and was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、任城王澄為之言于靈太后，令削封三百戶，解嘗食典禦。

translations.literal: Minister of Works and Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng spoke on his behalf to Empress Dowager Ling, who ordered his fief reduced by three hundred households and his post as Director of Imperial Tasting removed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yuan Cheng, Prince of Rencheng, pleaded his case before Empress Dowager Ling, who reduced his fief by three hundred households and stripped him of the directorship of Imperial Tasting.

sentences.zh: 剛於是頗為失意。

translations.literal: Gang was at this quite disheartened.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was deeply disheartened.

sentences.zh: 剛自太和進食，遂為典禦，曆兩都、三帝、二太后，將三十年，至此始解。

translations.literal: Gang had entered imperial service to serve meals from the Taihe era and had held the post of Director of Tasting through two capitals, three emperors, and two empress dowagers—nearly thirty years—before at last being removed here.
translations.idiomatic: Gang had entered the kitchens in the Taihe era and served as Director of Imperial Tasting through two capitals, three emperors, and two empresses dowager—nearly thirty years—before he was relieved of the post.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉元匡之廢也，剛為太傅、清河王懌所舉，除車騎將軍，領御史中尉。

translations.literal: When Director of the Censorate Yuan Kuang was dismissed, Gang was recommended by Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi and appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, concurrently serving as Director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Kuang was removed as Director of the Censorate, Grand Tutor Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, recommended Gang, who was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and again put in charge of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 及領軍元叉執政，剛長子，叉之妹夫，乃引剛為侍中、左衛將軍，還領嘗食典禦，以為枝援。

translations.literal: When the Director of the Army Yuan Cha took power—Gang's eldest son being Cha's brother-in-law—Cha brought Gang in as Palace Attendant and General of the Left Guard, restoring to him the directorship of Imperial Tasting as a supporting ally.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha, Director of the Army, seized power, he brought in Gang—whose eldest son was Cha's brother-in-law—as Palace Attendant and General of the Left Guard, restoring him to the directorship of Imperial Tasting as a pillar of support.

sentences.zh: 復令御史中尉。

translations.literal: He was again made Director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Director of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 剛啟軍旅稍興，國用不足，求以己邑俸粟，賑給征人，比至軍下。

translations.literal: Gang memorialized that with military campaigns rising, state revenue was insufficient, and requested that grain from his fief salary be used to relieve troops on campaign, delivered down to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Gang reported that military levies were growing while state funds ran short, and asked that grain from his fief income be used to feed conscripts right down to the front-line armies.

sentences.zh: 明帝許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming granted this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming approved.

sentences.zh: 孝昌元年，除領軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaochang, he was appointed Director of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaochang he was made Director of the Army.

sentences.zh: 初，元叉之解領軍，靈太后以叉腹心尚多，恐難卒制，故權以剛代之，示安其意。

translations.literal: At first, when Yuan Cha was removed from the directorship of the army, Empress Dowager Ling, knowing that Cha still had many partisans at heart, feared she could not quickly control him, and so provisionally replaced him with Gang to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha was first removed as Director of the Army, Empress Dowager Ling feared she could not quickly tame his many loyalists, and so temporarily put Gang in his place to mollify him.

sentences.zh: 尋出為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted out as governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 剛在道，詔暴其朋黨元叉，逼脅內外，降為征虜將軍，余悉削黜。

translations.literal: While Gang was on the road, an edict exposed his faction ally Yuan Cha for coercing court and countryside; Gang was demoted to General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and everything else was stripped away.
translations.idiomatic: While Gang was en route, an edict exposed his associate Yuan Cha for intimidating the court inside and out; Gang was demoted to General Who Conquers the Barbarians and all his other honors were stripped away.

sentences.zh: 終於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 永安中，贈司徒公。

translations.literal: During the Yong'an era, he was posthumously granted the title Duke of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he was posthumously made Duke of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 剛以上谷先有侯氏，於是始家焉。

translations.literal: Gang, because Shanggu had long had the Hou clan, thereupon established his household there.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shanggu had long been home to the Hou clan, Gang established his family seat there.

sentences.zh: 徐紇字，武伯，樂安博昌人也。

translations.literal: Xu He, styled Wubo, was a native of Bochang in Le'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu He, styled Wubo, came from Bochang in Le'an Commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世寒微。

translations.literal: His family for generations was humble and poor.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been humble for generations.

sentences.zh: 紇少好學，頗以文詞見稱。

translations.literal: He from youth loved learning and was quite praised for his literary compositions.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved study and won recognition for his literary talent.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，自主書除中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, on the basis of his own handwriting he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was appointed Secretariat Drafter on the strength of his calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 諂附趙脩，脩誅，坐徙枹罕。

translations.literal: He flattered and attached himself to Zhao Xiu; when Xiu was executed, he was implicated and exiled to Bohan.
translations.idiomatic: He fawned on Zhao Xiu; when Xiu was executed he was implicated and banished to Bohan.

sentences.zh: 雖在徒役，志氣不撓。

translations.literal: Though serving in penal labor, his spirit did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: Though condemned to penal labor, his spirit never broke.

sentences.zh: 故事，捉逃役流兵五人者，聽免，紇以此得還。

translations.literal: By precedent, one who captured five fugitive conscripts or deserters was permitted release; He used this to gain return.
translations.idiomatic: Under existing rules, anyone who captured five fugitive soldiers or deserters could be released from service; He secured his return by this means.

sentences.zh: 久之，復除中書舍人。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was again appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was again made Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 太傅、清河王懌以文翰待之。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi treated him as a literary companion.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, treated him as a literary companion.

sentences.zh: 及元叉害懌，出為雁門太守，稱母老解郡。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha killed Yi, he was sent out as governor of Yanmen, then citing his mother's age resigned the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Cha killed Yuan Yi, he was posted as governor of Yanmen, then resigned citing his mother's advanced age.

sentences.zh: 尋飾貌事叉，大得叉意。

translations.literal: Soon he adorned his manner to serve Cha and greatly won Cha's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he trimmed his manner to court Cha and won his deep favor.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，以紇曾為懌所顧待，復自母憂中起為中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, because He had once been favored by Yi, he was again raised from mourning for his mother to become Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling reclaimed power, He—who had once enjoyed Yuan Yi's patronage—was recalled from mourning for his mother and restored as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 曲事鄭儼，是以特被信任，俄遷給事黃門侍郎，仍領舍人，總攝中書、門下事，軍國詔命，莫不由之。

translations.literal: He bent himself to serve Zheng Yan, and for this was especially trusted; soon he was promoted to Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate, retaining his drafter post, overseeing overall the affairs of the Secretariat and Chancellery—all military and state edicts passed through him.
translations.idiomatic: He abased himself before Zheng Yan and thereby won exceptional trust; he was soon promoted to Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate while retaining his drafter duties, overseeing Secretariat and Chancellery business so that every military and state decree passed through his hands.

sentences.zh: 時有急速，令數吏執筆，或行或臥，人別占之，造次俱成，不失事理，雖無雅才，咸得濟用。

translations.literal: When matters were urgent, he would have several clerks take brush in hand—walking or lying down, each dictating in turn—and orders were completed instantly without losing coherence; though lacking refined talent, all proved useful.
translations.idiomatic: In urgent cases he had several clerks take dictation on the move or even lying down, each covering a separate thread; drafts were finished in haste yet never lost their point. Unrefined though they were, they always served their purpose.

sentences.zh: 時黃門侍郎太原王遵業、琅邪王誦，並稱文學，亦不免為紇執筆，承其指授。

translations.literal: At the time Supervising Secretaries Wang Zunye of Taiyuan and Wang Song of Langya, both famed for literary talent, also could not avoid serving as He's scribes and following his direction.
translations.idiomatic: Even Wang Zunye of Taiyuan and Wang Song of Langya—Supervising Secretaries famed for literary skill—had to take dictation for He and follow his instructions.

sentences.zh: 紇機辯有智數，當公斷決，終日不以為勞。

translations.literal: He was quick-witted and resourceful; when presiding over public decisions, he did not regard a whole day as labor.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and crafty, he could preside over public deliberations all day without fatigue.

sentences.zh: 長直禁中，略無休息。

translations.literal: He long held overnight duty within the palace and hardly rested at all.
translations.idiomatic: He kept long watches within the palace and scarcely rested.

sentences.zh: 時復與沙門講論，或分宵達曙，而心力無怠，道俗嘆服之。

translations.literal: At times he also debated with Buddhist monks, sometimes from night until dawn, yet his mind and strength did not flag; clergy and laity alike admired him.
translations.idiomatic: At times he debated with Buddhist monks through the night until dawn, yet his energy never flagged—monks and laymen alike marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 然性浮動，慕權利，外似謇正，內實諂諛。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was restless; he coveted power and profit. Outwardly he seemed upright, inwardly he was flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was restless by nature, greedy for power and profit; upright in appearance, he was a flatterer at heart.

sentences.zh: 時豪勝己，必相陵駕；

translations.literal: When the mighty of the time surpassed him, he was sure to try to dominate them;
translations.idiomatic: Toward contemporaries more powerful than himself he always tried to dominate;

sentences.zh: 書生貧士，矯意禮之。

translations.literal: toward poor scholars and men of humble station he affectation showed courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: toward poor scholars and men of humble station he put on exaggerated courtesy.

sentences.zh: 其詭態若此，有識鄙焉。

translations.literal: His devious manner was like this; men of discernment despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Such were his double-faced ways, and men of judgment held him in contempt.

sentences.zh: 紇既處腹心，參斷機密，勢傾一時，遠近填湊。

translations.literal: He now stood in the innermost confidence, shared in deciding secrets, and his power eclipsed the age; men from near and far crowded about him.
translations.idiomatic: Once established at the emperor's side, he shared in weighty secrets, eclipsed all rivals for a time, and was thronged by petitioners from far and near.

sentences.zh: 與鄭儼、李神軌寵任相亞，時稱徐、鄭焉。

translations.literal: With Zheng Yan and Li Shengui his favor and trust ranked a close second; at the time he was called Xu and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: His favor and trust rivaled those of Zheng Yan and Li Shengui, and people spoke of him together with Zheng as Xu and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 然無經國大體，好行小數，說靈太后以鐵券間爾硃榮左右。

translations.literal: Yet he lacked the great principles of governing a state; he loved petty stratagems and persuaded Empress Dowager Ling to use iron tallies to sow discord among Erzhu Rong's intimates.
translations.idiomatic: He had no grasp of statecraft on a grand scale and loved petty schemes, persuading Empress Dowager Ling to use iron tallies to drive wedges among Erzhu Rong's close associates.

sentences.zh: 榮知，深以為憾，啟求誅之。

translations.literal: When Rong learned of it he deeply resented it and memorialized asking that He be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong learned of this he was deeply aggrieved and submitted a memorial requesting He's execution.

sentences.zh: 榮將入洛，既克河梁，紇矯詔夜開殿中，取驊騮御馬十餘疋，東走兗州。

translations.literal: As Rong was about to enter Luoyang, having taken Heqiao, He forged an edict and at night opened the palace offices, took more than ten imperial thoroughbreds, and fled east to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was about to enter Luoyang after capturing Heqiao, He forged an edict, opened the palace offices by night, seized more than ten imperial horses, and fled east to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 羊侃時為太山太守，紇往投之，說侃令舉兵。

translations.literal: Yang Kan was then governor of Taishan; He went to join him and urged Kan to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kan was then governor of Taishan; He went to him and urged him to raise an army.

sentences.zh: 侃從之，遂聚兵反，共紇圍兗州。

translations.literal: Kan agreed, gathered troops in rebellion, and together with He besieged Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kan agreed, raised troops in revolt, and together with He besieged Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，遣侍中於暉為行台，與齊神武討之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu Hui was sent as chief of a mobile headquarters to suppress them together with Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign, Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu Hui was dispatched as head of a mobile headquarters to suppress them with Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 紇慮不免，說侃請乞師于梁，侃信之，遂奔梁。

translations.literal: He, fearing he could not escape, urged Kan to send to Liang for reinforcements; Kan believed him and fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he could not escape, He persuaded Kan to request troops from Liang; Kan believed him and fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 文筆駁論十卷，多有遺落，時或存於世焉。

translations.literal: His literary work Bolun in ten scrolls had many losses; some still survive in the world at times.
translations.idiomatic: His ten-scroll literary work Bolun has suffered many losses, though portions still circulate from time to time.

sentences.zh: 宗愛不知其所由來，以罪為閹人，曆碎職至中常侍。

translations.literal: Zong Ai's origins were unknown; for a crime he became a eunuch and through minor posts rose to Palace Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: No one knew where Zong Ai came from; punished for a crime, he entered the palace as a eunuch and rose through minor posts to Palace Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 正平元年元正，太武大會于江上，班賞群臣，以愛為秦郡公。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the first year of Zhengping, Emperor Taiwu held a great assembly on the river and distributed rewards to the ministers, making Ai Duke of Qin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day in the first year of Zhengping, Emperor Taiwu held a great assembly on the river, rewarded the ministers, and enfeoffed Ai as Duke of Qin Commandery.

sentences.zh: 景穆之監國也，每事精察，愛天性險暴，行多非法，景穆每銜之。

translations.literal: When Jingmu supervised the state he scrutinized everything minutely; Ai was naturally cruel and violent and his conduct was often illegal, and Jingmu always harbored resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising the realm, Jingmu scrutinized every matter closely; Ai was cruel and violent by nature and often acted unlawfully, and Jingmu always resented him.

sentences.zh: 給事中侯道盛、侍郎任平城等任事東宮，微為權勢，太武頗聞之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Hou Daosheng, Gentleman Ren Pingcheng, and others handled affairs in the Eastern Palace and slightly wielded power; Emperor Taiwu heard much of it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Hou Daosheng, Gentleman Ren Pingcheng, and others managed Eastern Palace affairs and wielded a measure of power; Emperor Taiwu heard frequent reports of it.

sentences.zh: 二人與愛並不睦，愛懼道盛等案其事，遂構告其罪，詔斬道盛等於都街。

translations.literal: The two men were not on good terms with Ai; Ai feared Daosheng and the others would investigate his affairs, so he framed and reported their crimes, and an edict ordered Daosheng and the others beheaded in the capital street.
translations.idiomatic: The two were on bad terms with Ai; fearing they would investigate him, Ai fabricated charges against them, and an edict ordered Daosheng and the others beheaded in the capital streets.

sentences.zh: 時太武震怒，景穆遂以憂薨。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Taiwu was greatly enraged, and Jingmu thereupon died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu was furious, and Jingmu died of grief.

sentences.zh: 是後，太武追悼不已，愛懼誅，遂謀逆。

translations.literal: After this, as Emperor Taiwu mourned without cease, Ai feared execution and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, as Emperor Taiwu mourned without end, Ai feared execution and plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 二年春，太武暴崩，愛所為也。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, Emperor Taiwu died suddenly—Ai's doing.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year Emperor Taiwu died suddenly—Ai was responsible.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射蘭延、侍中吳興公和疋、侍中太原公薛提等秘不發喪。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Lan Yan, Palace Attendant Duke of Wuxing He Pi, and Palace Attendant Duke of Taiyuan Xue Ti and others kept the death secret and did not announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Lan Yan, Palace Attendant Duke of Wuxing He Pi, Palace Attendant Duke of Taiyuan Xue Ti, and others concealed the death and did not announce mourning.

sentences.zh: 延、疋二人議，以文成沖幼、欲立長君，徵秦王翰，置之秘室。

translations.literal: Yan and Pi debated that, as Emperor Wencheng was young, they wished to install an elder ruler; they summoned Prince of Qin Han and placed him in a secret chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Pi argued that since Emperor Wencheng was young they should install an elder ruler; they summoned Prince of Qin Han and confined him in a secret chamber.

sentences.zh: 提以文成有世嫡之重，不可廢所宜立而更求君。

translations.literal: Ti held that Emperor Wencheng bore the weight of legitimate succession and that one could not set aside the one who ought to be installed and seek another ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Ti argued that Emperor Wencheng carried the weight of legitimate succession and that they could not set aside the rightful heir and seek another ruler.

sentences.zh: 延等猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Yan and the others hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and the others hesitated and could not reach a decision.

sentences.zh: 愛知其謀。

translations.literal: Ai learned of their plan.
translations.idiomatic: Ai learned of their plot.

sentences.zh: 始愛負罪於東宮，而與吳王餘素協，乃密迎餘，自中宮便門入，矯皇后令徵延等。

translations.literal: At first Ai had been guilty toward the Eastern Palace; he had long been in league with Prince of Wu Yu, so he secretly welcomed Yu, who entered through the side gate of the inner palace; Ai forged the empress's order summoning Yan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Ai had earlier offended the Eastern Palace but was long allied with Prince of Wu Yu; he secretly welcomed Yu through the inner palace side gate and forged the empress's order summoning Yan and the others.

sentences.zh: 延等以愛素賤，弗之疑，皆隨之入。

translations.literal: Yan and the others, because Ai had always been base, did not suspect him and all followed him in.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ai had always been lowly, Yan and the others did not suspect him and all followed him inside.

sentences.zh: 愛先使閹豎三十人持仗于宮內，及延等入，以次收縛，斬于殿堂。

translations.literal: Ai had first placed thirty eunuch attendants with weapons in the palace; when Yan and the others entered, they were seized in order and beheaded in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ai had posted thirty armed eunuchs in the palace; when Yan and the others entered, they were seized one by one and beheaded in the hall.

sentences.zh: 執秦王翰，殺之於永巷，而立餘。

translations.literal: They seized Prince of Qin Han, killed him in Yong Lane, and installed Yu.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Prince of Qin Han, killed him in Yong Lane, and enthroned Yu.

sentences.zh: 余以愛為大司馬、大將軍、太師、都督中外諸軍事，領中秘書，封馮翊王。

translations.literal: Yu made Ai Grand Marshal, Grand General, Grand Preceptor, Commander-in-Chief of All Forces at Home and Abroad, head of the Central Secretariat, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu appointed Ai Grand Marshal, Grand General, Grand Preceptor, Commander-in-Chief of All Forces at Home and Abroad, and head of the Central Secretariat, enfeoffing him as Prince of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 分既立餘，位居元輔，錄三省，兼總戎禁，坐召公卿，權恣日甚，內外憚之。

translations.literal: Once Yu was installed, Ai stood as chief minister, recorded the Three Ministries, and combined control of military guards; summoning ministers while seated, his power grew daily more arbitrary, and inside and outside feared him.
translations.idiomatic: With Yu enthroned, Ai became chief minister, oversaw the Three Ministries, and controlled military guards; he summoned ministers while seated, his power grew ever more arbitrary, and court and realm feared him.

sentences.zh: 群情咸以為愛必有趙高、閻樂之禍，餘疑之，遂謀奪其權。

translations.literal: All thought Ai would meet the fate of Zhao Gao and Yan Le; Yu grew suspicious and plotted to strip him of power.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone believed Ai would meet the fate of Zhao Gao and Yan Le; Yu grew suspicious and plotted to seize his power.

sentences.zh: 愛憤怒，使小黃門賈周等夜殺餘。

translations.literal: Enraged, Ai had the Lesser Yellow Gate Jia Zhou and others kill Yu by night.
translations.idiomatic: In fury Ai had Lesser Yellow Gate Jia Zhou and others kill Yu by night.

sentences.zh: 文成立，誅愛、周等，皆具五刑，夷三族。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng was enthroned, Ai, Zhou, and the others were executed, all suffering the five punishments, and their three clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne, Ai, Zhou, and the others were executed with the full five punishments and their three clans were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 仇洛齊，中山人也，本姓侯氏。

translations.literal: Qiu Luoqi was a man of Zhongshan; his original surname was Hou.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Luoqi was from Zhongshan; his original surname was Hou.

sentences.zh: 外祖父仇款，始出馮翊重泉，款仕石季龍末，徙鄴南枋頭。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather Qiu Kuan first came out of Chongquan in Fengyi; Kuan served at the end of Shi Jilong's reign and moved to Fangtou south of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather Qiu Kuan came originally from Chongquan in Fengyi; Kuan served at the end of Shi Jilong's reign and moved to Fangtou south of Ye.

sentences.zh: 仕慕容痈為烏丸護軍、長水校尉。

translations.literal: He served Murong Yong as Wuhuan Protector-General and Colonel of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: He served Murong Yong as Wuhuan Protector-General and Colonel of the Long River.

sentences.zh: 生二子，長曰嵩，小曰騰。

translations.literal: He had two sons; the elder was called Song, the younger Teng.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: the elder was Song, the younger Teng.

sentences.zh: 嵩仕慕容垂，遷居中山，位殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Song served Murong Chui, moved to Zhongshan, and held the post of Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Song served Murong Chui, moved to Zhongshan, and became Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 嵩有二子，長曰廣，小曰盆。

translations.literal: Song had two sons; the elder was called Guang, the younger Pen.
translations.idiomatic: Song had two sons: the elder was Guang, the younger Pen.

sentences.zh: 嵩妹子洛齊，生而非男，嵩養為子，因為仇姓。

translations.literal: Song's younger sister bore Luoqi, who was born not a male; Song raised him as a son, and he therefore took the surname Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Song's younger sister gave birth to Luoqi, who was not born male; Song raised him as a son, and he therefore took the surname Qiu.

sentences.zh: 初，嵩長女有姿色，充冉閔婦。

translations.literal: At first Song's eldest daughter was beautiful and became Ran Min's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Song's eldest daughter was beautiful and became Ran Min's wife.

sentences.zh: 閔破，入慕容俊，又轉賜盧豚，生子魯元。

translations.literal: When Min was defeated she entered Murong Jun's service and was later given to Lu Tun, bearing a son, Lu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Min fell she entered Murong Jun's household and was later given to Lu Tun, bearing a son named Lu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 魯元有寵于太武，而知外祖嵩已死，唯有三舅，每言於帝。

translations.literal: Lu Yuan was favored by Emperor Taiwu and knew that his maternal grandfather Song was already dead and that he had only three maternal uncles; he spoke of them often to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuan enjoyed Emperor Taiwu's favor; knowing his maternal grandfather Song was dead and that he had only three maternal uncles, he often mentioned them to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝為訪其舅。

translations.literal: The emperor sought out her uncles.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set out to find her uncles.

sentences.zh: 時東方罕有仕者，廣、盆皆不樂入平城。

translations.literal: At the time men from the east rarely entered office; Guang and Pen were both unwilling to go to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Few easterners then took office; Guang and Pen both disliked going to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 洛齊獨請行曰：「我養子，兼人道不全，當為兄弟試禍福也。」

translations.literal: Luoqi alone asked to go, saying, "I am an adopted son and moreover not fully a man in the human way; I ought to test fortune and misfortune for my brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Luoqi alone volunteered, saying, "I am an adopted son and, moreover, not a complete man; let me test fortune and misfortune for my brothers.

sentences.zh: 乃乘驢赴京。

translations.literal: Then he rode a donkey to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode a donkey to the capital.

sentences.zh: 魯元候知將至，結從者百餘騎，迎于桑乾河，見而下拜，從者亦同致敬。

translations.literal: Lu Yuan, knowing he was about to arrive, gathered more than a hundred mounted followers and met him at the Sanggan River; on seeing him he bowed, and his followers likewise paid respect.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuan, forewarned of his arrival, gathered more than a hundred mounted followers and met him at the Sanggan River; he bowed on sight, and his followers did likewise.

sentences.zh: 入言于太武。

translations.literal: He entered and reported to Emperor Taiwu.
translations.idiomatic: He entered and reported to Emperor Taiwu.

sentences.zh: 太武問其才用所宜，魯元曰：「臣舅不幸，生為閹人，唯合與陛下守宮闈耳。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu asked what talent and use suited him; Lu Yuan said, "My uncle, alas, was born a eunuch and is fit only to guard the palace precincts with Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu asked what post suited him; Lu Yuan said, "My uncle, alas, was born a eunuch and is fit only to guard the palace with Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 而不言其養子。

translations.literal: He did not mention that he was an adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: He did not mention that Luoqi was an adopted son.

sentences.zh: 帝矜焉，引見敘用，賜爵文安子，稍遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor took pity on him, summoned and employed him, enfeoffed him as Baron of Wen'an, and gradually promoted him to Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on him, summoned him to office, enfeoffed him as Baron of Wen'an, and gradually promoted him to Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 魏初，禁網疏闊，人戶隱匿，漏脫者多。

translations.literal: In the early Wei, the regulatory net was loose and many households were concealed and escaped registration.
translations.idiomatic: In early Wei the regulatory net was loose, and many households hid themselves and escaped registration.

sentences.zh: 東州既平，綾羅戶人樂葵，因是請采漏戶，供為綸綿，自後逃戶占為槹綾羅縠者非一。

translations.literal: After the eastern provinces were pacified, Yue Kui, a member of the silk-brocade households, thereupon requested to register escaped households to supply silk floss; afterward many fugitive households were registered as silk-brocade households—not just one case.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern provinces were pacified, Yue Kui of the silk-brocade households requested to register escaped households for silk floss; thereafter many fugitives were registered as silk-brocade households, and not in one case alone.

sentences.zh: 於是雜營戶帥遍於天下，不屬守宰，發賦輕易，人多私附，戶口錯亂，不可撿括。

translations.literal: Thereupon leaders of miscellaneous camp households spread throughout the realm, not subject to local officials; levies were light and easy, many privately attached themselves, household registers were confused, and could not be sorted out.
translations.idiomatic: Leaders of miscellaneous camp households then spread across the realm, outside the control of local officials; levies were light, many attached themselves privately, registers fell into chaos, and could not be straightened out.

sentences.zh: 洛齊奏議罷之，一屬郡縣。

translations.literal: Luoqi memorialized proposing to abolish the system and place all under commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Luoqi submitted a memorial proposing abolition and placing all households under commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 從征平涼，以功超遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: On the campaign to pacify Liangzhou he was promoted by merit to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liangzhou campaign he was promoted by merit to Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 又加中書令，進爵零陵公，拜侍中、冀州刺史、內都大官。

translations.literal: He was further made Director of the Secretariat, advanced to Duke of Lingling, and appointed Palace Attendant, governor of Jizhou, and Grand Inner Palace Official.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Director of the Secretariat, advanced to Duke of Lingling, and appointed Palace Attendant, governor of Jizhou, and Grand Inner Palace Official.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named Kang.

sentences.zh: 養子儼，襲爵。

translations.literal: His adopted son Yan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Yan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 太武時，又有段霸，以謹敏見知。

translations.literal: In Emperor Taiwu's time there was also Duan Ba, known for careful diligence.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Taiwu's reign there was also Duan Ba, known for careful diligence.

sentences.zh: 曆中常侍、殿中尚書、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Palace Regular Attendant, Palace Director of the Masters of Writing, and governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Palace Regular Attendant and Palace Director of the Masters of Writing to governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 王琚，高平人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ju was a man of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ju was from Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 自雲本太原人，高祖始，晉豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He claimed his ancestors were originally men of Taiyuan; from the time of the high ancestor they had been governors of Yuzhou in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Taiyuan; from the time of the high ancestor his family had held the post of governor of Yuzhou under Jin.

sentences.zh: 琚以秦常中被刑，入宮禁。

translations.literal: Ju was punished during the Qinchang era and entered the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Ju was punished during the Qinchang era and entered palace service.

sentences.zh: 小心守節，久乃見敘用，稍遷禮部尚書，賜爵廣平公。

translations.literal: Careful and upright, after a long time he was employed, gradually rose to Minister of Rites, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and upright, he was eventually given office, rose to Minister of Rites, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 孝文以琚曆奉前朝，志存公正，授散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, because Ju had long served the previous dynasty and kept his mind on fairness, appointed him Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, noting that Ju had long served the previous dynasty with a mind for fairness, appointed him Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後歷位冀州刺史，假廣平王，進爵高平王。

translations.literal: Later he successively held the post of governor of Jizhou, was given the title Prince of Guangping in name, and advanced to Prince of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as governor of Jizhou, was granted the nominal title Prince of Guangping, and advanced to Prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 孝文、文明太后東巡冀州，親幸其家。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming toured Jizhou in the east, they personally visited his home.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming toured eastern Jizhou, they personally visited his home.

sentences.zh: 還京，以其年老，拜散騎常侍，養老於家，前後賜以車馬、衣物，不可稱計。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, because he was old he was appointed Regular Attendant and retired at home; before and after he was given carriages, horses, and clothing beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he was made Regular Attendant and allowed to retire at home; over the years he received carriages, horses, and clothing beyond count.

sentences.zh: 又降爵為公。

translations.literal: His title was again reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His title was reduced again to duke.

sentences.zh: 扶老自平城從遷洛邑。

translations.literal: Leaning on a staff, he followed the move from Pingcheng to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Leaning on a staff, he followed the transfer from Pingcheng to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 常飲牛乳，色如處子。

translations.literal: He constantly drank cow's milk and his complexion was like that of a maiden.
translations.idiomatic: He drank cow's milk constantly and his complexion was like a maiden's.

sentences.zh: 卒年九十，贈冀州刺史，諡靖公。

translations.literal: He died at ninety; posthumously he was made governor of Jizhou and posthumously named Duke Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety and was posthumously made governor of Jizhou with the posthumous name Duke Jing.

sentences.zh: 趙默，字文靜，初名海，本涼州隸戶。

translations.literal: Zhao Mo, styled Wenjing, originally named Hai, was originally a dependent household of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Mo, styled Wenjing, originally named Hai, came from a dependent household of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 自雲，其先河內溫人也，五世祖術，晉末為西夷校尉，因居酒泉安彌縣。

translations.literal: He claimed his ancestors were men of Wen in Henei; his fifth-generation ancestor Shu in the late Jin served as Colonel of the Western Barbarians and therefore settled in Anmi County, Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed his ancestors were from Wen in Henei; his fifth-generation ancestor Shu served as Colonel of the Western Barbarians in late Jin and settled in Anmi County, Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 海生而涼州平，沒入而為閹人，因改名默。

translations.literal: When Hai was born Liangzhou was pacified; he was confiscated and became a eunuch, and therefore changed his name to Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Hai was born just as Liangzhou was pacified; confiscated, he became a eunuch and changed his name to Mo.

sentences.zh: 有容貌，恭謹小心，賜爵睢陽侯，累遷選部尚書。

translations.literal: Handsome in appearance, respectful and careful, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Suiyang and successively rose to Minister of the Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and respectful, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Suiyang and rose to Minister of the Selection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 能自謹勵，當官任舉，頗得其人，加侍中，進爵河內公。

translations.literal: Able to discipline himself, in office his recommendations were mostly well chosen; he was made Palace Attendant and advanced to Duke of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Disciplined in office, his recommendations were mostly apt; he was made Palace Attendant and advanced to Duke of Henei.

sentences.zh: 獻文將傳位京兆王子推，訪諸群臣，百官唯唯，莫敢先言，唯源賀等辭義正直，不肯奉詔。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen was about to pass the throne to Zitu, son of the Prince of Jingzhao; he consulted the ministers, and the officials all murmured assent and none dared speak first—only Yuan He and others spoke uprightly and refused to obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen planned to abdicate in favor of Zitu, son of the Prince of Jingzhao, he consulted the ministers; all murmured assent and none dared speak first—only Yuan He and others spoke uprightly and refused the edict.

sentences.zh: 獻文怒，變色，復以問默。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen was angry, his expression changed, and he again asked Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen grew angry, his face changed, and he asked Mo again.

sentences.zh: 默對曰：「臣以死奉戴皇太子。」

translations.literal: Mo replied, "Your servant will uphold the crown prince even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Mo replied, "Your servant will uphold the crown prince even unto death.

sentences.zh: 獻文默然良久，遂傳位孝文。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen was silent a long time and thereupon passed the throne to Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen was silent a long while and then abdicated to Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 孝文立，得幸兩宮，祿賜優厚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen was enthroned, Mo enjoyed favor in both palaces and received generous salary and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen took the throne, Mo enjoyed favor in both palaces and received generous stipends and gifts.

sentences.zh: 時尚書李䐶亦有寵于獻文，與默對綰選部。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Chong was also favored by Emperor Xianwen; he and Mo jointly oversaw the Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Chong was also favored by Emperor Xianwen; he and Mo jointly oversaw the Selection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 䐶奏中書侍郎崔鑒為東徐州，北部主書郎公孫處顯為荊州，選部監公孫蘧為幽州，皆曰有能，實有私焉。

translations.literal: Chong recommended Secretariat Gentleman Cui Jian for eastern Xuzhou, Northern Department Chief Clerk Gongsun Chuxian for Jingzhou, and Selection Bureau Supervisor Gongsun Qu for Youzhou—all said to be capable, but in fact there was favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Chong recommended Secretariat Gentleman Cui Jian for eastern Xuzhou, Northern Department Chief Clerk Gongsun Chuxian for Jingzhou, and Selection Bureau Supervisor Gongsun Qu for Youzhou—all called capable, but in fact motivated by private favor.

sentences.zh: 默疾其虧亂選體，遂爭於殿庭曰：「以功授官，因爵與祿，國之常典。

translations.literal: Mo resented that he was undermining the selection system and therefore argued in the court hall, saying, "Granting office by merit and salary by rank is the constant rule of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Mo resented the corruption of the selection system and argued in court: "Granting office by merit and salary by rank is the state's constant rule.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、尚書主書郎、諸曹監，勳能俱立，不過列郡。

translations.literal: Directors of the Secretariat, chief clerks of the Masters of Writing, and supervisors of the various bureaus, however meritorious, did not exceed appointment to a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Directors of the Secretariat, chief clerks of the Masters of Writing, and bureau supervisors, however meritorious, were not promoted beyond commandery rank.

sentences.zh: 今䐶皆以為州，臣實為惑。」

translations.literal: Now Chong has made them all governors; your servant is truly perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chong has made them all governors; I am truly perplexed.

sentences.zh: 於是默與䐶遂為深隙。

translations.literal: Thereupon Mo and Chong became deeply estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Mo and Chong thereafter became bitter enemies.

sentences.zh: 䐶竟列默為監藏。

translations.literal: Chong finally had Mo listed as supervisor of the storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Chong finally had Mo posted as supervisor of the storehouse.

sentences.zh: 因黜為門士。

translations.literal: He was then demoted to gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was then demoted to gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 默廢寢忘食，規報前怨。

translations.literal: Mo neglected sleep and food, plotting to repay the old grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Mo neglected sleep and food, plotting revenge.

sentences.zh: 逾年，還入為侍御、散騎常侍、侍中、尚書左僕射，復兼選部如昔。

translations.literal: After more than a year he returned to office as Attendant of the Imperial Guard, Regular Attendant, Palace Attendant, and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, again jointly overseeing the Selection Bureau as before.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he returned as Attendant of the Imperial Guard, Regular Attendant, Palace Attendant, and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, again jointly overseeing the Selection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 及䐶將獲罪，默因抅成以誅之，然後食甘寢安，志於職事。

translations.literal: When Chong was about to be punished, Mo fabricated charges to have him executed; only then did he eat sweetly and sleep peacefully and devote himself to duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong was about to be punished, Mo fabricated charges to have him executed; only then did he eat and sleep in peace and devote himself to duty.

sentences.zh: 出為儀同三司、定州刺史，進爵為王。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Commissioner with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies and governor of Dingzhou, and advanced to prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Commissioner with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies and governor of Dingzhou, and advanced to prince.

sentences.zh: 克己清儉，事濟公私。

translations.literal: Restraining himself and living plainly, his affairs benefited both public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: Restrained and plain in living, his affairs served both public and private ends.

sentences.zh: 後薨于冀州刺史，追贈司空，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Later he died while governor of Jizhou; posthumously he was made Director of Works and posthumously named Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He later died as governor of Jizhou and was posthumously made Director of Works with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 孫小，字茂翹，咸陽石安人也。

translations.literal: Sun Xiao, styled Maoqiao, was a man of Shi'an in Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiao, styled Maoqiao, was from Shi'an in Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 父瓚，姚泓安定護軍，為赫連屈丐所殺，小沒入宮刑。

translations.literal: His father Zan was Protector-General of Anding under Yao Hong and was killed by Helian Qugai; Xiao was subjected to palace punishment.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zan was Protector-General of Anding under Yao Hong and was killed by Helian Qugai; Xiao underwent palace punishment.

sentences.zh: 會魏平統萬，遂徙平城。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Tongwan he was moved to Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei pacified Tongwan he was moved to Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 內侍東宮，以聰識有智略稱。

translations.literal: Serving in the Eastern Palace within the palace, he was known for intelligence and strategic insight.
translations.idiomatic: Serving the Eastern Palace from within the palace, he was known for intelligence and strategic insight.

sentences.zh: 未幾，轉四台中散。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Central Scribe of the Four Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Central Scribe of the Four Offices.

sentences.zh: 太武幸瓜步，慮有北寇之虞，賜爵泥陽子，除留台將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu visited Guabu, fearing northern raids, he enfeoffed Xiao as Baron of Niyang and appointed him General of the Rear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu visited Guabu, fearing northern raids, he enfeoffed Xiao as Baron of Niyang and made him General of the Rear Guard.

sentences.zh: 車駕還都，乃請父瓚贈諡，求更改葬。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he requested posthumous honors for his father Zan and asked to rebury him.
translations.idiomatic: When the court returned to the capital, he requested posthumous honors for his father Zan and asked to rebury him.

sentences.zh: 詔贈秦州刺史、石安縣子，諡曰戴。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made Zan governor of Qinzhou and Baron of Shi'an County, posthumously named Dai.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made Zan governor of Qinzhou and Baron of Shi'an County with the posthumous name Dai.

sentences.zh: 小後拜并州刺史，進爵中都侯。

translations.literal: Later Xiao was appointed governor of Bingzhou and advanced to Marquis of Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was later appointed governor of Bingzhou and advanced to Marquis of Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 州內四郡百餘人，詣闕頌其政化。

translations.literal: More than a hundred men from four commanderies within the province went to court to praise his governance.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred men from four commanderies in the province went to court to praise his governance.

sentences.zh: 後遷冀州刺史，聲稱微少於前。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to governor of Jizhou; his reputation was slightly less than before.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to governor of Jizhou, where his reputation was slightly diminished.

sentences.zh: 然所在清約，當時牧伯，無能及也。

translations.literal: Yet wherever he served he was plain and frugal; among the governors of the time none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet wherever he served he was plain and frugal, and no contemporary governor could match him.

sentences.zh: 性頗忍酷，所養子息，驅逐鞭撻，視如仇讎。

translations.literal: By nature he was rather cruel; the sons he had adopted he drove out and flogged, treating them like enemies.
translations.idiomatic: He was rather cruel by nature; he drove out and flogged the sons he had adopted, treating them like enemies.

sentences.zh: 小之為并州，以郭祚為主簿。

translations.literal: When Xiao was in Bingzhou he took Guo Zuo as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao governed Bingzhou he took Guo Zuo as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 重祚文才，兼任以書記，時人多之。

translations.literal: He valued Zuo's literary talent and also gave him secretarial duties; many at the time praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He valued Zuo's literary talent and also gave him secretarial duties, which many praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 張宗之，字益宗，河南鞏人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongzhi, styled Yizong, was a man of Gong in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongzhi, styled Yizong, was from Gong in Henan.

sentences.zh: 家世寒微。

translations.literal: His family for generations was poor and humble.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been poor and humble for generations.

sentences.zh: 父孟舒，晉將劉裕西征，板假洛陽令。

translations.literal: His father Mengshu, when Jin general Liu Yu marched west, was provisionally appointed magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mengshu was provisionally appointed magistrate of Luoyang when Jin general Liu Yu marched west.

sentences.zh: 初、緱氏宗文邕謀反，脅孟舒等事晉。

translations.literal: At first Zong Wen'ao of Goushi plotted rebellion and coerced Mengshu and others to serve Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Wen'ao of Goushi plotted rebellion he coerced Mengshu and others to serve Jin.

sentences.zh: 孟舒敗，走免。

translations.literal: Mengshu was defeated and fled to safety.
translations.idiomatic: Mengshu was defeated and escaped.

sentences.zh: 宗之被執入京，腐刑。

translations.literal: Zongzhi was seized and taken to the capital and subjected to castration.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi was seized, taken to the capital, and castrated.

sentences.zh: 以忠厚謹慎，擢為侍御中散，賜爵鞏縣侯。

translations.literal: For loyalty and carefulness he was promoted to Attendant Central Scribe and enfeoffed as Marquis of Gong County.
translations.idiomatic: For loyalty and carefulness he was promoted to Attendant Central Scribe and enfeoffed as Marquis of Gong County.

sentences.zh: 曆儀曹、庫部二曹尚書，領中秘書，進爵彭城公，後例降為侯。

translations.literal: He successively served as Minister of the Rites Bureau and Minister of the Storehouse Bureau, headed the Central Secretariat, advanced to Duke of Pengcheng, and later by precedent was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of the Rites and Storehouse Bureaus, headed the Central Secretariat, advanced to Duke of Pengcheng, and was later reduced to marquis by precedent.

sentences.zh: 卒于冀州刺史，贈懷州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died while governor of Jizhou; posthumously he was made governor of Huaizhou and posthumously named Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died as governor of Jizhou and was posthumously made governor of Huaizhou with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 始宗之納南來殷孝祖妻蕭氏，宋儀同三司思話弟思度女也，多悉婦人儀飾故事。

translations.literal: At first Zongzhi took as wife Xiao, wife of Yin Xiaozu who had come from the south—a daughter of Sihu, younger brother of Song's Commissioner with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies Sihua—and she knew much of women's ceremonial adornment and precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzhi first married Xiao, widow of the southern refugee Yin Xiaozu and daughter of Sihu, brother of Song Commissioner Sihua; she knew much of women's ceremonial dress and precedent.

sentences.zh: 太和中，初制六宮服章，蕭被命在內，豫見訪采，數蒙賜賚云。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, when regulations for the six palaces' insignia were first made, Xiao was ordered to serve within and took part in consultation and collection; she repeatedly received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: During Taihe, when insignia for the six palaces were first regulated, Xiao was ordered to serve within, consulted on the designs, and repeatedly received imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 劇鵬，高陽人也。

translations.literal: Ju Peng was a man of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Peng was from Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 粗覽經史，閑曉吏事。

translations.literal: He had roughly surveyed the classics and histories and was familiar with administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had a rough knowledge of the classics and histories and was versed in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 與王質等俱充宦官，性通率，不以閽閹為恥。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Zhi and others he served as a palace eunuch; open and direct by nature, he was not ashamed of being a gatekeeper-eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a palace eunuch together with Wang Zhi and others; frank by nature, he was not ashamed of being a gatekeeper-eunuch.

sentences.zh: 孝文遷洛，常為宮官任事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang he constantly served as a palace official.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang he regularly served as a palace official.

sentences.zh: 幽後之惑薛菩薩也，鵬密諫止之，不從，遂發憤卒。

translations.literal: When Empress You was infatuated with Xue Pusa, Peng secretly remonstrated to stop it; she would not listen, and he died of indignant rage.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress You was infatuated with Xue Pusa, Peng secretly remonstrated against it; she refused to listen, and he died of indignant rage.

sentences.zh: 張祐，字安福，安定石唐人也。

translations.literal: Zhang You, styled Anfu, was a man of Shitang in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang You, styled Anfu, was from Shitang in Anding.

sentences.zh: 父成，扶風太守，太武末，坐事誅。

translations.literal: His father Cheng was governor of Fufeng; at the end of Emperor Taiwu's reign he was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cheng was governor of Fufeng; at the end of Emperor Taiwu's reign he was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 祐充腐刑，積勞至曹監、中給事。

translations.literal: You underwent castration; through accumulated service he rose to Bureau Supervisor and Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: You was castrated and through accumulated service rose to Bureau Supervisor and Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 文明太后臨朝，中官用事，祐寵倖冠諸閹，官特遷、尚書，進爵隴東公，仍綰內藏曹。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming held court, palace eunuchs held power; You's favor surpassed all eunuchs; he was specially promoted to Minister of the Masters of Writing, advanced to Duke of Longdong, and still oversaw the Inner Storehouse Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming held court, palace eunuchs ruled; You's favor surpassed all others; he was specially promoted to Minister of the Masters of Writing, advanced to Duke of Longdong, and continued to oversee the Inner Storehouse Bureau.

sentences.zh: 未幾監都曹，加侍中，與王睿等俱入八議。

translations.literal: Before long he supervised the Capital Bureau, was made Palace Attendant, and together with Wang Rui and others entered the Eight Deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he supervised the Capital Bureau, was made Palace Attendant, and with Wang Rui and others entered the Eight Deliberations.

sentences.zh: 太后嘉其忠誠，為造甲第。

translations.literal: The empress dowager praised his loyalty and had a grand mansion built for him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager praised his loyalty and had a grand mansion built for him.

sentences.zh: 宅成，孝文、太后親率文武往宴會焉。

translations.literal: When the mansion was completed, Emperor Xiaowen and the empress dowager personally led civil and military officials to feast there.
translations.idiomatic: When the mansion was finished, Emperor Xiaowen and the empress dowager personally led officials to feast there.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書左僕射，進爵新平王，受職于太華庭，備威儀于宮城南，觀者以為榮。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, advanced to Prince of Xinping, received office in Taihua Court, and full ceremonial was prepared south of the palace gate; onlookers considered it glorious.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Xinping, took office in Taihua Court with full ceremony south of the palace gate, and onlookers deemed it glorious.

sentences.zh: 孝文、太后親幸其宅，饗會百官。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen and the empress dowager personally visited his mansion and feasted with the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen and the empress dowager personally visited his mansion and feasted with the officials.

sentences.zh: 祐性恭密，出入機禁二十餘年，未嘗有過。

translations.literal: You was respectful and discreet; for more than twenty years entering and leaving the inner precincts he never had a fault.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful and discreet, for more than twenty years in the inner precincts he never committed a fault.

sentences.zh: 由是特被恩寵，歲月賞賜，家累巨萬。

translations.literal: For this he was especially favored; month by month he received rewards until his household wealth reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was especially favored; rewards month by month made his household wealth enormous.

sentences.zh: 與王質等十七人，俱賜金券，許以不死。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Zhi and sixteen others he was all given gold warrants promising immunity from death.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Wang Zhi and sixteen others he received gold warrants promising immunity from death.

sentences.zh: 薨，孝文親臨之，詔鴻臚典護喪事。

translations.literal: When he died Emperor Xiaowen personally attended; an edict ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonial to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When he died Emperor Xiaowen attended in person; an edict ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonial to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Director of Works and posthumously named Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of Works with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 葬日，車駕親送近郊。

translations.literal: On the day of burial the imperial carriage personally escorted him to the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial the imperial carriage personally escorted him to the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 祐養子顯明，後名慶，少曆內職，有姿貌，江陽王繼以女妻之。

translations.literal: You's adopted son Xianming, later named Qing, in youth held inner posts; handsome in appearance, Prince of Jiangyang Ji gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: You's adopted son Xianming, later named Qing, served in inner posts from youth; handsome, he married the daughter of Prince of Jiangyang Ji.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，降為隴東公，又降為侯。

translations.literal: He inherited the title, which was reduced to Duke of Longdong and then again to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title, which was reduced to Duke of Longdong and then to marquis.

sentences.zh: 抱嶷，字道德，安定石唐人也，居於直谷。

translations.literal: Bao Ni, styled Daode, was a man of Shitang in Anding and lived in Zhigu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Ni, styled Daode, was from Shitang in Anding and lived in Zhigu Valley.

sentences.zh: 自言其先姓郐巳，漢靈帝時，郐巳匡為安定太守。

translations.literal: He claimed his ancestors bore the surname Guiji; in Emperor Ling of Han's time Guiji Kuang was governor of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed his ancestors bore the surname Guiji; in Emperor Ling of Han's time Guiji Kuang was governor of Anding.

sentences.zh: 董卓時，懼誅易氏，即家焉。

translations.literal: In Dong Zhuo's time, fearing execution they changed the surname and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: In Dong Zhuo's time, fearing execution, they changed the surname and settled there.

sentences.zh: 無得而知也。

translations.literal: Nothing more can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing more can be known.

sentences.zh: 幼時，隴東人張乾王反，家染其逆。

translations.literal: In his youth Zhang Qianwang of Longdong rebelled, and the family was implicated in the treason.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Zhang Qianwang of Longdong rebelled, and the family was implicated in treason.

sentences.zh: 及乾王敗，父睹生逃免。

translations.literal: When Qianwang was defeated, his father Dusheng escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianwang was defeated, his father Dusheng escaped.

sentences.zh: 嶷獨與母沒入內宮，受刑，遂為宦人。

translations.literal: Ni alone, with his mother, was confiscated into the inner palace, punished, and thus became a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Ni alone, with his mother, was confiscated into the inner palace, punished, and became a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 小心慎密，累遷中常侍、中曹侍御尚書，賜爵安定公。

translations.literal: Careful and discreet, he successively rose to Palace Regular Attendant and Attendant Director of the Masters of Writing in the Central Bureau, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and discreet, he rose to Palace Regular Attendant and Attendant Director of the Masters of Writing in the Central Bureau and was enfeoffed as Duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 自總納言，職當機近，諸所奏議，必致抗直。

translations.literal: Once he oversaw the Secretariat, his duties were close to power, and in every memorial and proposal he was sure to speak forthrightly.
translations.idiomatic: Once overseeing the Secretariat, close to power, he spoke forthrightly in every memorial and proposal.

sentences.zh: 孝文、文明太后嘉之，以為殿中侍御尚書。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming praised him and made him Attendant Director of the Masters of Writing in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen and Empress Dowager Wenming praised him and made him Attendant Director of the Masters of Writing in the Palace.

sentences.zh: 太后既寵之，乃征其父睹生，拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: Once the empress dowager favored him, she summoned his father Dusheng and appointed him Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager favored him, she summoned his father Dusheng and appointed him Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 將還，見於皇信堂，孝文執手曰：「老人歸途，幾日可達？

translations.literal: About to return, he was received in Huangxin Hall; Emperor Xiaowen took his hand and said, "Old sir, on the road home, how many days until you arrive?
translations.idiomatic: About to return home, he was received in Huangxin Hall; Emperor Xiaowen took his hand and said, "Old sir, how many days until you reach home?

sentences.zh: 好慎行路！」

translations.literal: Take good care on the road!
translations.idiomatic: Travel safely!

sentences.zh: 其見幸如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 睹生卒，贈秦州刺史，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: When Dusheng died he was posthumously made governor of Qinzhou and posthumously named Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Dusheng died he was posthumously made governor of Qinzhou with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 賜黃金八十斤，繒彩及絹八百疋，以供喪用。

translations.literal: They gave eighty jin of gold, eight hundred bolts of silk and colored silk for funeral use.
translations.idiomatic: They gave eighty jin of gold and eight hundred bolts of silk and colored silk for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 並別使勞尉。

translations.literal: A separate envoy was also sent to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: A separate envoy was also sent to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 加嶷大長秋卿。

translations.literal: Ni was further made Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Ni was further made Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 嶷老疾，乞外祿，乃出為涇州刺史，特加右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Ni was old and ill and begged an outside post; he was sent out as governor of Jingzhou and specially made Right Grand Master of Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Old and ill, Ni begged an outside post; he was sent out as governor of Jingzhou and specially made Right Grand Master of Splendor.

sentences.zh: 將之州，孝文餞于西郊樂陽殿，以禦白羽扇賜之。

translations.literal: As he was about to go to his province, Emperor Xiaowen gave a farewell feast at Leyang Hall in the western suburb and bestowed on him the imperial white-feather fan.
translations.idiomatic: As he departed for his province, Emperor Xiaowen feasted him at Leyang Hall in the western suburb and bestowed the imperial white-feather fan.

sentences.zh: 十九年，以刺史從駕南征，以老舊，每見勞問，數道稱嶷之正直。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, as governor he followed the campaign south; because he was old and long in service, whenever they met the emperor inquired after him and often praised Ni's uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he followed the southern campaign as governor; because he was old and long in service, the emperor often inquired after him and praised Ni's uprightness.

sentences.zh: 命乘馬出入行禁之間，與司徒馮誕同例。

translations.literal: He was ordered to ride a horse in and out within the traveling guard, the same privilege as Director of Works Feng Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was permitted to ride in and out within the traveling guard, the same privilege as Director of Works Feng Yan.

sentences.zh: 軍回，還州。

translations.literal: When the army returned he went back to his province.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he went back to his province.

sentences.zh: 自以故老前官，為政多守往法，不能遵用新制。

translations.literal: Considering himself an old former official, in governing he mostly kept to former laws and could not follow the new system.
translations.idiomatic: Considering himself an old former official, he mostly governed by former laws and could not follow the new system.

sentences.zh: 侮慢土族，簡於禮接。

translations.literal: He insulted and slighted the gentry clans and was brief in ceremonial reception.
translations.idiomatic: He insulted the gentry clans and was perfunctory in ceremonial reception.

sentences.zh: 天性酷薄，雖弟侄甥婿，略無存潤。

translations.literal: By nature he was harsh and stingy; even nephews and sons-in-law received hardly any kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh and stingy by nature, he showed hardly any kindness even to nephews and sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 卒於州。

translations.literal: He died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 先以從弟老壽為後，又養太師馮熙子次興。

translations.literal: He had first taken his younger cousin Laoshou as heir and also adopted Cixing, son of Grand Preceptor Feng Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He had first taken his younger cousin Laoshou as heir and also adopted Cixing, son of Grand Preceptor Feng Xi.

sentences.zh: 嶷死後，二人爭立。

translations.literal: After Ni died the two contended over succession.
translations.idiomatic: After Ni died the two contended over succession.

sentences.zh: 嶷妻張氏，致訟經年，得以熙子為後。

translations.literal: Ni's wife Lady Zhang brought suit for years and finally secured Xi's son as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Ni's wife Lady Zhang litigated for years and finally secured Xi's son as heir.

sentences.zh: 老壽亦仍陳訴，終獲紹爵，次興還於本族。

translations.literal: Laoshou also continued to petition; in the end he recovered the title, and Cixing returned to his original clan.
translations.idiomatic: Laoshou also continued to petition; in the end he recovered the title, and Cixing returned to his original clan.

sentences.zh: 老壽凡薄，酒色肆情。

translations.literal: Laoshou was vulgar and shallow and indulged freely in wine and women.
translations.idiomatic: Laoshou was vulgar and indulged freely in wine and women.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉王顯奏言：「前洛州刺史陰平子石榮、積射將軍抱老壽，恣蕩非軌，易室而奸，臊聲布於朝野，醜音被于行路，男女三人，莫知誰子。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian memorialized, saying, "Former governor of Luoyang Baron of Yinping Shi Rong and General of Rapid-Shooting Bao Laoshou have indulged beyond all bounds, changed households and committed adultery; foul reports fill court and countryside, shameful talk spreads on the roads; three children, male and female, and none knows whose they are.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian memorialized: "Former governor of Luoyang Baron of Yinping Shi Rong and General of Rapid-Shooting Bao Laoshou have indulged beyond all bounds, changed households and committed adultery; foul reports fill court and countryside, shameful talk spreads on the roads; three children, and none knows whose they are.

sentences.zh: 人理所未聞，鳥獸之不若。

translations.literal: What human reason has never heard of—worse than birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: What human reason has never heard of—worse than birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 請以見事免官，付廷尉正罪。」

translations.literal: I request that by the facts at hand they be removed from office and handed to the Court of Justice for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I request that by the facts at hand they be removed from office and handed to the Court of Justice for punishment.

sentences.zh: 詔可之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 老壽死後，其舊奴婢尚六七百人。

translations.literal: After Laoshou died his old male and female servants still numbered six or seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: After Laoshou died his old servants still numbered six or seven hundred.

sentences.zh: 老壽及石榮祖父皆造碑銘，就鄉建立，言西方直谷出二貴人。

translations.literal: Laoshou and Shi Rong's grandfathers both had stele inscriptions made and erected in their home districts, saying that two great men came forth from Zhigu Valley in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Laoshou and Shi Rong's grandfathers both had stele inscriptions erected in their home districts, saying two great men came forth from Zhigu Valley in the west.

sentences.zh: 石榮自被劾後，遂廢頓。

translations.literal: After Shi Rong was impeached he fell into decline.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Rong was impeached he fell into decline.

sentences.zh: 子長宣，位南兗州刺史，與侯景反，伏法。

translations.literal: His son Changxuan held the post of governor of southern Yanzhou; he joined Hou Jing in rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changxuan was governor of southern Yanzhou; he joined Hou Jing in rebellion and was executed.

sentences.zh: 王遇，字慶時，本名他惡，馮翊李潤鎮羌也。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, styled Qingshi, originally named Ta'e, was from Zhenqiang in Fufeng's Lirun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, styled Qingshi, originally named Ta'e, was from Zhenqiang in Fufeng's Lirun.

sentences.zh: 與雷、党、不蒙俱為羌中強族。

translations.literal: Together with Lei, Dang, and Bumeng he was among the powerful clans of the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Lei, Dang, and Bumeng he was among the powerful Qiang clans.

sentences.zh: 自雲其先姓王，後改為鉗耳氏，宣武時，改為王焉。

translations.literal: He claimed his ancestors originally bore the surname Wang, later changed to Qian'er, and in Emperor Xuanwu's time changed again to Wang.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed his ancestors originally bore the surname Wang, later changed to Qian'er, and in Emperor Xuanwu's time changed again to Wang.

sentences.zh: 自晉已來，恆為渠長。

translations.literal: From Jin onward they had constantly been canal chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin onward they had constantly served as canal chiefs.

sentences.zh: 遇坐事腐刑，累遷吏部尚書，爵宕昌公。

translations.literal: Yu was castrated for an offense and successively rose to Minister of the Personnel Bureau and was enfeoffed as Duke of Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was castrated for an offense, rose to Minister of the Personnel Bureau, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 出為華州刺史，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was sent out as governor of Huazhou and made Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Huazhou and made Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 幽後之前廢也，遇頗言其過。

translations.literal: When Empress You was deposed the first time, Yu spoke much of her faults.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress You was first deposed, Yu spoke much of her faults.

sentences.zh: 及後進幸，孝文對李沖等申後無咎，而稱遇謗議之罪，遂免遇官，奪其爵。

translations.literal: When she was later restored to favor, Emperor Xiaowen told Li Chong and others that the empress was blameless and cited Yu's crime of slander; Yu was removed from office and stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: When she was later restored to favor, Emperor Xiaowen told Li Chong and others that the empress was blameless and cited Yu's slander; Yu was removed from office and stripped of his title.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，為光祿大夫，復舊爵。
