translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made Grand Master of Splendor and restored to his former title.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made Grand Master of Splendor and restored to his former title.

sentences.zh: 馮氏為尼也，公私罕相供恤，遇自以嘗更奉接，往來祗謁，不替舊敬。

translations.literal: When the Feng clan became nuns, public and private persons rarely offered support; Yu, considering that he had once served them, continued to visit and pay respects without diminishing his old reverence.
translations.idiomatic: When the Feng clan became nuns, few offered support; Yu, having once served them, continued to visit and pay respects without diminishing his old reverence.

sentences.zh: 遇性工巧，強於部分。

translations.literal: Yu was skilled in craftsmanship and strong in planning and division of labor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was skilled in craftsmanship and strong in planning and division of labor.

sentences.zh: 北都方山、靈泉道俗居宇，及文明太后陵廟，洛京東郊馬射壇殿，修廣文昭太后墓園，及東西兩堂，內外諸門制度，皆遇監作。

translations.literal: The dwellings of clergy and laity at Fangshan and Lingquan in the northern capital, Empress Dowager Wenming's tomb and temple, the horse-archery hall and pavilion in Luoyang's eastern suburb, the expanded tomb park of Empress Dowager Wenzhao, and the eastern and western halls and all inner and outer gate systems were all supervised by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The dwellings at Fangshan and Lingquan in the northern capital, Empress Dowager Wenming's tomb and temple, the horse-archery hall in Luoyang's eastern suburb, the expanded tomb park of Empress Dowager Wenzhao, the eastern and western halls, and all inner and outer gate systems were all supervised by Yu.

sentences.zh: 雖年在耆老，朝夕不倦。

translations.literal: Though advanced in years, morning and evening he did not weary.
translations.idiomatic: Though advanced in years, he never wearied from morning to evening.

sentences.zh: 又長於人事，留意酒食之間。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in human relations and attentive to wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled in human relations and attentive to hospitality.

sentences.zh: 每逢僚舊，觴膳精豐。

translations.literal: Whenever he met old colleagues, the wine and dishes were refined and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he met old colleagues, the wine and dishes were lavish.

sentences.zh: 然競于榮利，趨求勢門。

translations.literal: Yet he competed for glory and profit and rushed to seek powerful patrons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he competed for glory and profit and rushed to seek powerful patrons.

sentences.zh: 趙脩之寵也，遇深附會，受敕為之造宅，增於本旨，笞擊作人，莫不嗟怨。

translations.literal: When Zhao Xiu was favored, Yu deeply attached himself to him; by imperial order he built a mansion for him beyond the original plan, flogging the laborers until all sighed in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Xiu was in favor, Yu attached himself deeply; by imperial order he built Xiu a mansion beyond the original plan, flogging laborers until all resented it.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 初遇之疾，太傅北海王與太妃俱往臨問，視其危惙，為之泣下。

translations.literal: When Yu first fell ill, Grand Tutor Prince of Beihai and the grand consort both went to inquire; seeing him in critical distress, they wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu first fell ill, Grand Tutor Prince of Beihai and the grand consort both visited him; seeing him near death, they wept.

sentences.zh: 其善奉諸貴，致相悲悼如此。

translations.literal: In serving the great so well he could move the great to such grief.
translations.idiomatic: So well did he serve the great that they grieved for him like this.

sentences.zh: 贈雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 苻承祖，略陽氐人也。

translations.literal: Fu Chengzu was a man of the Di of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chengzu was a man of the Di of Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 因事為閹人，為文明太后所寵，賜爵略陽公。

translations.literal: For an offense he became a eunuch and was favored by Empress Dowager Wenming; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he became a eunuch and was favored by Empress Dowager Wenming, who enfeoffed him as Duke of Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 曆吏部尚書，加侍中，知都曹事。

translations.literal: He successively served as Minister of the Personnel Bureau, was made Palace Attendant, and managed Capital Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of the Personnel Bureau, was made Palace Attendant, and managed Capital Bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，太后以承祖居腹之心任，許以不死之詔。

translations.literal: At first the empress dowager, trusting Chengzu with her innermost heart, granted him an edict of immunity from death.
translations.idiomatic: At first the empress dowager, trusting Chengzu with her innermost heart, granted him an edict promising immunity from death.

sentences.zh: 後承祖坐贓應死，孝文原之，命削職禁錮在家，授悖義將軍、佞濁子。

translations.literal: Later Chengzu was guilty of embezzlement and deserved death; Emperor Xiaowen pardoned him, ordered his office stripped and house arrest at home, and gave him the titles General of Perverse Righteousness and Viscount of Flattery and Filth.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chengzu was guilty of embezzlement and deserved death; Emperor Xiaowen pardoned him, stripped his office, confined him at home, and gave him the titles General of Perverse Righteousness and Viscount of Flattery and Filth.

sentences.zh: 月餘遂死。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month he died.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a month later he died.

sentences.zh: 王質，字紹奴，高陽易人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi, styled Shaonu, was a man of Yi in Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, styled Shaonu, was from Yi in Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 其家坐事，幼下蠶室。

translations.literal: His family was implicated in an offense and he entered the silkworm chamber in youth.
translations.idiomatic: His family was implicated in an offense and he entered the silkworm chamber in youth.

sentences.zh: 頗解書學，為中曹吏、內典監。

translations.literal: He understood writing and learning fairly well and served as Central Bureau Clerk and Inner Canon Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: He understood writing and learning fairly well and served as Central Bureau Clerk and Inner Canon Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 稍遷秘書中散，賜爵永昌子，領監禦。

translations.literal: He gradually rose to Secretariat Central Scribe, was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongchang, and headed the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually rose to Secretariat Central Scribe, was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongchang, and headed the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 遷為侍御給事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 又領選部、監禦二曹事，進爵魏昌侯。

translations.literal: He also jointly oversaw the Selection Bureau and Imperial Guard bureaus and advanced to Marquis of Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: He also jointly oversaw the Selection Bureau and Imperial Guard and advanced to Marquis of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 轉選部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Selection Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of the Selection Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出為瀛州刺史，風化粗行，人庶畏服之；

translations.literal: Sent out as governor of Yingzhou, he roughly carried out moral transformation and the people feared and submitted to him;
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as governor of Yingzhou, he roughly carried out moral transformation and the people feared and submitted to him;

sentences.zh: 而刑政峻刻，號為威酷。

translations.literal: but his punishments and governance were harsh and he was called formidable and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: but his punishments were harsh and he was called formidable and cruel.

sentences.zh: 孝文頗念其忠勤宿舊，每行留大故、馮司徒亡、廢馮後、陸睿、穆泰等事，皆賜質以璽書手筆，莫不委至，同之戚貴。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen often remembered his long loyalty and old service; on every major leave-taking, the death of Director of Works Feng, the deposition of Empress Feng, and the cases of Lu Rui and Mu Tai and the like, he gave Zhi handwritten edicts with the imperial seal—every detail entrusted, the same as to kin and nobles.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen often remembered his long loyalty; on every major leave-taking, Feng's death, Empress Feng's deposition, and the cases of Lu Rui and Mu Tai, he gave Zhi handwritten sealed edicts with every detail entrusted, as to kin and nobles.

sentences.zh: 質皆寶掌。

translations.literal: Zhi treasured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi treasured them all.

sentences.zh: 入為大長秋卿，卒。

translations.literal: He entered office as Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service and died.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service and died.

sentences.zh: 李堅，字次壽，高陽易人也。

translations.literal: Li Jian, styled Cishou, was a man of Yi in Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jian, styled Cishou, was from Yi in Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 文成初，坐事為閹人，稍遷中給事中，賜爵魏昌伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wencheng's reign he became a eunuch for an offense and gradually rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace, enfeoffed as Count of Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wencheng's reign he became a eunuch for an offense, gradually rose to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace, and was enfeoffed as Count of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 小心謹慎，常在左右，雖不及王遇、王質等，而亦見任用。

translations.literal: Careful and cautious, always at the emperor's side—though not equal to Wang Yu and Wang Zhi and the like, he was also employed.
translations.idiomatic: Careful and cautious, always at the emperor's side—though not equal to Wang Yu and Wang Zhi, he was also employed.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，自太僕卿出為瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he went out from Grand Master of the Household to become governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he left the post of Grand Master of the Household to become governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 本州之榮，同于王質。

translations.literal: The honor in his native province was the same as Wang Zhi's.
translations.idiomatic: The honor in his native province equaled Wang Zhi's.

sentences.zh: 所在受納，家產巨萬。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he accepted bribes until his household wealth reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he accepted bribes until his household wealth was enormous.

sentences.zh: 卒于光祿大夫，贈相州刺史。

translations.literal: He died as Grand Master of Splendor; posthumously he was made governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Grand Master of Splendor and was posthumously made governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 太和末，又有秦松、白整，位並長秋卿。

translations.literal: At the end of Taihe there were also Qin Song and Bai Zheng, both holding the post of Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Taihe there were also Qin Song and Bai Zheng, both Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 劉騰，字青龍，本平原城人也，徙屬南兗州之譙郡。

translations.literal: Liu Teng, styled Qinglong, was originally a man of Pingyuan City and was moved to Qiao Commandery of southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Teng, styled Qinglong, was originally from Pingyuan City and was moved to Qiao Commandery of southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼時坐事受刑，補小黃門，轉中黃門。

translations.literal: In youth he was punished for an offense, entered service as Lesser Yellow Gate, and was transferred to Central Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Punished in youth, he entered service as Lesser Yellow Gate and was transferred to Central Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 孝文之在縣瓠，問其中事，騰具言幽後私隱，與陳留公主所告符協，由是進冗從僕射，仍中黃門。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen was at Xuanhu he questioned him on inner-palace affairs; Teng fully reported Empress You's private misconduct, matching what Princess of Chenliu had reported, and for this was promoted to Supernumerary Vice Director of the Retinue while remaining Central Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen was at Xuanhu he questioned him on inner-palace affairs; Teng fully reported Empress You's private misconduct, matching Princess of Chenliu's report, and was promoted to Supernumerary Vice Director of the Retinue while remaining Central Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 後與茹皓使徐、兗，采召人女。

translations.literal: Later together with Ru Hao he was sent to Xu and Yan to gather and summon women.
translations.idiomatic: Later with Ru Hao he was sent to Xu and Yan to gather women.

sentences.zh: 還，遷中給事。

translations.literal: On returning he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，以與於忠保護勳，除崇訓太僕，加侍中，封長樂縣公。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, because of his merit in protecting Yu Zhong he was made Grand Master of the Household for Honored Instruction, Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Changle County.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, for protecting Yu Zhong he was made Grand Master of the Household for Honored Instruction, Palace Attendant, and Duke of Changle County.

sentences.zh: 拜其妻魏氏為巨鹿郡君，每引入內，受賞賚亞于諸主外戚。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Wei was made Lady of Julu Commandery; each time she was brought within she received rewards second only to princesses and maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Wei was made Lady of Julu Commandery; brought within, she received rewards second only to princesses and maternal kin.

sentences.zh: 所養二子，為郡守、尚書郎。

translations.literal: The two sons he had adopted became a commandery governor and a Masters of Writing Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The two sons he had adopted became a commandery governor and a Masters of Writing Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 騰曾疾篤，靈太后慮或不救，遷衛將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Teng once fell gravely ill, Empress Dowager Ling feared he might not recover and promoted him to General of the Guard and Commissioner with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Teng once fell gravely ill, Empress Dowager Ling feared he might not recover and promoted him to General of the Guard and Commissioner with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 後疾瘳。

translations.literal: Later his illness cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Later he recovered.

sentences.zh: 騰之拜命，孝明當為臨軒，會日，大風寒甚，乃遣使持節授之。

translations.literal: When Teng received appointment Emperor Xiaoming was to preside at the hall audience; on the day a great wind blew bitterly cold, so an envoy bearing credentials was sent to invest him.
translations.idiomatic: When Teng received appointment Emperor Xiaoming was to preside at the hall audience; bitter cold wind blew that day, so an envoy bearing credentials was sent to invest him.

sentences.zh: 騰幼充宮役，手不解書，裁知署名而已，而奸謀有餘，善射人意。

translations.literal: Teng from youth served in the palace and did not understand writing; he could barely sign his name, yet he had ample wicked schemes and was skilled at reading people's minds.
translations.idiomatic: Teng had served in the palace from youth and barely knew writing beyond signing his name, yet he was full of wicked schemes and skilled at reading minds.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，特蒙進寵，多所幹托，內外碎密，棲棲不倦。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court he was especially favored and advanced; he handled many entreaties, inside and outside, trivial and secret, tirelessly and without rest.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court he was especially favored; he handled endless entreaties, trivial and secret, inside and outside, tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 洛北永橋、太上公、太上君及城東三寺，皆主修營。

translations.literal: North of Luoyang at Yong Bridge, the Grand Duke and Grand Lady and the three temples east of the city were all chiefly built under his supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Bridge north of Luoyang, the Grand Duke and Grand Lady, and the three temples east of the city were all chiefly built under his supervision.

sentences.zh: 吏部嘗望騰意，奏其弟為郡，帶戍。

translations.literal: The Personnel Bureau once sought Teng's favor and memorialized his younger brother for a commandery with garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: The Personnel Bureau once sought Teng's favor and memorialized his younger brother for a commandery with garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 人資乖越，清河王懌抑而不奏。

translations.literal: The man's qualifications were far beyond his rank; Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi suppressed the memorial and did not submit it.
translations.idiomatic: The man's qualifications far exceeded the post; Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi suppressed the memorial.

sentences.zh: 騰以為恨，遂與領軍元叉害懌，廢靈太后于宣光殿。

translations.literal: Teng resented this and thereupon together with Army Director Yuan Cha killed Yi and deposed Empress Dowager Ling in Xuanguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Teng resented this and together with Army Director Yuan Cha killed Yi and deposed Empress Dowager Ling in Xuanguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 宮門晝夜長閉，內外斷絕。

translations.literal: The palace gates were closed day and night; inside and outside were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The palace gates were closed day and night and inside and outside were cut off.

sentences.zh: 騰自執管籥，明帝亦不得見，裁聽傳食而已。

translations.literal: Teng himself held the keys; Emperor Xiaoming also could not see the empress dowager and was allowed only to receive food passed in.
translations.idiomatic: Teng himself held the keys; even Emperor Xiaoming could not see the empress dowager and was allowed only food passed in.

sentences.zh: 太后服膳俱廢，不免饑寒。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's clothing and food were both cut off; she could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's clothing and food were cut off; she could not escape hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 又使中常侍賈粲假言侍明帝書，密令防察。

translations.literal: He also had Palace Regular Attendant Jia Can falsely claim to attend Emperor Xiaoming's writing and secretly order surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Palace Regular Attendant Jia Can falsely claim to attend Emperor Xiaoming's writing and secretly order surveillance.

sentences.zh: 叉以騰為司空，表裏擅權，共相樹置。

translations.literal: Cha made Teng Director of Works; inside and outside they monopolized power and mutually installed their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Cha made Teng Director of Works; inside and outside they monopolized power and installed each other's followers.

sentences.zh: 叉為外禦，騰為內防，迭直禁闥，共裁刑賞。

translations.literal: Cha was outer defense, Teng inner guard; they alternated duty in the forbidden gate and jointly decided punishments and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Cha was outer defense, Teng inner guard; they alternated at the forbidden gate and jointly decided punishments and rewards.

sentences.zh: 騰遂與崔光同受詔，乘步挽出入殿門。

translations.literal: Teng thereupon together with Cui Guang received edicts and rode in a sedan chair in and out of the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Teng then with Cui Guang received edicts and rode in a sedan chair through the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 四年之中，生殺之威，決於叉、騰之手。

translations.literal: Within four years the power of life and death rested in the hands of Cha and Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Within four years the power of life and death rested in the hands of Cha and Teng.

sentences.zh: 八坐九卿，旦造騰宅，參其顏色，然後方赴省府；

translations.literal: The eight excellencies and nine ministers each morning visited Teng's mansion to read his expression before then going to their ministries;
translations.idiomatic: The eight excellencies and nine ministers each morning visited Teng's mansion to read his mood before going to their ministries;

sentences.zh: 亦有曆日不能見者。

translations.literal: some went days without being received.
translations.idiomatic: some went days without being received.

sentences.zh: 公私屬請，唯在財貨，舟車之利，水陸無遺，山澤之饒，所在固護，剝削六鎮，交通底市，歲入利息以巨萬計。

translations.literal: Public and private petitions sought only wealth; profits from boats and carts on water and land left nothing untouched; riches of mountains and marshes were guarded wherever found; they stripped the Six Garrisons, traded with market agents, and yearly interest income reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private petitions sought only wealth; profits from transport on water and land left nothing untouched; riches of mountains and marshes were guarded everywhere; they stripped the Six Garrisons, traded with market agents, and yearly interest reached enormous sums.

sentences.zh: 又頗役嬪御，時有徵求，婦女器物，公然受納，逼奪鄰居，廣開室宇，天下鹹苦之。

translations.literal: They also frequently conscript palace women; whenever there were requisitions, women's goods were openly accepted; they seized neighbors' property and expanded their mansions until all under heaven suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: They also frequently conscript palace women, openly accepted women's goods, seized neighbors' property, and expanded their mansions until the realm suffered bitterly.

sentences.zh: 薨於位，中官為義息衰絰者四十餘人。

translations.literal: He died in office; more than forty eunuchs wore mourning hemp for him as adopted sons.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; more than forty eunuchs wore mourning hemp for him as adopted sons.

sentences.zh: 騰之立宅也，奉車都尉周恃為之筮，不吉，深諫止之。

translations.literal: When Teng built his mansion, Commandant of the Imperial Carriage Zhou Shi divined for him; it was inauspicious and he remonstrated deeply to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When Teng built his mansion, Commandant of the Imperial Carriage Zhou Shi divined for him, found it inauspicious, and remonstrated deeply.

sentences.zh: 騰怒而不用。

translations.literal: Teng was angry and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Teng was angry and refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 恃告人曰：「必困於三月、四月之交。」

translations.literal: Shi told others, "He is sure to be trapped at the junction of the third and fourth months.
translations.idiomatic: Shi told others, "He is sure to be trapped at the junction of the third and fourth months.

sentences.zh: 至是果死。

translations.literal: At this he indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: At this he indeed died.

sentences.zh: 査事甫成，陳屍其下。

translations.literal: The investigation had just been completed and his corpse was displayed beneath it.
translations.idiomatic: The investigation had just been completed and his corpse was displayed beneath it.

sentences.zh: 追贈太尉、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Grand Commandant and governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant and governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 葬，閹官為義服，杖絰衰縞者以百數。

translations.literal: At the burial eunuchs wore mourning; those in hemp with staff, mourning sash, and white hemp numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial eunuchs wore mourning; hundreds wore hemp with staff, mourning sash, and white hemp.

sentences.zh: 朝貴皆從，軒蓋填塞，相屬郊野。

translations.literal: Court nobles all followed; carriages and canopies filled and blocked the road, strung out across the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Court nobles all followed; carriages and canopies filled the road across the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 魏初以來，權閹存亡之盛，莫及焉。

translations.literal: Since the beginning of Wei, no powerful eunuch in life or death had ever reached such splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Since the beginning of Wei, no powerful eunuch in life or death had reached such splendor.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，追奪爵位，發其塚，散露骸骨，沒入財產。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power she stripped his title, opened his tomb, scattered the exposed bones, and confiscated his property.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power she stripped his title, opened his tomb, scattered his bones, and confiscated his property.

sentences.zh: 後騰所養一子叛入梁，太后大怒，悉徙騰余養於北裔，尋遣密使追殺之於汲郡。

translations.literal: Later one son Teng had adopted defected to Liang; the empress dowager was furious, moved all Teng's remaining adopted sons to the northern frontier, and soon sent secret agents to pursue and kill them in Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later one adopted son defected to Liang; the empress dowager was furious, moved all Teng's remaining adopted sons to the northern frontier, and soon sent secret agents to kill them in Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 賈粲，字季宣，酒泉人也。

translations.literal: Jia Can, styled Jixuan, was a man of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Can, styled Jixuan, was from Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 太和中，坐事腐刑。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was castrated for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he was castrated for an offense.

sentences.zh: 頗涉書記。

translations.literal: He was fairly versed in writing and record-keeping.
translations.idiomatic: He was fairly versed in writing and record-keeping.

sentences.zh: 與元叉、劉騰等同其謀謨，進光祿勳卿。

translations.literal: Together with Yuan Cha and Liu Teng he shared their plotting and was promoted to Director of the Household for Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Yuan Cha and Liu Teng he shared their plotting and was promoted to Director of the Household for Splendor.

sentences.zh: 專侍明帝，與叉、騰等伺帝動靜。

translations.literal: He exclusively attended Emperor Xiaoming and together with Cha, Teng, and the others watched the emperor's movements.
translations.idiomatic: He exclusively attended Emperor Xiaoming and with Cha, Teng, and others watched the emperor's movements.

sentences.zh: 右衛奚康生之謀殺叉也，靈太后、明帝同升于宣光殿，左右侍臣，俱立西階下。

translations.literal: When Right Guard Xi Kangsheng plotted to kill Cha, Empress Dowager Ling and Emperor Xiaoming ascended Xuanguang Hall together; attendant ministers all stood below the western steps.
translations.idiomatic: When Right Guard Xi Kangsheng plotted to kill Cha, Empress Dowager Ling and Emperor Xiaoming ascended Xuanguang Hall together while attendant ministers stood below the western steps.

sentences.zh: 康生既被囚執，粲紿太后曰：「侍官懷恐不安，陛下宜親安慰。」

translations.literal: Once Kangsheng was seized and bound, Can deceived the empress dowager, saying, "The attendants are fearful and uneasy; Your Majesty should personally comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Kangsheng was seized, Can deceived the empress dowager: "The attendants are fearful; Your Majesty should personally comfort them.

sentences.zh: 太后信之，適下殿，粲便扶明帝出東序，前禦顯陽，還閉太后于宣光殿。

translations.literal: The empress dowager believed him; just as she descended the hall, Can supported Emperor Xiaoming out the eastern corridor, proceeded to Xianyang in front, and again shut the empress dowager in Xuanguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager believed him; as she descended, Can supported Emperor Xiaoming out the eastern corridor, proceeded to Xianyang, and again shut the empress dowager in Xuanguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 粲既叉黨，威福亦震於京邑。

translations.literal: Can being Cha's partisan, his power and favor also shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Can being Cha's partisan, his power and favor also shook the capital.

sentences.zh: 自雲本出武威，魏太尉文和之後，遂移家屬焉。

translations.literal: He claimed descent from Wuwei and from Wei Grand Commandant Wenhe, and moved his family there.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Wuwei and Wei Grand Commandant Wenhe and moved his family there.

sentences.zh: 時武威太守韋景承粲意，以其兄緒為功曹。

translations.literal: At the time Wuwei governor Wei Jing indulged Can's wishes and made his elder brother Xu chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wuwei governor Wei Jing indulged Can's wishes and made his elder brother Xu chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 緒時年向七十。

translations.literal: Xu was then nearly seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was then nearly seventy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又以緒為西平太守。

translations.literal: Before long Xu was also made governor of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xu was also made governor of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，欲誅粲，以叉、騰黨與不一，恐驚動內外，乃止。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power she wished to execute Can, but because Cha and Teng's partisans were not all of one mind she feared alarming inside and outside and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power she wished to execute Can, but fearing alarm because Cha and Teng's partisans were not united, she stopped.

sentences.zh: 出粲為濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Can was sent out as governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Can was sent out as governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遣武衛將軍刁宣馳驛殺之。

translations.literal: Before long General of the Military Guard Diao Xuan was sent by post to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long General of the Military Guard Diao Xuan was sent by post to kill him.

sentences.zh: 楊範，字法僧，長樂廣宗人也。

translations.literal: Yang Fan, styled Faseng, was a man of Guangzong in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fan, styled Faseng, was from Guangzong in Changle.

sentences.zh: 文成時，坐事宮刑，為王琚所養，恩若父子。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wencheng's time he was castrated for an offense, was adopted by Wang Ju, and their affection was like father and son.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wencheng's time he was castrated for an offense, was adopted by Wang Ju, and their affection was like father and son.

sentences.zh: 累遷為中尹。

translations.literal: He successively rose to Central Director.
translations.idiomatic: He successively rose to Central Director.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，為中常侍、崇訓太僕，領中嘗藥典禦，賜爵華陰子，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court he was Palace Regular Attendant, Grand Master of the Household for Honored Instruction, head of the Central Bureau for Tasting Medicine and Imperial Guard, enfeoffed as Baron of Huayin, and sent out as governor of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court he was Palace Regular Attendant, Grand Master of the Household for Honored Instruction, head of the Central Bureau for Tasting Medicine and Imperial Guard, Baron of Huayin, and governor of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 中官內侍貴者，靈太后皆許其方岳，以範年長，拜跪為難，故遂其請。

translations.literal: For honored inner eunuchs Empress Dowager Ling granted them all provincial posts; because Fan was old and bowing and kneeling were difficult for him, she granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: For honored inner eunuchs Empress Dowager Ling granted provincial posts; because Fan was old and bowing and kneeling were difficult, she granted his request.

sentences.zh: 父子納貨，為御史所糾，遂廢於家。

translations.literal: Father and son accepted bribes and were impeached by the censor; they were then dismissed at home.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son accepted bribes, were impeached by the censor, and were dismissed at home.

sentences.zh: 後為崇訓太僕、華州大中正，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was again Grand Master of the Household for Honored Instruction and Chief Rectifier of Huazhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again Grand Master of the Household for Honored Instruction and Chief Rectifier of Huazhou and died.

sentences.zh: 成軌，字洪義，上谷居庸人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Gui, styled Hongyi, was a man of Juyong in Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gui, styled Hongyi, was from Juyong in Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 少以罪刑，入事宮掖。

translations.literal: In youth he was punished by castration and entered service in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Punished by castration in youth, he entered palace service.

sentences.zh: 以謹厚稱，為中謁者僕射。

translations.literal: Known for carefulness and steadiness, he became Vice Director of Central Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Known for carefulness and steadiness, he became Vice Director of Central Attendants.

sentences.zh: 孝文意有所欲，軌候容色，時有奏發，輒合帝心。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen desired something, Gui watched his expression and at times made proposals that always matched the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen desired something, Gui watched his expression and proposed what always matched the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 從駕南征，專進禦食。

translations.literal: On the southern campaign he exclusively presented imperial food.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign he exclusively presented imperial food.

sentences.zh: 時孝文不豫，常居禁中，晝夜無懈。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xiaowen was unwell and constantly stayed within the forbidden precincts, day and night without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Xiaowen was unwell and constantly stayed within the forbidden precincts, day and night without slackening.

sentences.zh: 延昌末，遷中常侍、嘗食典禦、光祿大夫，統京染都將。

translations.literal: At the end of Yanchang he was transferred to Palace Regular Attendant, Director of the Bureau for Tasting Food and Imperial Guard, Grand Master of Splendor, and commander of the Capital Dyeing Command.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yanchang he was transferred to Palace Regular Attendant, Director of the Bureau for Tasting Food and Imperial Guard, Grand Master of Splendor, and commander of the Capital Dyeing Command.

sentences.zh: 孝昌二年，以勤舊封始平縣伯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaochang, for long service he was enfeoffed as Count of Shiping County.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaochang, for long service he was enfeoffed as Count of Shiping County.

sentences.zh: 明帝所幸潘嬪以軌為假父，頗為中官之所敬憚。

translations.literal: Consort Pan, favored by Emperor Xiaoming, took Gui as her nominal father; he was rather feared by the palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Pan, favored by Emperor Xiaoming, took Gui as her nominal father; palace eunuchs rather feared him.

sentences.zh: 後進爵為侯，卒于衛將軍，贈雍州刺史，諡曰孝惠。

translations.literal: Later he advanced to marquis, died as General of the Guard, was posthumously made governor of Yongzhou, and posthumously named Xiaohui.
translations.idiomatic: He later advanced to marquis, died as General of the Guard, and was posthumously made governor of Yongzhou with the posthumous name Xiaohui.

sentences.zh: 王溫，字桃湯，趙郡欒城人也。

translations.literal: Wang Wen, styled Taotang, was a man of Luancheng in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen, styled Taotang, was from Luancheng in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父冀，高邑令，坐事誅，溫與兄繼叔俱充宦者，稍遷中嘗食典禦、中給事，加左中郎將。

translations.literal: His father Ji was magistrate of Gaoyi; executed for an offense, Wen and his elder brother Jishu both entered service as eunuchs and gradually rose to Director of the Bureau for Tasting Food and Imperial Guard, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace, and Left Commandant of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji was magistrate of Gaoyi; executed for an offense, Wen and his elder brother Jishu both became eunuchs and rose to Director of the Bureau for Tasting Food and Imperial Guard, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace, and Left Commandant of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 宣武之崩，群官迎明帝于東宮，溫於臥中起明帝，與保母扶抱明帝，入踐帝位。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu died the officials welcomed Emperor Xiaoming at the Eastern Palace; Wen roused Xiaoming from bed and together with the wet nurse supported and carried him to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died officials welcomed Emperor Xiaoming at the Eastern Palace; Wen roused Xiaoming from bed and with the wet nurse supported him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 高陽王雍既居塚宰，慮中人朋黨，出為巨鹿太守。

translations.literal: Prince of Gaoyang Yong having become chief minister, fearing factions among the inner staff, sent Wen out as governor of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Gaoyang Yong, now chief minister, fearing inner factions, sent Wen out as governor of Julu.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，徵為中常侍，賜爵欒城伯。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court he was recalled as Palace Regular Attendant and enfeoffed as Count of Luancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court he was recalled as Palace Regular Attendant and enfeoffed as Count of Luancheng.

sentences.zh: 累遷左光祿大夫、光祿勳卿、侍中，進封欒城縣侯。

translations.literal: He successively rose to Left Grand Master of Splendor, Director of the Household for Splendor, Palace Attendant, and was advanced to Marquis of Luancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Grand Master of Splendor, Director of the Household for Splendor, Palace Attendant, and Marquis of Luancheng County.

sentences.zh: 溫自陳本陽平武陽人，改封武陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Wen stated that he was originally from Wuyang in Yangping and changed his enfeoffment to Marquis of Wuyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Wen stated he was originally from Wuyang in Yangping and changed his enfeoffment to Marquis of Wuyang County.

sentences.zh: 建義初，于河陰遇害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 孟欒，字龍兒，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Meng Luan, styled Long'er, was from an unknown place.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Luan, styled Long'er, was from an unknown place.

sentences.zh: 坐事為閹人。

translations.literal: For an offense he became a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he became a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，為左中郎將、給事中。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court he was Left Commandant of the Central Guard and Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court he was Left Commandant of the Central Guard and Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 素被病，面常黯黑。

translations.literal: He had long suffered illness and his face was constantly dark.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been ill and his face was constantly dark.

sentences.zh: 于九龍殿下暴疾，歸家，甚夜亡。

translations.literal: Below Jiulong Hall he suddenly fell ill, returned home, and died that very night.
translations.idiomatic: Below Jiulong Hall he suddenly fell ill, returned home, and died that very night.

sentences.zh: 欒初出，靈太后聞之曰：「欒必不濟，我為之憂。」

translations.literal: When Luan first went out Empress Dowager Ling heard of it and said, "Luan surely will not recover; I am worried for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan first went out Empress Dowager Ling said, "Luan surely will not recover; I am worried for him.

sentences.zh: 乃奏其死，為之下淚曰：「其事我如此，不見我一日忻樂時也。」

translations.literal: She then reported his death and wept for him, saying, "He served me like this, yet I never saw him happy for a single day."
translations.idiomatic: She then reported his death and wept: "He served me like this, yet I never saw him happy for a single day."

sentences.zh: 賜帛三百疋、黃絹一十疋，以供喪用。

translations.literal: She gave three hundred bolts of silk and ten bolts of yellow silk for funeral use.
translations.idiomatic: She gave three hundred bolts of silk and ten bolts of yellow silk for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 七日，靈太后為設二百僧齋。

translations.literal: On the seventh day Empress Dowager Ling held a vegetarian feast for two hundred monks.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day Empress Dowager Ling held a vegetarian feast for two hundred monks.

sentences.zh: 平季，字幼穆，燕國薊人也。

translations.literal: Ping Ji, styled Youmu, was a man of Ji in Yan Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Ji, styled Youmu, was from Ji in Yan Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 坐事腐刑。

translations.literal: He was castrated for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was castrated for an offense.

sentences.zh: 累遷新興太守。

translations.literal: He successively rose to governor of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: He successively rose to governor of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，與爾硃榮等議立莊帝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaoming died he discussed with Erzhu Rong and others installing Emperor Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaoming died he discussed with Erzhu Rong and others installing Emperor Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，超拜肆州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was enthroned he was specially promoted to governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang was enthroned he was specially promoted to governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋除中侍中。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Attendant of the Central Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Attendant of the Central Palace.

sentences.zh: 以參謀勳，封元城縣侯。

translations.literal: For merit in planning he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in planning he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuancheng County.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，加驃騎大將軍，卒。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was made General of Agile Cavalry and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he was made General of Agile Cavalry and died.

sentences.zh: 封津，字醜漢，勃海蓚人也。

translations.literal: Feng Jin, styled Chouhan, was a man of Tiao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jin, styled Chouhan, was from Tiao in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 父令德，娶常寶女。

translations.literal: His father Lingde married Chang Bao's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingde married Chang Bao's daughter.

sentences.zh: 寶伏誅，令德以連坐伏法。

translations.literal: When Bao was executed Lingde was executed by association.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao was executed Lingde was executed by association.

sentences.zh: 津受刑，給事宮掖。

translations.literal: Jin was punished and entered service in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was punished and entered palace service.

sentences.zh: 累遷奉車都尉、中給事中。

translations.literal: He successively rose to Commandant of the Imperial Carriage and Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Commandant of the Imperial Carriage and Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 靈太后令津侍明帝書，遷常山太守。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling had Jin attend Emperor Xiaoming's writing and transferred him to governor of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling had Jin attend Emperor Xiaoming's writing and transferred him to governor of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 津少長宮闈，給事左右，善候時情，號為機悟。

translations.literal: Jin grew up in the palace precincts serving at the emperor's side; skilled at reading the times, he was called clever and quick-witted.
translations.idiomatic: Jin grew up in the palace serving at the emperor's side; skilled at reading the times, he was called clever and quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 天平初，除開府儀同三司、懷州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping he was made Commissioner with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies and governor of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was made Commissioner with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies and governor of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 元象初，復為中侍中、大長秋卿，仍開府儀同。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he was again Attendant of the Central Palace and Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service, still Commissioner with the Same Powers.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang he was again Attendant of the Central Palace and Grand Director of the Palace Domestic Service, still Commissioner with the Same Powers.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司徒、冀州刺史，諡曰孝惠。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Director of Works and governor of Jizhou and posthumously named Xiaohui.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Director of Works and governor of Jizhou with the posthumous name Xiaohui.

sentences.zh: 劉思逸，平原人也。

translations.literal: Liu Siyi was a man of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Siyi was from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 以罪，少充腐刑。

translations.literal: For a crime he underwent castration in youth.
translations.idiomatic: For a crime he underwent castration in youth.

sentences.zh: 初為小史，累遷中侍中。

translations.literal: At first he was a petty clerk and successively rose to Attendant of the Central Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At first a petty clerk, he rose to Attendant of the Central Palace.

sentences.zh: 武定中，與元瑾等謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he plotted rebellion together with Yuan Jin and others and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he plotted rebellion with Yuan Jin and others and was executed.

sentences.zh: 又有張景嵩、毛暢者，咸以閽寺在明帝左右。

translations.literal: There were also Zhang Jingsong and Mao Chang, both gatekeeper-eunuchs at Emperor Xiaoming's side.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Zhang Jingsong and Mao Chang, both gatekeeper-eunuchs at Emperor Xiaoming's side.

sentences.zh: 靈太后亦密仗之通傳意計於明帝。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling also secretly relied on them to convey plans to Emperor Xiaoming.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling also secretly relied on them to convey plans to Emperor Xiaoming.

sentences.zh: 元叉之出，景嵩、暢頗有力焉。

translations.literal: In Cha's removal Jingsong and Chang were rather influential.
translations.idiomatic: In Cha's removal Jingsong and Chang were rather influential.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，以妹故，未即戮叉。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, because of her sister she did not immediately execute Cha.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, because of her sister she did not immediately execute Cha.

sentences.zh: 時內外喧喧，元叉還欲入知政事。

translations.literal: At the time inside and outside were in uproar; Yuan Cha still wished to re-enter and manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside were in uproar; Yuan Cha still wished to re-enter and manage state affairs.

sentences.zh: 暢等恐禍及己，乃啟明帝，欲詔右衛將軍楊津密往殺叉。

translations.literal: Chang and the others feared disaster would reach them and reported to Emperor Xiaoming, wishing to edict Right Guard General Yang Jin to go secretly and kill Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Chang and the others feared for themselves and reported to Emperor Xiaoming, wishing to edict Right Guard General Yang Jin to go secretly and kill Cha.

sentences.zh: 詔書已成，未及出外，叉妻知之，告太后：「景嵩、暢與清河王息<召己>欲廢太后。」

translations.literal: The edict was already written but not yet sent out when Cha's wife learned of it and told the empress dowager, "Jingsong and Chang together with a son of the Prince of Qinghe, Zhaoji, wish to depose the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was written but not yet sent when Cha's wife told the empress dowager, "Jingsong and Chang together with a son of the Prince of Qinghe, Zhaoji, wish to depose the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后信之，責暢。

translations.literal: The empress dowager believed it and rebuked Chang.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager believed it and rebuked Chang.

sentences.zh: 暢出詔草以呈太后。

translations.literal: Chang produced the draft edict and presented it to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Chang produced the draft edict and presented it to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后讀之，知無廢己狀，意小解。

translations.literal: The empress dowager read it, knew there was no intent to depose her, and her anger slightly eased.
translations.idiomatic: She read it, saw there was no intent to depose her, and her anger slightly eased.

sentences.zh: 然叉妻構之不已，出暢為頓丘太守，景嵩為魯郡太守。

translations.literal: Yet Cha's wife kept framing them; Chang was sent out as governor of Dunqiu and Jingsong as governor of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Cha's wife kept framing them; Chang was sent out as governor of Dunqiu and Jingsong as governor of Lu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋令捕殺暢。

translations.literal: Before long an order was issued to capture and kill Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an order was issued to capture and kill Chang.

sentences.zh: 景嵩，孝靜時位至中侍中，坐事死。

translations.literal: Jingsong in Emperor Xiaojing's time rose to Attendant of the Central Palace and was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsong in Emperor Xiaojing's time rose to Attendant of the Central Palace and was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 郭秀，范陽涿人也。

translations.literal: Guo Xiu was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiu was from Zhuo in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 事齊神武，稍遷行台右丞，封壽陽伯。

translations.literal: He served Gao Huan and gradually rose to Right Vice Director of the Mobile Headquarters and was enfeoffed as Count of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served Gao Huan and gradually rose to Right Vice Director of the Mobile Headquarters and was enfeoffed as Count of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 親寵日隆，多受賂遺，進退人物。

translations.literal: Favor grew daily; he accepted many bribes and controlled the advancement and dismissal of men.
translations.idiomatic: Favor grew daily; he accepted many bribes and controlled advancement and dismissal.

sentences.zh: 張伯德、祁仲彥、張華原之徒，皆深相附會。

translations.literal: Zhang Bode, Qi Zhongyan, Zhang Huayuan, and the like all attached themselves deeply to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bode, Qi Zhongyan, Zhang Huayuan, and the like all attached themselves deeply to him.

sentences.zh: 秀疾，神武親視之，問所欲官，乃啟為七兵尚書，除書未至而卒。

translations.literal: When Xiu fell ill Gao Huan personally visited him, asked what office he desired, and he requested to be Minister of the Seven Arms; the appointment letter had not arrived when he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu fell ill Gao Huan personally visited, asked what office he desired, and he requested Minister of the Seven Arms; the appointment letter had not arrived when he died.

sentences.zh: 家無成人子弟，神武自至其宅，親使錄知其家資粟帛多少，然後去。

translations.literal: The household had no adult sons or younger brothers; Gao Huan personally came to the mansion and had the household grain and silk counted before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: The household had no adult sons; Gao Huan personally came to the mansion, had grain and silk counted, and then left.

sentences.zh: 贈儀同三司、恆州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Commissioner with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies and governor of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Commissioner with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies and governor of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 命其子孝義與太原公以下同學讀書。

translations.literal: He ordered his son Xiaoyi to study reading together with the sons of the Prince of Taiyuan and those below.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his son Xiaoyi to study together with the sons of the Prince of Taiyuan and those below.

sentences.zh: 初，秀忌嫉楊愔，誑脅令其逃亡。

translations.literal: At first Xiu envied Yang Yin and coerced and threatened him into flight.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xiu envied Yang Yin and coerced him into flight.

sentences.zh: 秀死後，愔還，神武追忿秀，即日斥遣孝義，終身不齒。

translations.literal: After Xiu died Yin returned; Gao Huan, recalling anger at Xiu, that very day expelled Xiaoyi and never admitted him to company for life.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu died Yin returned; Gao Huan, recalling anger at Xiu, that very day expelled Xiaoyi and never admitted him for life.

sentences.zh: 和士開，字彥通，清都臨漳人也。

translations.literal: He Shikai, styled Yantong, was a man of Linzhang in Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai, styled Yantong, was from Linzhang in Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 其先西域商胡，本姓素和氏。

translations.literal: His ancestors were Western Region merchant Hu; the original surname was Suhe.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were Western Region merchant Hu; the original surname was Suhe.

sentences.zh: 父安，恭敏善事人，稍遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: His father An was respectful, diligent, and skilled at serving people and gradually rose to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: His father An was respectful, diligent, skilled at serving people, and gradually rose to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 魏靜帝嘗夜與朝賢講集，命安看斗柄所指。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing of Wei once at night gathered with court worthies for discussion and ordered An to observe where the Dipper's handle pointed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing of Wei once gathered court worthies at night for discussion and ordered An to observe where the Dipper's handle pointed.

sentences.zh: 安曰：「臣不識北斗。」

translations.literal: An said, "Your servant does not know the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: An said, "Your servant does not know the Northern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 齊神武聞之，以為淳直，由是啟除給事黃門侍郎，位儀州刺史。

translations.literal: Gao Huan heard of this and considered it plain and straight; for this he was recommended and removed to Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate and appointed governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan heard of this and considered it plain and straight; for this An was recommended as Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate and governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 士開貴，贈司空公、尚書左僕射、冀州刺史，諡文貞公。

translations.literal: When Shikai became honored, An was posthumously made Duke of Works, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, governor of Jizhou, and posthumously named Duke Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Shikai became honored, An was posthumously made Duke of Works, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, governor of Jizhou, with the posthumous name Duke Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 士開幼而聰慧，選為國子學生，解悟捷疾，為同業所尚。

translations.literal: Shikai from youth was intelligent; selected as an Imperial University student, quick in understanding, he was admired by his fellows.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai from youth was intelligent; selected as an Imperial University student, quick in understanding, he was admired by his fellows.

sentences.zh: 天保初，武成封長廣王，辟士開開府行參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, when Wucheng was enfeoffed as Prince of Changgang he recruited Shikai as acting staff officer of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao, when Wucheng was enfeoffed as Prince of Changgang he recruited Shikai as acting staff officer of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 武成好握槊，士開善此戲，由是遂有斯舉。

translations.literal: Wucheng loved polo; Shikai was skilled at this game, and for this he gained the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Wucheng loved polo; Shikai was skilled at the game and gained the appointment.

sentences.zh: 加以傾巧便僻，又能彈胡琵琶，因致親寵。

translations.literal: Added to this he was artful, clever, and obsequious and could also play the foreign pipa; thus he won intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: Artful, clever, and obsequious, and able to play the foreign pipa, he won intimate favor.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂王曰：「殿下非天人也，是天帝也。」

translations.literal: He once told the prince, "Your Highness is not a man of heaven but a heavenly emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He once told the prince, "Your Highness is not a man of heaven but a heavenly emperor.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「卿非世人也，是世神也。」

translations.literal: The prince said, "You are not a man of the world but a worldly god."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "You are not a man of the world but a worldly god."

sentences.zh: 其深相愛重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the depth of their mutual affection and esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of their mutual affection and esteem.

sentences.zh: 文宣知其輕薄，不欲令王與小人相親善，責其戲狎過度，徙之馬城。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan knew he was frivolous and did not wish the prince to be close to such petty men; he rebuked him for excessive playful intimacy and exiled him to Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan knew he was frivolous and did not wish the prince close to petty men; rebuking excessive playful intimacy, he exiled Shikai to Macheng.

sentences.zh: 乾明元年，孝昭誅楊愔等，敕追還，長廣王請之也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ganming, when Emperor Xiaozhao executed Yang Yin and others, an edict recalled him—Prince of Changgang had requested it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ganming, when Emperor Xiaozhao executed Yang Yin and others, an edict recalled him at Prince of Changgang's request.

sentences.zh: 武成即位，累遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Wucheng was enthroned he successively rose to Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Wucheng was enthroned he successively rose to Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 侍中高元海、黃門郎高乾和及御史中丞畢義雲等疾之，將言其事。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Gao Yuanhai, Supervising Secretary Gao Ganhe, and Censor-in-Chief Bi Yiyun and others resented him and were about to report the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Gao Yuanhai, Supervising Secretary Gao Ganhe, and Censor-in-Chief Bi Yiyun resented him and were about to report the matter.

sentences.zh: 士開乃奏元海等交結朋黨，欲擅威福。

translations.literal: Shikai thereupon memorialized that Yuanhai and the others formed cliques and sought to monopolize authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai memorialized that Yuanhai and the others formed cliques and sought to monopolize authority and favor.

sentences.zh: 乾和因被疏斥，義雲反納貨於士開，除兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Ganhe was therefore distanced and dismissed; Yiyun instead gave bribes to Shikai and was made governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ganhe was distanced and dismissed; Yiyun instead bribed Shikai and was made governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 士開初封定州真定縣子，尋進為伯。

translations.literal: Shikai was at first enfeoffed as Baron of Zhending County in Dingzhou and soon advanced to count.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai was first enfeoffed as Baron of Zhending County in Dingzhou and soon advanced to count.

sentences.zh: 天統元年，加儀同三司，尋除侍中，加開府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiantong he was made Commissioner with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies, soon removed to Palace Attendant and given an open headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiantong he was made Commissioner with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies, soon Palace Attendant with an open headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及遭母劉氏憂，帝聞而悲惋，遣武衛將軍侯呂芬詣宅，晝夜扶侍，並節哀止哭。

translations.literal: When he suffered mourning for his mother Lady Liu the emperor heard and grieved; he sent General of the Military Guard Hou Lüfen to the mansion to attend day and night and restrain grief and stop weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When he mourned his mother Lady Liu the emperor grieved; he sent General of the Military Guard Hou Lüfen to attend day and night and restrain grief.

sentences.zh: 又遣侍中韓寶業齎手敕慰諭云：「朕之與卿，本同心腹，今懷抱痛割，與卿無異。

translations.literal: He also sent Palace Attendant Han Baoye bearing a handwritten edict of consolation, saying, "I and you were originally of one heart and belly; now the pain cuts my breast no differently from yours.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Palace Attendant Han Baoye with a handwritten edict: "I and you were originally of one heart; now the pain cuts my breast no differently from yours.

sentences.zh: 當深思至理，以自開慰。」

translations.literal: You should deeply ponder ultimate principle to open and comfort yourself.
translations.idiomatic: You should deeply ponder ultimate principle to comfort yourself.

sentences.zh: 成服後，呂芬等始還。

translations.literal: After the mourning garments were completed Lüfen and the others only then returned.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning garments were completed Lüfen and the others only then returned.

sentences.zh: 其日，遣韓寶業以犢車迎士開入內，帝親握手，下泣曉諭，然後遣還。

translations.literal: That day Han Baoye was sent with a calf cart to welcome Shikai within; the emperor personally took his hand, wept and admonished him, and then sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: That day Han Baoye was sent with a calf cart to welcome Shikai in; the emperor took his hand, wept and admonished him, then sent him back.

sentences.zh: 駕幸晉陽，給假，聽過七日續發，其見重如此。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Jinyang he was granted leave and allowed to set out after the seventh day; such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage visited Jinyang he was granted leave to set out after the seventh day; such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 並諸弟四人，並起復本官。

translations.literal: All four of his younger brothers likewise resumed their former offices without waiting out mourning.
translations.idiomatic: All four younger brothers likewise resumed their former offices without waiting out mourning.

sentences.zh: 四年，再遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was again transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was again transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 帝先患氣疾，因飲酒輒大發動，士開每諫不從。

translations.literal: The emperor had earlier suffered from qi illness; because of drinking wine it would greatly flare up; Shikai often remonstrated but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had earlier suffered qi illness; drinking made it flare greatly; Shikai often remonstrated but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 後屬帝氣疾發，又欲飲酒，士開淚下噓欷而不能言。

translations.literal: Later when the emperor's qi illness flared and he again wished to drink wine, Shikai wept and sighed but could not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Later when the emperor's qi illness flared and he again wished to drink, Shikai wept and sighed but could not speak.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿此是不言之諫。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your silence is remonstrance without words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your silence is remonstrance without words.

sentences.zh: 因不飲酒。

translations.literal: Therefore he did not drink wine.
translations.idiomatic: And so he refrained from drinking.

sentences.zh: 及冬，公主出降段氏，帝幸平原王第，始飲酒焉。

translations.literal: When winter came, the princess was given in marriage to the Duan clan, and the emperor visited the residence of the Prince of Pingyuan—only then did he begin to drink wine.
translations.idiomatic: By winter, when the princess was married into the Duan family, the emperor visited the Prince of Pingyuan's mansion and resumed drinking.

sentences.zh: 又除尚書左僕射，仍兼侍中。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and still held the concurrent post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat while retaining his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武成外朝視事，或在內宴賞，須臾之間，不得不與士開相見。

translations.literal: When Wucheng conducted state business in the outer court or feasted and rewarded people within, in no time at all he had to see Shikai.
translations.idiomatic: Whether Wucheng was holding court in the outer hall or feasting within the palace, within moments he would summon Shikai to his side.

sentences.zh: 或累月不歸，一日數入；

translations.literal: Sometimes he would not return home for months on end, yet enter the palace several times in a single day;
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he stayed away from home for months, yet entered the palace several times in a day;

sentences.zh: 或放還之後，俄頃即追，未至之間，連騎催喚。

translations.literal: or after being sent home, within a moment he would be summoned back—before he even arrived, riders in succession urged and called him.
translations.idiomatic: or after being sent home, he would be recalled almost immediately, with messenger riders urging him on before he could even get there.

sentences.zh: 奸諂日至，寵愛彌隆，前後賞賜，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Flattery and sycophancy increased day by day, favor grew ever more splendid, and the rewards bestowed before and after could not be fully reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery poured in daily, his favor grew ever greater, and the rewards lavished on him were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 言辭容止，極諸鄙褻，以夜繼晝，無復君臣之禮。

translations.literal: In speech and bearing he reached the extreme of vulgarity and intimacy, making night follow upon day, with no remaining propriety between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: His speech and conduct were utterly vulgar and indecent; day blurred into night, and all propriety between sovereign and subject vanished.

sentences.zh: 至說武成云：「自古帝王，盡為灰土，堯舜、桀紂，竟復何異？

translations.literal: He even said to Wucheng: "Since antiquity, emperors and kings have all turned to ash and dust—what difference is there in the end between Yao and Shun and Jie and Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: He even told Wucheng, "From ancient times every emperor and king has ended as dust and ashes—what difference is there, in the end, between Yao and Shun and Jie and Zhou?

sentences.zh: 陛下宜及少壯，恣意作樂，從橫行之，即是一日快活敵千年。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should, while still young and strong, indulge in pleasure at will and do as you please—one day of such happiness rivals a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should enjoy yourself to the full while you are still young and vigorous—one day of such pleasure is worth a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 國事分付大臣，何慮不辦？

translations.literal: Entrust state affairs to great ministers—why worry that they will not be handled?
translations.idiomatic: Leave state affairs to your senior ministers—why worry that anything will go undone?

sentences.zh: 無為自勤約也。」

translations.literal: Do not needlessly impose austerity on yourself.
translations.idiomatic: There is no need to burden yourself with thrift and self-restraint.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，於是委趙彥深掌官爵，元文遙掌財用，唐邕掌外兵，白建掌騎兵，馮子琮、胡長粲掌東宮。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, and thereupon entrusted Zhao Yanshen with official ranks, Yuan Wenyao with finances, Tang Yong with external military affairs, Bai Jian with cavalry, and Feng Zicong and Hu Changcan with the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted. He put Zhao Yanshen in charge of appointments, Yuan Wenyao in charge of finances, Tang Yong in charge of external military affairs, Bai Jian in charge of cavalry, and Feng Zicong and Hu Changcan in charge of the crown prince's palace.

sentences.zh: 帝三四日乃一坐朝，書數字而已，略無言，須臾罷入。

translations.literal: The emperor held court only once every three or four days, writing a few characters and nothing more, scarcely speaking, and withdrew after a brief while.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held court only once every three or four days, writing a few characters and saying almost nothing before retiring within moments.

sentences.zh: 及帝寢疾于乾壽殿，士開入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill and lay in Qianshou Hall, Shikai entered to attend him with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill in Qianshou Hall, Shikai entered to nurse him and administer medicine.

sentences.zh: 帝謂士開有伊、霍之才，殷勤屬以後事，臨崩握其手曰：「勿負我也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said Shikai had the talent of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, earnestly entrusted him with affairs after death, and on his deathbed grasped his hand, saying, "Do not fail me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declared that Shikai possessed the talent of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, earnestly entrusted the future to him, and on his deathbed clasped his hand and said, "Do not betray me.

sentences.zh: 仍絕於士開之手。

translations.literal: He then breathed his last in Shikai's hands.
translations.idiomatic: He died with Shikai's hand still in his.

sentences.zh: 後主以武成顧托，深委任之。

translations.literal: The Later Ruler, because of Wucheng's deathbed entrustment, deeply relied on and entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wucheng had entrusted him on his deathbed, the Later Ruler placed deep trust in him.

sentences.zh: 又先得幸于胡太后，是以彌見親密。

translations.literal: Moreover, having first won favor with Empress Dowager Hu, he was thus all the more seen as intimate.
translations.idiomatic: He had also won Empress Dowager Hu's favor earlier, which made their intimacy all the more pronounced.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王睿與婁定遠、元文遙等謀出士開，仍引任城、馮翊二王及段韶、安吐根共為計策。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui, together with Lou Dingyuan, Yuan Wenyao, and others, plotted to remove Shikai, and also enlisted the Princes of Rencheng and Fenyang, along with Duan Shao and An Tugen, to devise a plan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery, together with Lou Dingyuan, Yuan Wenyao, and others, plotted to oust Shikai. They also brought in the Princes of Rencheng and Fenyang, along with Duan Shao and An Tugen, to join in the plan.

sentences.zh: 屬太后觴朝貴於前殿，睿面陳士開罪失云：「士開，先帝弄臣，城狐社鼠，受納貨賄，穢亂宮掖。

translations.literal: It happened that the empress dowager was hosting the court nobles for wine in the front hall, and Rui openly stated Shikai's crimes and faults, saying, "Shikai was the late emperor's plaything of a minister—a rat in the wall and fox at the altar—accepting bribes and defiling the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager was hosting the court nobility for wine in the front hall, Rui openly denounced Shikai's crimes. "Shikai was the late emperor's favorite plaything—a creature of the palace walls who took bribes and defiled the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 臣等義無杜口，冒以死陳。」

translations.literal: We, your subjects, in righteousness cannot keep silent—we risk death to speak plainly.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot in conscience remain silent—we speak even at the risk of our lives.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「先帝在時，王等何意不道？

translations.literal: The empress dowager said, "When the late emperor was alive, why did you, princes, not speak of this?
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "When the late emperor was alive, why did none of you say a word?

sentences.zh: 今日欲欺孤寡邪！

translations.literal: Do you now wish to deceive the widow and orphan?
translations.idiomatic: Do you mean to take advantage of a widow and her young son?

sentences.zh: 但飲酒，勿多言。」

translations.literal: Only drink your wine—say no more."
translations.idiomatic: Drink your wine and say no more."

sentences.zh: 睿詞色愈厲。

translations.literal: Rui's words and expression grew ever harsher.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's tone and expression grew sharper still.

sentences.zh: 安吐根繼進曰：「臣本商胡，得在諸貴行末，既受厚恩，豈敢惜死？

translations.literal: An Tugen then stepped forward and said, "I am originally a Sogdian merchant—fortunate to stand at the end of the ranks of the nobles. Having received great favor, how could I spare my life?
translations.idiomatic: An Tugen stepped forward next. "I am but a Sogdian merchant who happened to stand among the nobility. Having received such great favor, how could I hold back my life?

sentences.zh: 不出士開，朝野不定。」

translations.literal: If Shikai is not removed, court and countryside will know no stability.
translations.idiomatic: Unless Shikai is removed, neither court nor countryside will be stable.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「別日論之，王等且散。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said, "We shall discuss this another day—you princes may disperse for now."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "We will discuss this another day. For now, disperse."

sentences.zh: 睿等或投冠於地，或拂衣而起，言詞咆哱，無所不至。

translations.literal: Rui and the others either threw their caps to the ground or rose with a sweep of their robes, roaring in speech to every extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Some of Rui's party flung their caps to the floor; others stormed out. Their shouts and rage knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 明日，睿等復于雲龍門令文遙入奏，三反，太后不聽。

translations.literal: The next day, Rui and the others again had Wenyao enter to memorialize at the Yunlong Gate; three times they tried, and the empress dowager would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Rui and his allies again had Wenyao submit a memorial at the Yunlong Gate. Three times they tried; the empress dowager refused to hear them.

sentences.zh: 段韶呼胡長粲傳言于太后。

translations.literal: Duan Shao summoned Hu Changcan to convey a message to the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Shao sent Hu Changcan to relay a message to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 曰：「梓宮在殯，事太匆速，猶欲王等更思量。」

translations.literal: He said, "The late emperor's coffin is still in mourning rites—the matter is too hasty; we still wish you princes to reconsider.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The late emperor's coffin has not yet been laid to rest—the matter is too rushed. We ask you princes to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王等遂並拜謝。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao Commandery and the others thereupon all bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui and the others thereupon bowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 長粲復命，太后謂曰：「成妹母子家計者，兄之力也。」

translations.literal: Changcan reported back, and the empress dowager said to him, "As for the household affairs of my brother's daughter and her son, it is through your brother's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: When Changcan reported back, the empress dowager told him, "The household affairs of my brother's daughter and her son are owed to your brother's efforts.

sentences.zh: 厚賜睿等而罷之。

translations.literal: She richly rewarded Rui and the others and dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: She lavished rewards on Rui and his allies and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 太后及後主召問士開，士開曰：「先帝群臣中，待臣最重。

translations.literal: The empress dowager and the Later Ruler summoned Shikai to question him, and Shikai said, "Among the late emperor's ministers, he treated me with the greatest weight.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager and the Later Ruler summoned Shikai for questioning. He said, "Of all the late emperor's ministers, I was the one he favored most.

sentences.zh: 陛下諒陰始爾，大臣皆有覬覦，今若出臣，正是翦陛下羽翼。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's mourning has only just begun, and the great ministers all harbor covetous designs; if you remove me now, you will precisely be clipping Your Majesty's wings.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's mourning has only just begun, and the senior ministers all harbor designs of their own. If you remove me now, you will be cutting away your own wings.

sentences.zh: 宜謂睿等，雲文遙與臣同是任用，豈得一去一留，並可以為州。

translations.literal: You should tell Rui and the others that Wenyao and I are both in active employment—how can one be sent away and one kept? Both can be made provincial governors.
translations.idiomatic: Tell Rui and the others that Wenyao and I are both in active service—how can one be dismissed and the other kept? Send us both to govern provinces.

sentences.zh: 且依舊出納，待過山陵，然後發遣。

translations.literal: Moreover, let me continue handling receipts and disbursements as before; wait until after the imperial tomb rites, and then send us off.
translations.idiomatic: Let me continue my duties at court for now, and send us away only after the tomb rites are complete.

sentences.zh: 睿等謂臣真出，心必喜之。」

translations.literal: Rui and the others, believing Shikai was truly being sent out, would surely be delighted at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and his allies, believing Shikai was truly being removed, would surely rejoice.

sentences.zh: 後主及太后告睿等，如其言，以士開為兗州刺史，文遙為西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: The Later Ruler and the empress dowager told Rui and the others as he advised, appointing Shikai Governor of Yan Province and Wenyao Governor of Western Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Ruler and the empress dowager told Rui and the others exactly what Shikai had advised, appointing Shikai Governor of Yan Province and Wenyao Governor of Western Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 山陵畢，睿等促士開就路。

translations.literal: When the tomb rites were finished, Rui and the others pressed Shikai to set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Once the tomb rites were complete, Rui and his allies pressed Shikai to depart.

sentences.zh: 士開載美女珠簾及諸寶玩以詣婁定遠，謝曰：「諸貴欲殺士開，蒙王特賜性命，用作方伯。

translations.literal: Shikai loaded beautiful women, pearl curtains, and various treasures and curiosities and went to Lou Dingyuan, saying in thanks, "The nobles wished to kill Shikai; I owe my life to Your Highness, who granted me appointment as a regional governor.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai loaded up beautiful women, pearl curtains, and all manner of treasures and went to Lou Dingyuan. "The nobles wanted me dead," he said gratefully. "You alone spared my life and made me a regional governor.

sentences.zh: 今欲奉別，且送二女子、一珠簾。」

translations.literal: Now, wishing to take leave, I present two women and one pearl curtain.
translations.idiomatic: As I take my leave, I bring you two women and a pearl curtain.

sentences.zh: 定遠大喜，謂士開曰：「欲還入不？」

translations.literal: Dingyuan was greatly pleased and said to Shikai, "Do you wish to go back inside?"
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan was delighted and asked Shikai, "Do you want to go back inside?"

sentences.zh: 士開曰：「在內久，常不自安，不願更人。」

translations.literal: Shikai said, "Having been inside so long, I am constantly ill at ease—I do not wish to enter again."
translations.idiomatic: Shikai said, "I have been inside so long that I never feel at ease there. I have no wish to go back."

sentences.zh: 定遠信之，送至門。

translations.literal: Dingyuan believed him and escorted him to the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan believed him and saw him to the gate.

sentences.zh: 士開曰：「今日遠出，願一辭觀二宮。」

translations.literal: Shikai said, "Today, going far away, I wish once to take leave of the two palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai said, "Since I am leaving today, I wish to bid farewell to the two palaces.

sentences.zh: 定遠許之。

translations.literal: Dingyuan permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 由是得見後主及太后，進說曰：「先帝一旦登遐，臣愧不能自死。

translations.literal: By this means he was able to see the Later Ruler and the empress dowager, and he advanced his plea, saying, "The late emperor suddenly ascended to the far realm—I am ashamed that I could not die with him.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he gained audience with the Later Ruler and the empress dowager and pleaded, "When the late emperor suddenly passed away, I was ashamed that I could not die with him.

sentences.zh: 觀朝貴意勢，欲以陛下為乾明。

translations.literal: Looking at the intent and power of the court nobles, they wish to make Your Majesty into a Qianming.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by the intent and power of the court nobles, they mean to reduce Your Majesty to another Qianming.

sentences.zh: 臣出之後，必有大變，復何面目見先帝於地下！」

translations.literal: After I go out, there will surely be great upheaval—how could I again show my face to the late emperor underground!
translations.idiomatic: Once I am gone, there will surely be a great upheaval. How could I face the late emperor in the grave!

sentences.zh: 因慟哭。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into bitter weeping.

sentences.zh: 後主及太后皆泣，問計將安出。

translations.literal: The Later Ruler and the empress dowager both wept and asked where a plan might be found.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Ruler and the empress dowager wept as well and asked what could be done.

sentences.zh: 士開曰：「臣已得入，復何所慮？

translations.literal: Shikai said, "I have already gotten back inside—what is there still to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: Shikai said, "I am already back inside—what is there left to fear?

sentences.zh: 正須數行詔書耳。」

translations.literal: It needs only a few lines of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: A few edicts will suffice.

sentences.zh: 於是詔定遠為青州刺史；

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict appointed Dingyuan Governor of Qing Province;
translations.idiomatic: Edicts were issued appointing Dingyuan Governor of Qing Province;

sentences.zh: 責趙郡王睿以不臣，召入殺之；

translations.literal: rebuked Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui for disloyalty, summoned him in, and killed him;
translations.idiomatic: condemning Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery for disloyalty, summoning him in and executing him;

sentences.zh: 復除士開侍中、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: and restored Shikai to Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: and restoring Shikai as Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 定遠歸士開所遺，加以餘珍賂之。

translations.literal: Dingyuan returned what Shikai had given him and added further precious gifts to bribe him.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan returned Shikai's gifts and added further treasures as a bribe.

sentences.zh: 武平元年，封淮陽王，尋除尚書令，還錄尚書事，食定州常山郡幹。
