translations.literal: In the first year of Wuping, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyang, and soon appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat, again recording the affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, with income from the fief of Changshan Commandery in Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping he was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyang, soon made Director of the Imperial Secretariat and again put in charge of its affairs, with income from Changshan Commandery in Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 武成時，恆令士開與太后握槊，又出入臥內，遂與太后為亂。

translations.literal: During Wucheng's time, he constantly had Shikai and the empress dowager play pitch-pot, and Shikai also went in and out of the sleeping quarters, whereupon he and the empress dowager engaged in illicit relations.
translations.idiomatic: During Wucheng's reign he often had Shikai and the empress dowager play pitch-pot together. Shikai also entered and left the inner sleeping quarters, and he and the empress dowager became lovers.

sentences.zh: 及武成崩後，彌自放恣。

translations.literal: After Wucheng's death, he indulged himself all the more without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: After Wucheng's death he gave himself over to unrestrained indulgence.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王儼惡之，與領軍大將軍厙狄伏連、侍中馮子琮、書侍御史王子宜、武衛大將軍高舍洛等謀誅之。

translations.literal: Prince of Langye Yan detested him and, together with General-in-Chief of the Guards Kudil Foulian, Palace Attendant Feng Zicong, Supervising Secretary Wang Ziyi, and Great General of the Military Guard Gao Sheluo and others, plotted to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan of Langye hated him and, together with General-in-Chief of the Guards Kudil Foulian, Palace Attendant Feng Zicong, Supervising Secretary Wang Ziyi, Great General of the Military Guard Gao Sheluo, and others, plotted his death.

sentences.zh: 伏連發京畿軍士帖神武千秋門外，並私約束，不聽士開入殿。

translations.literal: Foulian mobilized capital-region troops and posted them outside the Qianqiu Gate of Shenwu, also privately binding them not to let Shikai enter the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Foulian mobilized capital troops and posted them outside Shenwu's Qianqiu Gate, privately ordering them not to let Shikai enter the hall.

sentences.zh: 士開雖為領軍，恆性好內，多早下，縱當直，必須還宅，晚始來。

translations.literal: Although Shikai was General-in-Chief of the Guards, his temperament always favored the inner quarters; he often left early, and even when on duty he had to return home, coming only late.
translations.idiomatic: Although Shikai held the post of General-in-Chief of the Guards, he always preferred the inner palace. He often left early, and even when on duty he had to return home, arriving only late.

sentences.zh: 門禁宿衛，略不在意。

translations.literal: Gate guards and night watchmen he scarcely paid any attention to.
translations.idiomatic: He paid little heed to gate guards or night watchmen.

sentences.zh: 及旦，士開依式早參，厙狄伏連把士開手曰：「今有一大好事。」

translations.literal: At dawn, Shikai attended early audience according to custom, and Kudil Foulian grasped Shikai's hand, saying, "Today there is a great good affair.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Shikai came for the customary early audience. Kudil Foulian seized his hand and said, "Today something wonderful is about to happen.

sentences.zh: 王子宜便授一函云：「有敕，令王向台。」

translations.literal: Wang Ziyi at once handed him a box, saying, "There is an edict ordering the prince to go to the tribunal."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ziyi immediately handed him a box. "There is an edict," he said, "ordering the prince to go to the tribunal."

sentences.zh: 遣軍士防送，禁治書侍御査事。

translations.literal: He sent soldiers to guard and escort him, and forbade the Supervising Secretary from investigating the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers were sent to guard and escort him, and the Supervising Secretary was forbidden to investigate.

sentences.zh: 儼遣都督馮永洛就台斬之。

translations.literal: Yan sent Commander Feng Yongluo to the tribunal to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sent Commander Feng Yongluo to the tribunal to behead him.

sentences.zh: 先是鄴下童謠云：「和士開，當入台。」

translations.literal: Earlier, a children's song in Ye had said, "He Shikai is about to enter the tribunal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a children's song in Ye had run, "He Shikai is about to enter the tribunal.

sentences.zh: 士開謂入上臺，至是果驗。

translations.literal: Shikai thought it meant entering the upper tribunal—and at this time it indeed came true.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai had taken it to mean entering the upper tribunal—and now the prophecy was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 儼令御史李幼業、羊立正將令史就宅簿錄家口，自領兵士縱殿西北角出。

translations.literal: Yan ordered Supervising Secretaries Li Youye and Yang Lizheng to lead clerks to his residence to register his household members, and himself led soldiers out through the northwest corner of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ordered Supervising Secretaries Li Youye and Yang Lizheng to lead clerks to Shikai's residence to register his household, while he himself led troops out through the northwest corner of the palace.

sentences.zh: 斛律明月說後主親自曉告軍士，軍士果散。

translations.literal: Hulü Mingyue persuaded the Later Ruler to personally announce the matter to the soldiers at dawn, and the soldiers indeed dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Mingyue persuaded the Later Ruler to address the troops himself at dawn, and the soldiers dispersed.

sentences.zh: 即斬伏連及王子宜，並支解，棄屍殿西街。

translations.literal: He immediately beheaded Foulian and Wang Ziyi, and also dismembered them, casting their corpses on West Street of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately executed Foulian and Wang Ziyi, dismembered them, and cast their bodies on the palace's West Street.

sentences.zh: 自餘皆辮頭反縛，付趙彥深於涼風堂推問，死者十餘人。

translations.literal: The rest were bound with braided hair and hands reversed behind them, handed over to Zhao Yanshen at Liangfeng Hall for interrogation; more than ten were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were bound with braided hair and hands tied behind their backs and handed to Zhao Yanshen at Liangfeng Hall for interrogation. More than ten were put to death.

sentences.zh: 帝哀悼，不視事數日。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned and did not attend to state affairs for several days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned and neglected state affairs for several days.

sentences.zh: 後追憶不已，詔起復其子道盛通直散騎常侍，又敕其弟士休入內省，參典機密。

translations.literal: Later, recalling him without end, he issued an edict restoring his son Daosheng to Regular Attendant of the Palace Cadre, and also ordered his younger brother Shixiu to enter the Inner Secretariat to participate in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, unable to stop grieving, he issued an edict restoring Shikai's son Daosheng as Regular Attendant of the Palace Cadre and ordering his younger brother Shixiu into the Inner Secretariat to handle confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔贈士開假黃鉞、右丞相、太宰、司徒公，錄尚書事，諡曰文定。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously conferred on Shikai the Golden Battle-Axe, Right Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, and Duke of the Secretariat, with recording of the affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, and gave him the posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously conferred on Shikai the Golden Battle-Axe, the title of Right Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, and Duke of the Secretariat with charge over imperial secretariat affairs, and the posthumous name Wending.

sentences.zh: 士開稟性庸鄙，不窺書傳，發言吐論，唯以諂媚自資。

translations.literal: Shikai's innate character was vulgar and base; he did not look into books or records, and in speech and argument he relied solely on flattery as his resource.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai was vulgar and ignorant by nature. He never read books or records, and in speech and debate relied entirely on flattery.

sentences.zh: 自河清、天統以後，威權轉盛，富商大賈，朝夕填門，聚斂貨財，不知紀極。

translations.literal: From the Heqing and Tiantong periods onward, his authority grew ever greater; rich merchants and great traders filled his gate morning and evening, and he amassed goods and wealth beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: From the Heqing and Tiantong periods onward his power grew ever greater. Rich merchants thronged his gate morning and evening, and he amassed wealth beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 雖公府屬掾，郡縣守長，不拘階次，啟牒即成。

translations.literal: Even staff of public offices and prefectural and county chiefs—without regard to rank—had their petitions approved as soon as submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Even staff of government offices and prefectural and county chiefs, regardless of rank, had their petitions approved on submission.

sentences.zh: 朝士不知廉恥者，多相附會，甚者為其假子，與市道小人丁鄒、嚴興等同在昆季行列。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen who knew no shame mostly attached themselves to him; some went so far as to become his nominal sons, standing in the same fraternal row as market riffraff such as Ding Zou and Yan Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Shameless courtiers flocked to him. Some became his nominal sons, standing as brothers alongside market lowlifes such as Ding Zou and Yan Xing.

sentences.zh: 又有一人士，曾參士開疾患，遇醫人云，王傷寒極重，應服黃龍湯，士開有難色。

translations.literal: There was also one gentleman who once visited Shikai during an illness; encountering a physician, he said the prince's cold injury was extremely severe and he ought to take Yellow Dragon Decoction, and Shikai showed a troubled expression.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when a gentleman visited Shikai during an illness, a physician said the prince's cold injury was extremely severe and he should take Yellow Dragon Decoction. Shikai looked troubled.

sentences.zh: 是人云：「此物甚易，王不須疑惑，請為王先嘗之。」

translations.literal: The man said, "This thing is very easy—Your Highness need not hesitate; allow me to taste it for you first.
translations.idiomatic: The man said, "It is a simple remedy—Your Highness need not hesitate. Let me taste it for you first.

sentences.zh: 一舉便盡。

translations.literal: In one draft he drank it all.
translations.idiomatic: He drained it in one draft.

sentences.zh: 士開深感此心，為之強服，遂得汗病癒。

translations.literal: Shikai was deeply moved by this loyalty and forcibly took the medicine himself, whereupon he sweated and the illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved by this devotion, Shikai forced himself to take the medicine and sweated out the illness.

sentences.zh: 其勢傾朝廷如此。

translations.literal: His power overawed the court to such a degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the degree to which he dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 雖以左道事之者，不隔賢愚，無不進擢；

translations.literal: Even those who served him with heterodox methods—without distinction between worthy and foolish—all were promoted;
translations.idiomatic: Even those who served him through heterodox means, whether worthy or foolish, were promoted without distinction;

sentences.zh: 而正理違忤者，亦頗能含容之。

translations.literal: yet those who opposed him on proper grounds he could also to some extent tolerate.
translations.idiomatic: yet he could also to some extent tolerate those who opposed him on principle.

sentences.zh: 士開見人將加刑戮，多所營救，既得免罪，即令諷論，責其珍寶，謂之贖命物。

translations.literal: When Shikai saw someone about to be punished with execution, he often intervened to save them; once they were spared, he would have them lectured and charged for precious treasures, calling this the price of redeeming one's life.
translations.idiomatic: When Shikai saw someone about to be executed, he often intervened to save them. Once they were spared, he would have them lectured and charged for precious treasures—the price of redeeming one's life.

sentences.zh: 雖有全濟，皆非直道。

translations.literal: Although many were wholly saved, none of it was by the straight path.
translations.idiomatic: Although many lives were saved, none of it was done by upright means.

sentences.zh: 安吐根，安息胡人，曾祖入魏，家於酒泉。

translations.literal: An Tugen was a man of Parthian origin; his great-grandfather entered Wei and the family settled in Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: An Tugen was a Parthian. His great-grandfather had entered Wei and settled the family in Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 吐根魏末充使蠕蠕，因留塞北。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei, Tugen served as envoy to the Rouran and therefore remained in the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wei, Tugen served as envoy to the Rouran and remained on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 天平初，蠕蠕主使至晉陽，吐根密啟本蕃情狀，神武得為之備。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, the Rouran ruler sent envoys to Jinyang, and Tugen secretly reported the conditions of his own realm, enabling Shenwu to prepare against them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping the Rouran ruler sent envoys to Jinyang. Tugen secretly reported conditions in his homeland, enabling Shenwu to prepare defenses.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕果遣兵入掠，無獲而反。

translations.literal: The Rouran indeed sent troops in to plunder but gained nothing and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran did send troops to raid, but gained nothing and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 神武以其忠款，厚加賞賚。

translations.literal: Shenwu, because of his loyalty and sincerity, richly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu richly rewarded him for his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 其後與蠕蠕和親，結成婚媾，皆吐根為行人也。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever peace and marriage alliances were made with the Rouran, Tugen served as the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever peace and marriage alliances were negotiated with the Rouran, Tugen served as envoy.

sentences.zh: 吐根性和善，頗有計策，頻使入朝，為神武親待。

translations.literal: Tugen's nature was gentle and good, and he possessed considerable stratagem; he frequently served as envoy to court and was personally treated with favor by Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Tugen was gentle by nature and shrewd in counsel. He frequently came to court as envoy and was personally favored by Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 在其本蕃，為人所譖，奔投神武。

translations.literal: In his own realm he was slandered by others and fled to join Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In his homeland he was slandered by others and fled to Shenwu for refuge.

sentences.zh: 文襄嗣事，以為假節、涼州刺史、率義侯，稍遷儀同三司，食永昌郡幹。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang succeeded to affairs, he was made Acting Commissioner with Full Powers, Governor of Liang Province, and Marquis of Shuaiyi, and was gradually promoted to Third Rank with Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies, with income from the fief of Yongchang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang succeeded to power, Tugen was made Acting Commissioner with Full Powers, Governor of Liang Province, and Marquis of Shuaiyi, and was gradually promoted to Third Rank with Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies, with income from Yongchang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 皇建中，加開府。

translations.literal: In the Huangjian period he was further made General of the Opening Gate.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangjian he was further made General of the Opening Gate.

sentences.zh: 齊亡年，卒。

translations.literal: In the year Qi fell, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the year Qi fell, he died.

sentences.zh: 穆提婆，本性駱，漢陽人也。

translations.literal: Mu Tipo's original surname was Luo, and he was a man of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Tipo's original surname was Luo, and he came from Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 父超，以謀叛伏法，提婆母陸令萱配入掖庭，提婆為奴。

translations.literal: His father Chao was executed for plotting rebellion; Tipo's mother Lu Lingxuan was assigned to the inner palace, and Tipo became a slave.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chao was executed for plotting rebellion. Tipo's mother Lu Lingxuan was assigned to the inner palace, and Tipo became a slave.

sentences.zh: 後主在繈褓中，令其鞠養，謂之乾阿妳，呼姊姊，遂為胡太后昵愛。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler was still in swaddling clothes, she was ordered to nurse and raise him; he called her "Gan A'ni" and "elder sister," and thus came to be doted on by Empress Dowager Hu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler was still in swaddling clothes, she was ordered to nurse him. He called her "Gan A'ni" and "elder sister," and thus won the affection of Empress Dowager Hu.

sentences.zh: 令萱奸巧多機辯，取媚百端，宮掖之中，獨擅威福，封為郡君。

translations.literal: Lingxuan was cunning and clever, with many stratagems and eloquence; she took a hundred ways to win favor, and within the inner palace alone wielded authority and blessing, and was enfeoffed as Lady of a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxuan was cunning and eloquent, finding a hundred ways to win favor. Within the inner palace she alone wielded power and was enfeoffed as Lady of a Commandery.

sentences.zh: 和士開，高阿那肱皆為郡君義子。

translations.literal: He Shikai and Gao Anagong both became her nominal sons.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai and Gao Anagong both became her nominal sons.

sentences.zh: 天統初，奏引提婆入侍後主，朝夕左右，大被親狎，無所不為。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiantong, she memorialized to bring Tipo in to attend the Later Ruler, day and night at his side; he was greatly favored and intimate, and nothing was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tiantong she petitioned to bring Tipo in to attend the Later Ruler day and night. He was greatly favored and intimate, and nothing was forbidden between them.

sentences.zh: 武平元年，稍遷儀同三司，又加開府，尋授武衛大將軍、秦州大中正。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wuping he was gradually promoted to Third Rank with Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies, and further made General of the Opening Gate; soon he was appointed Great General of the Military Guard and Chief Rectifier of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping he was gradually promoted to Third Rank with Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies and made General of the Opening Gate, and soon appointed Great General of the Military Guard and Chief Rectifier of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 二年，除侍中，轉食樂陵郡幹，寵遇彌隆。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Palace Attendant and transferred to income from the fief of Leling Commandery; favor grew ever more splendid.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Palace Attendant and given income from Leling Commandery; his favor grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 遂至尚書左右僕射、領軍大將軍、錄尚書，封城陽郡王。

translations.literal: He eventually reached Left and Right Vice Directors of the Imperial Secretariat, General-in-Chief of the Guards, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Imperial Secretariat, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Chengyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to Left and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, General-in-Chief of the Guards, and Recorder of Imperial Secretariat Affairs, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Chengyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 贈其父司徒公、尚書左僕射、城陽王。

translations.literal: His father was posthumously conferred Duke of the Secretariat, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Prince of Chengyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father was posthumously conferred Duke of the Secretariat, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Prince of Chengyang.

sentences.zh: 令萱又佞媚穆昭儀，養之為女，是以提婆改姓穆。

translations.literal: Lingxuan also fawned on Honorary Consort Mu and adopted her as a daughter, and for this reason Tipo changed his surname to Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxuan also fawned on Honorary Consort Mu and adopted her as a daughter, which is why Tipo changed his surname to Mu.

sentences.zh: 及穆氏定位，號視第一品，班在長公主之上。

translations.literal: When Lady Mu was established in rank, her title was treated as first rank, and her precedence was above that of senior princesses.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Mu was established in rank, her title was treated as first rank and she took precedence even over senior princesses.

sentences.zh: 自武平三年之後，令萱母子勢傾內外，賣官鬻獄，取斂無厭，每一賜與，動傾府藏。

translations.literal: From after the third year of Wuping, the power of Lingxuan and her son overawed inside and outside; they sold offices and traded in judgments, extracting wealth without satiety—each grant of favor could shake the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: From after the third year of Wuping, Lingxuan and her son dominated court and countryside. They sold offices and traded in judgments, extracting wealth without limit—each act of favor could drain the treasury.

sentences.zh: 令萱則自太后以下，皆受其指麾；

translations.literal: Lingxuan, from the empress dowager downward, all received her commands;
translations.idiomatic: From the empress dowager downward, all obeyed Lingxuan's commands;

sentences.zh: 提婆則唐邕之徒，皆重跡屏氣。

translations.literal: as for Tipo, men such as Tang Yong all walked in double file and held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: as for Tipo, men such as Tang Yong walked in double file and held their breath before him.

sentences.zh: 提婆嘗有罪，太姬於帝前駕之曰：「奴斷我兒！」

translations.literal: Tipo once committed an offense, and the Grand Consort rebuked him before the emperor, saying, "The slave has ruined my son!"
translations.idiomatic: Tipo once committed an offense, and the Grand Consort rebuked him before the emperor: "The slave has ruined my son!"

sentences.zh: 兒謂帝，奴謂提婆也。

translations.literal: Son" meant the emperor; "slave" meant Tipo.
translations.idiomatic: Son" meant the emperor; "slave" meant Tipo.

sentences.zh: 斛律皇后之廢也，太后欲以胡昭儀正位後宮，力不能遂，乃卑辭厚禮，以求令萱。

translations.literal: When Empress Hulü was deposed, the empress dowager wished to establish Honorary Consort Hu as empress of the inner palace, but her strength could not achieve it; she therefore used humble words and rich gifts to win over Lingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Hulü was deposed, the empress dowager wished to make Honorary Consort Hu empress but could not manage it alone. She therefore used humble words and rich gifts to win over Lingxuan.

sentences.zh: 令萱亦以胡氏寵倖方睦，不得已而白後主立之。

translations.literal: Lingxuan also, because Lady Hu's favor and intimacy were then harmonious, against her will informed the Later Ruler to establish her.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxuan, because Lady Hu was then in favor, reluctantly persuaded the Later Ruler to establish her.

sentences.zh: 然意在穆昭儀，每私謂後主曰：「豈有男為皇太子，而身為婢妾？」

translations.literal: Yet her intent was on Honorary Consort Mu, and she often privately said to the Later Ruler, "How can there be a man who is crown prince while his mother remains a maidservant and concubine?
translations.idiomatic: Yet her heart was set on Honorary Consort Mu, and she often said privately to the Later Ruler, "How can a man be crown prince while his mother remains a maidservant and concubine?

sentences.zh: 又恐胡後不可以正義離間，乃外求左道行厭蠱之術，旬朔之間，胡氏遂即精神恍惚，言笑無恆，後主遂漸相畏惡。

translations.literal: She also feared that Empress Hu could not be estranged by upright reasoning, and therefore outwardly sought practitioners of heterodox arts to perform curse-and-poison rites; within ten days or a month, Lady Hu's spirit became confused and her speech and laughter were inconstant, and the Later Ruler gradually came to fear and loathe her.
translations.idiomatic: She also feared that Empress Hu could not be turned aside by honest argument, and so sought out practitioners of sorcery and poison rites. Within weeks Lady Hu became confused in spirit, her speech and laughter erratic, and the Later Ruler gradually came to fear and loathe her.

sentences.zh: 令萱一旦忽以皇后服御衣被穆昭儀，又先別造寶帳，爰及枕席器玩，莫匪珍奇，坐昭儀於帳中，謂後主云：「有一聖女出，將大家看之。」

translations.literal: One day Lingxuan suddenly draped the empress's robes and covers on Honorary Consort Mu, and also separately made a precious canopy, extending to pillows, mats, and curios—nothing that was not rare—and seated the honorary consort in the canopy, saying to the Later Ruler, "A holy woman has appeared; let us all look at her.
translations.idiomatic: One day Lingxuan suddenly draped the empress's robes and covers on Honorary Consort Mu, and had a precious canopy made with pillows, mats, and curios of every rarity. She seated the honorary consort in the canopy and told the Later Ruler, "A holy woman has appeared—come and see.

sentences.zh: 及見，昭儀更相媚悅。

translations.literal: When he saw her, he and the honorary consort were all the more mutually pleased and delighted.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw her, he and the honorary consort were mutually delighted.

sentences.zh: 令萱云：「如此人不作皇后，遣何物人作皇后？」

translations.literal: Lingxuan said, "If a person like this is not made empress, what sort of person should be made empress?
translations.idiomatic: Lingxuan said, "If someone like this is not made empress, what sort of person should be?

sentences.zh: 於是立穆氏為右皇后，以胡氏為左皇后，尋復黜胡，以穆為正嫡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lady Mu was established as Right Empress and Lady Hu as Left Empress; soon Hu was again deposed and Mu made the principal consort.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Mu was then made Right Empress and Lady Hu Left Empress; soon Hu was deposed and Mu made principal consort.

sentences.zh: 引祖珽為宰相，殺胡長仁，皆令萱所為也。

translations.literal: Bringing in Zu Ting as chancellor and killing Hu Changren were both Lingxuan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Bringing in Zu Ting as chancellor and killing Hu Changren were both Lingxuan's work.

sentences.zh: 自外殺生與奪，不可盡言。

translations.literal: Apart from these, killings, grants of life, and seizures of property cannot all be told.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these, the killings, pardons, and seizures of property are beyond full recounting.

sentences.zh: 提婆雖庸品廝濫，而性乃和善，不甚害物。

translations.literal: Although Tipo was vulgar in quality and mixed with the rabble, his nature was yet gentle and good, and he did not greatly harm people.
translations.idiomatic: Although Tipo was a vulgar mediocrity, his nature was gentle and he did not greatly harm people.

sentences.zh: 耽聲色，極奢侈，晚朝早退，全不以公事關懷。

translations.literal: He indulged in music and women to the extreme of luxury, leaving court early and arriving late, wholly unconcerned with public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He indulged in music and women with extreme luxury, leaving court early and arriving late, wholly unconcerned with public affairs.

sentences.zh: 未嘗毒害，士人亦由此稱之。

translations.literal: He never poisoned anyone, and for this reason gentlemen also praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He never poisoned anyone, and for this reason courtiers also spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 晉州軍敗，後主還鄴，提婆奔投周軍，令萱自殺，子孫小大皆棄市，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: When the Jinzhou army was defeated, the Later Ruler returned to Ye; Tipo fled to join the Zhou army, Lingxuan killed herself, and children and adults alike were executed in the marketplace and their household property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jinzhou army was defeated and the Later Ruler returned to Ye, Tipo fled to the Zhou army. Lingxuan killed herself, and the entire family, young and old, was executed in the marketplace and their property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 周武帝以提婆為柱國、宜州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou made Tipo a Pillar of the State and Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou made Tipo a Pillar of the State and Governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 未幾，雲將據宜州起兵，與後主相應，誅死。

translations.literal: Before long, Yun Jiang occupied Yi Province and raised troops in response to the Later Ruler, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Yun Jiang seized Yi Province and raised troops in coordination with the Later Ruler, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 後主及齊氏諸王，並因此非命。

translations.literal: The Later Ruler and all the princes of the Qi clan likewise met untimely deaths because of this.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Ruler and all the princes of the Qi clan likewise met untimely deaths because of this.

sentences.zh: 高阿那肱，善無人也。

translations.literal: Gao Anagong was a man of Shanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Anagong came from Shanwu.

sentences.zh: 父市貴，從神武以軍功封常山郡公，位晉州刺史，贈太尉公。

translations.literal: His father Shigui followed Shenwu and, for military merit, was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshan Commandery, held the post of Governor of Jin Province, and was posthumously conferred Grand Duke.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shigui followed Shenwu and, for military merit, was enfeoffed Duke of Changshan Commandery, served as Governor of Jin Province, and was posthumously made Grand Duke.

sentences.zh: 及阿那肱貴寵，贈成皋王。

translations.literal: When Anagong became honored and favored, Shigui was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: When Anagong rose to honor and favor, Shigui was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 阿那肱初為庫直，每從征討，以功封直城縣男。

translations.literal: Anagong at first served as a palace attendant of the storehouse; each time he followed on campaign, and for merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhicheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Anagong first served as a palace storehouse attendant. He followed on every campaign and, for merit, was enfeoffed Baron of Zhicheng County.

sentences.zh: 天保初，除庫直都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed Commander of Palace Attendants of the Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was made Commander of Palace Storehouse Attendants.

sentences.zh: 四年，從破契丹及蠕蠕，以蹻捷見知。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed in the defeat of the Khitan and the Rouran and was known for swiftness and agility.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he took part in defeating the Khitan and the Rouran and was noted for swiftness and agility.

sentences.zh: 大寧初，除假儀同三司、武衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daning he was appointed Acting Third Rank with Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies and General of the Military Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daning he was made Acting Third Rank with Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies and General of the Military Guard.

sentences.zh: 那肱工於騎射，便僻善事人，每宴射之次，大為武成愛重。

translations.literal: Anagong was skilled at mounted archery and adept at fawning and pleasing people; at each feast and archery contest he was greatly loved and esteemed by Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Anagong was skilled at mounted archery and adept at fawning. At every feast and archery contest Wucheng greatly favored him.

sentences.zh: 又諂悅和士開，尤相褻狎。

translations.literal: He also fawned on and pleased He Shikai and was especially intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: He also fawned on He Shikai and was especially intimate with him.

sentences.zh: 士開每見為之言，由是彌見親待。

translations.literal: Shikai often spoke on his behalf when he saw him, and by this means he was all the more personally treated with favor.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai often spoke on his behalf, and through this he won still greater favor.

sentences.zh: 河清中，除儀同三司，食汾州定陽、仵城二郡幹。

translations.literal: In the Heqing period he was appointed Third Rank with Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies, with income from the fiefs of Dingyang and Wucheng in Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Heqing he was made Third Rank with Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies, with income from Dingyang and Wucheng in Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 以破突厥，封宜君縣伯。

translations.literal: For defeating the Turks he was enfeoffed as Earl of Yijun County.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating the Turks he was enfeoffed Earl of Yijun County.

sentences.zh: 天統初，加開府，除侍中、驃騎大將軍、領軍，別封昌國縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiantong he was further made General of the Opening Gate, appointed Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and General-in-Chief of the Guards, and separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Changguo County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tiantong he was further made General of the Opening Gate, Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and General-in-Chief of the Guards, and separately enfeoffed Marquis of Changguo County.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，除並省右僕射。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler ascended the throne, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Combined Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler ascended the throne, he was made Right Vice Director of the Combined Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武平元年，封淮陰郡王，仍遷並省尚書左僕射，又除並省尚書令、領軍大將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wuping he was enfeoffed as Prince of Huaiyin Commandery, still transferred to Left Vice Director of the Combined Imperial Secretariat, and further appointed Director of the Combined Imperial Secretariat, General-in-Chief of the Guards, and Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping he was enfeoffed Prince of Huaiyin Commandery, made Left Vice Director of the Combined Imperial Secretariat, and further appointed Director of the Combined Imperial Secretariat, General-in-Chief of the Guards, and Governor of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 那肱才技庸劣，不涉文史，識用尤在士開下。

translations.literal: Anagong's talent and skill were mediocre and inferior; he did not involve himself in literature and history, and in knowledge and employment he was especially below Shikai.
translations.idiomatic: Anagong's talents were mediocre. He knew nothing of literature or history, and in judgment he was well below Shikai.

sentences.zh: 而奸巧計數，亦不逮士開。

translations.literal: Yet in cunning stratagem and calculation he also did not reach Shikai.
translations.idiomatic: In cunning and calculation he also fell short of Shikai.

sentences.zh: 既為武成所幸，多令在東宮侍衛，後主所以大寵遇之。

translations.literal: Because he was favored by Wucheng, he was often ordered to attend in the Eastern Palace as guard, and for this reason the Later Ruler greatly favored and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wucheng favored him, he was often assigned to guard the Eastern Palace, which is why the Later Ruler greatly favored him.

sentences.zh: 士開死後，後主謂其識度足繼士開，遂致位宰輔。

translations.literal: After Shikai's death, the Later Ruler said his judgment and capacity were sufficient to succeed Shikai, and thus he reached the rank of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: After Shikai's death the Later Ruler said his judgment was sufficient to succeed Shikai, and thus he rose to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 武平四年，令其錄尚書事，又總知外兵及內省機密。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wuping he was ordered to record the affairs of the Imperial Secretariat and also to oversee external military affairs and the secrets of the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wuping he was ordered to record imperial secretariat affairs and to oversee external military affairs and Inner Secretariat secrets.

sentences.zh: 頓不如和士開、駱提婆母子賣獄鬻官，韓長鸞憎疾良善；

translations.literal: Only he did not, like He Shikai and Mu Tipo and his mother, sell judgments and trade in offices, and Han Changluan hated and detested the good and worthy;
translations.idiomatic: Only he did not, like He Shikai and Mu Tipo and his mother, sell judgments and trade in offices, and Han Changluan hated the good and worthy;

sentences.zh: 而那肱少言辭，不妄喜怒，亦不察人陰私，虛相讒構。

translations.literal: whereas Anagong spoke little, did not rashly show anger or joy, and also did not investigate people's private affairs, falsely slandering and framing them.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Anagong spoke little, did not rashly show anger or joy, and did not investigate private affairs to slander and frame people.

sentences.zh: 遂至司徒公、右丞相，其錄尚書、刺史並如故。

translations.literal: He eventually reached Grand Duke and Right Chancellor, while his recording of the Imperial Secretariat and governorship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to Grand Duke and Right Chancellor, while retaining his secretariat and governorship posts.

sentences.zh: 及周師逼平陽，後主于天池校獵，晉州頻遣馳奏，從旦至午，驛馬三至。

translations.literal: When Zhou troops pressed Pingyang, the Later Ruler was hunting at Tianchi, and Jin Province repeatedly sent urgent memorials by fast relay—from dawn to noon the post horses came three times.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou troops pressed Pingyang, the Later Ruler was hunting at Tianchi. Jin Province sent urgent dispatches repeatedly—from dawn to noon the post horses came three times.

sentences.zh: 那肱云：「大家正作樂，邊境小小兵馬，自是常事，何急奏聞？」

translations.literal: Anagong said, "His Majesty is just enjoying himself—a small band of frontier troops is naturally a common affair; why urgently memorialize and report?
translations.idiomatic: Anagong said, "His Majesty is just enjoying himself—a small band of frontier troops is a common affair. Why report so urgently?

sentences.zh: 向暮，更有使至，雲平陽城已陷賊，方乃奏知。

translations.literal: Toward evening another messenger came, saying Pingyang city had already fallen to the enemy, and only then was it reported and known.
translations.idiomatic: Toward evening another messenger arrived saying Pingyang had already fallen to the enemy—only then was it reported.

sentences.zh: 明即欲引軍，淑妃又請更合圍，所以彌致遲緩。

translations.literal: The next day he wished to lead the army, but the Honored Consort again asked to encircle once more, and for this reason delay grew all the greater.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he wished to lead the army out, but the Honored Consort again asked to complete the encirclement hunt, causing further delay.

sentences.zh: 及軍赴晉州，命那肱率前軍先進，仍總節度諸軍。

translations.literal: When the army went to Jin Province, he ordered Anagong to lead the vanguard in advance and still to command all the armies overall.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched to Jin Province, he ordered Anagong to lead the vanguard and overall command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 後主至平陽城下，謂那肱曰：「戰是邪？

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler reached below Pingyang city, he said to Anagong, "Shall we fight?
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler reached Pingyang he asked Anagong, "Shall we fight?

sentences.zh: 不戰是邪？」

translations.literal: Or shall we not fight?
translations.idiomatic: Or shall we not?

sentences.zh: 那肱曰：「兵雖多，堪戰者不過十萬，病傷及繞城火頭，三分除一。

translations.literal: Anagong said, "Although the troops are many, those fit for battle are no more than a hundred thousand; the sick, wounded, and those around the city fires—remove a third.
translations.idiomatic: Anagong said, "Although our troops are many, no more than a hundred thousand are fit for battle. Counting the sick, wounded, and those fighting fires around the city, subtract a third.

sentences.zh: 昔攻玉壁，援軍來，即退。

translations.literal: In former times at the siege of Yubi, when relief troops came, we withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Yubi, when relief troops arrived we withdrew.

sentences.zh: 今日將士豈勝神武皇帝時？

translations.literal: Can today's officers and soldiers compare with those of Emperor Shenwu's time?
translations.idiomatic: Can today's officers and soldiers compare with those of Emperor Shenwu's day?

sentences.zh: 不如勿戰，守高梁橋。」

translations.literal: Better not to fight, but to hold Gaoliang Bridge."
translations.idiomatic: Better not to fight, but hold Gaoliang Bridge."

sentences.zh: 安吐根曰：「一把子賊，馬上刺取擲汾河中。」

translations.literal: An Tugen said, "A handful of bandits—spear them on horseback and throw them into the Fen River."
translations.idiomatic: An Tugen said, "A handful of bandits—we can spear them from horseback and throw them into the Fen River."

sentences.zh: 帝未決，諸內參曰：「彼亦天子，我亦天子，彼尚能縣軍遠來，我何為守塹示弱？」

translations.literal: The emperor had not decided, and the various inner attendants said, "They too are Son of Heaven, and we too are Son of Heaven—they can still lead an army from afar; why should we hold the trenches and show weakness?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not decided. The inner attendants said, "They are Son of Heaven and we are Son of Heaven—they marched an army from afar. Why should we hold the trenches and show weakness?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This saying is correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is right."

sentences.zh: 於是橋塹進軍，使內參讓阿那肱曰：「爾富貴足，惜性命邪！」

translations.literal: Thereupon they advanced across the bridge and trenches with the army, and had an inner attendant rebuke Anagong, saying, "You are rich and honored enough—do you cherish your life?"
translations.idiomatic: They advanced across the bridge and trenches, and an inner attendant rebuked Anagong: "You are rich and honored enough—are you afraid for your life?"

sentences.zh: 後主從穆提婆觀戰，東偏頗有退者，提婆怖曰：「大家去！

translations.literal: The Later Ruler watched the battle with Mu Tipo; on the eastern flank there was considerable retreating, and Tipo said in fear, "His Majesty, go!
translations.idiomatic: The Later Ruler watched the battle with Mu Tipo. On the eastern flank troops began to fall back, and Tipo cried in fear, "Your Majesty, go!

sentences.zh: 大家去！」

translations.literal: His Majesty, go!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, go!

sentences.zh: 帝與淑妃奔高梁。

translations.literal: The emperor and the Honored Consort fled to Gaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and the Honored Consort fled to Gaoliang.

sentences.zh: 開府奚長樂諫曰：「半進半退，戰家常體。

translations.literal: General of the Opening Gate Xi Changle remonstrated, saying, "Half advancing and half retreating is the usual form of battle.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Opening Gate Xi Changle remonstrated: "Half advancing and half retreating is the normal way of battle.

sentences.zh: 今眾全整，未有傷敗，陛下舍此安之？

translations.literal: Now the masses are wholly intact, with no wounds or defeat—where will Your Majesty go if you abandon this?
translations.idiomatic: Our forces are still intact, with no rout—where will Your Majesty go if you leave now?

sentences.zh: 御馬一動，人情驚亂，願速還安慰之。」

translations.literal: Once the imperial horse moves, people's hearts will be alarmed and disordered—I wish you would quickly return and reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the imperial horse moves, hearts will panic. I beg you to return quickly and reassure the troops.

sentences.zh: 武衛張常山自後至，亦曰：「軍尋收訖，甚整頓，圍城兵亦不動，至尊宜回。

translations.literal: Military Guard Zhang Changshan arrived from behind and also said, "The army will soon be gathered and settled—very well ordered; the besieging troops also do not move. Your Majesty should turn back.
translations.idiomatic: Military Guard Zhang Changshan arrived from the rear and also said, "The army is regrouping in good order and the besiegers are not moving. Your Majesty should turn back.

sentences.zh: 不信臣言，乞將內參往視。」

translations.literal: If you do not believe my words, I beg to take inner attendants to go and look."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not believe me, I beg to take inner attendants and go see for myself."

sentences.zh: 帝將從之，提婆引帝肘曰：「此言何可信！」

translations.literal: The emperor was about to follow this, but Tipo pulled the emperor's elbow, saying, "How can such words be trusted!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to agree, but Tipo pulled his elbow and said, "How can such words be trusted!"

sentences.zh: 帝遂北馳。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon galloped north.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor galloped north.

sentences.zh: 有軍士雷相，告稱：「阿那肱遣臣招引西軍，行到文侯城，恐事不果，故還聞奏。」

translations.literal: There was a soldier named Lei Xiang who reported, saying, "Anagong sent me to recruit and lead the western army; going as far as Wenhou city, fearing the affair would not succeed, I therefore returned to report.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier named Lei Xiang reported, "Anagong sent me to recruit the western army. I reached Wenhou city, but fearing the plot would fail, I returned to report.

sentences.zh: 後主召侍中斛律孝卿，令其檢校。

translations.literal: The Later Ruler summoned Palace Attendant Hulü Xiaoqing and ordered him to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Ruler summoned Palace Attendant Hulü Xiaoqing and ordered an investigation.

sentences.zh: 孝卿固執云：「此人自欲投賊，行至文侯城，迷不得去，畏死妄語耳。」

translations.literal: Xiaoqing firmly maintained, "This man himself wished to defect to the enemy; going as far as Wenhou city, he lost his way and could not leave, and in fear of death spoke falsely—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoqing firmly maintained, "This man wished to defect to the enemy himself. He reached Wenhou city, lost his way, and in fear of death lied—that is all.

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter thereupon lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 還至晉陽，那肱腹心人馬子平告那肱謀反，又以為虛妄，斬子平。

translations.literal: When they returned to Jinyang, Anagong's trusted follower Ma Ziping reported that Anagong was plotting rebellion, and this too was taken as false; Ziping was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned to Jinyang, Anagong's trusted follower Ma Ziping reported that Anagong was plotting rebellion. This too was dismissed as false, and Ziping was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 乃顛沛還鄴，侍衛逃散，唯那肱及閹寺等數十騎從行。

translations.literal: They then fled in distress back to Ye; the guards scattered in flight, and only Anagong and several dozen eunuchs and others followed on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: They fled in distress back to Ye. The guards scattered, and only Anagong and a few dozen eunuchs followed on horseback.

sentences.zh: 復除大丞相。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 後主走度河，令那肱以數千人投濟州關，仍遣覘候周軍進止，日夕馳報。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler fled across the river, he ordered Anagong to lead several thousand men to Jizhou Pass, and still sent him to observe the Zhou army's advance and retreat, reporting day and night by fast relay.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler fled across the river, he ordered Anagong to lead several thousand men to Jizhou Pass and sent him to observe the Zhou army's movements, reporting day and night.

sentences.zh: 那肱每奏云：「周軍未至，且在青州集兵馬，未須南行。」

translations.literal: Each time Anagong reported, he said, "The Zhou army has not yet arrived; for now gather troops and horses at Qing Province—there is no need yet to march south.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Anagong reported he said, "The Zhou army has not yet arrived. Gather troops at Qing Province for now—there is no need to march south yet.

sentences.zh: 及周軍且至關首，所部兵馬皆散，那肱遂降。

translations.literal: When the Zhou army was about to reach the pass head, the troops under his command all scattered, and Anagong thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army reached the pass, his troops scattered and Anagong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 時人皆云，那肱表款周武，必仰生致齊主，故不速報兵至，使後主被禽。

translations.literal: People at the time all said that Anagong had expressed sincerity to Emperor Wu of Zhou and must have hoped to deliver the Qi ruler alive, and therefore did not quickly report that troops had arrived, causing the Later Ruler to be captured.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time said Anagong had pledged loyalty to Emperor Wu of Zhou and hoped to deliver the Qi ruler alive, and therefore delayed reporting the army's arrival, causing the Later Ruler's capture.

sentences.zh: 那肱至長安，授大將軍，封郡公，尋出為隆州刺史。

translations.literal: When Anagong reached Chang'an, he was appointed Great General and enfeoffed as Duke of a Commandery; soon he was sent out as Governor of Long Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Anagong reached Chang'an he was made Great General and enfeoffed Duke of a Commandery, and soon sent out as Governor of Long Province.

sentences.zh: 大象末，在蜀從王謙起兵，誅死。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, in Shu he followed Wang Qian in raising troops and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daxiang, in Shu he followed Wang Qian in raising troops and was executed.

sentences.zh: 初，天保中，文宣自晉陽還鄴，愚僧禿師于路中大叫，呼文宣姓名云：「阿那瑰終破你國。」

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Tianbao period, when Wenzuan returned from Jinyang to Ye, a foolish monk named Tushi shouted on the road, calling Wenzuan by name and saying, "Anagui will ultimately destroy your state.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during Tianbao, when Wenzuan returned from Jinyang to Ye, a foolish monk named Tushi shouted on the road, calling Wenzuan by name: "Anagui will ultimately destroy your state.

sentences.zh: 時蠕蠕主阿那瑰在塞北強盛，帝尤忌之，所以每歲討擊。

translations.literal: At that time the Rouran ruler Anagui was powerful in the northern frontier, and the emperor especially feared him, and for this reason each year launched punitive campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Rouran ruler Anagui was powerful on the northern frontier, and the emperor especially feared him, launching punitive campaigns every year.

sentences.zh: 後亡齊者遂屬高阿那肱云。

translations.literal: Later, when Qi fell, it was attributed to Gao Anagong.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Qi fell, the blame was laid on Gao Anagong.

sentences.zh: 雖作「肱」字，世人皆稱為「瑰」音。

translations.literal: Although the character was written as "gong," people all pronounced it with the sound of "gui."
translations.idiomatic: Although the character was written as "gong," everyone pronounced it as "gui."

sentences.zh: 斯固亡秦者胡，蓋縣定於窈冥也。

translations.literal: This is indeed like "the one who destroyed Qin was the Hu"—the thread was fixed in the hidden realm.
translations.idiomatic: This is indeed like "the one who destroyed Qin was a Hu"—the thread of fate was fixed in the hidden realm.

sentences.zh: 韓鳳，字長鸞，昌黎人也，父永興，開府、青州刺史、高密郡公。

translations.literal: Han Feng, styled Changluan, was a man of Changli; his father Yongxing was General of the Opening Gate, Governor of Qing Province, and Duke of Gaomi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Han Feng, styled Changluan, came from Changli. His father Yongxing was General of the Opening Gate, Governor of Qing Province, and Duke of Gaomi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 鳳少聰察，有膂力，善騎射，稍遷烏賀真、大賢真正都督。

translations.literal: Feng in youth was perceptive and intelligent, had physical strength, and was skilled at mounted archery; he was gradually promoted to Commander of the Wuhazhen and Great Sage Zhen ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was perceptive and strong in youth, skilled at mounted archery, and was gradually promoted to Commander of the Wuhazhen and Great Sage Zhen ranks.

sentences.zh: 後主居東宮，年尚幼，武成簡都督三十人，送令侍衛，鳳在其數。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler resided in the Eastern Palace and was still young, Wucheng selected thirty commanders and sent them to attend as guards; Feng was among the number.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler lived in the Eastern Palace and was still young, Wucheng selected thirty commanders to serve as his guards; Feng was among them.

sentences.zh: 後主親就眾中牽鳳手曰：「都督，看兒來。」

translations.literal: The Later Ruler personally went among the crowd and took Feng's hand, saying, "Commander, look—your boy has come.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Ruler personally went among the crowd, took Feng's hand, and said, "Commander, look—your boy has come.

sentences.zh: 因此被識，數喚共戲。

translations.literal: Because of this he was recognized, and was repeatedly summoned to play together.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he was remembered, and was repeatedly summoned to play with the prince.

sentences.zh: 襲爵高密郡公，位開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Gaomi Commandery and held the rank of General of the Opening Gate with Third Rank Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title Duke of Gaomi Commandery and held the rank of General of the Opening Gate with Third Rank Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 武平二年，和士開為厙狄伏連等矯害，敕咸陽王斛律明月、宜陽王趙彥深在涼風堂推問支黨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuping, when He Shikai was falsely killed by Kudil Foulian and others, an edict ordered Prince of Xianyang Hulü Mingyue and Prince of Yiyang Zhao Yanshen to interrogate the partisans at Liangfeng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuping, when He Shikai was killed by Kudil Foulian and others under a false charge, an edict ordered Prince Hulü Mingyue of Xianyang and Prince Zhao Yanshen of Yiyang to interrogate the partisans at Liangfeng Hall.

sentences.zh: 其事秘密，皆令鳳口傳，然後宣詔敕號令文武。

translations.literal: The affair was secret; all were ordered to pass through Feng's mouth, and only then were edicts and commands proclaimed to civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was secret. Everything passed through Feng's mouth before edicts and commands were proclaimed to civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 禁掖防守，悉以委之。

translations.literal: Defense of the inner palace was wholly entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Defense of the inner palace was wholly entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 除侍中、領軍，總知內省機密。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Attendant and General-in-Chief of the Guards, with overall charge of the secrets of the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Palace Attendant and General-in-Chief of the Guards, with overall charge of Inner Secretariat secrets.

sentences.zh: 祖珽曾與鳳於後主前論事，珽語鳳云：「強弓長槊，容相推謝；

translations.literal: Zu Ting once discussed affairs with Feng before the Later Ruler, and Ting said to Feng, "Strong bows and long spears—we can defer to each other;
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting once discussed affairs with Feng before the Later Ruler and said to him, "Strong bows and long spears—we can defer to each other;

sentences.zh: 軍國謀算，何由得爭？」

translations.literal: but in military and state stratagem, how can we contend?
translations.idiomatic: but in military and state strategy, how can we contend?

sentences.zh: 鳳答云：「各出意見，豈在文武優劣！」

translations.literal: Feng replied, "Each gives his own opinion—how does it lie in the superiority or inferiority of civil and military men!"
translations.idiomatic: Feng replied, "Each gives his own opinion—what does civil or military rank matter!"

sentences.zh: 後主將誅斛律明月，鳳固執不從。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler was about to execute Hulü Mingyue, Feng firmly refused to agree.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler was about to execute Hulü Mingyue, Feng firmly refused to agree.

sentences.zh: 祖珽因有讒言，既誅明月，數日後主不興語，後尋復舊。

translations.literal: Zu Ting thereupon had slanderous words, and after Mingyue was executed, for several days the Later Ruler would not speak with him; later he soon returned to the old ways.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting then slandered him. After Mingyue was executed, the Later Ruler would not speak with Feng for several days; later relations resumed as before.

sentences.zh: 仍封舊國昌黎郡王，又加特進。

translations.literal: He was still enfeoffed as Prince of the old domain, Changli Commandery, and further given Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He was still enfeoffed Prince of his old domain, Changli Commandery, and given Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 及祖珽除北徐州刺史，即令赴任。

translations.literal: When Zu Ting was appointed Governor of Northern Xuzhou, he was immediately ordered to proceed to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Ting was appointed Governor of Northern Xuzhou, he was immediately ordered to proceed to his post.

sentences.zh: 既辭之後，遲留不行。

translations.literal: After he had taken leave, he delayed and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: After taking leave he delayed and did not depart.

sentences.zh: 其省事徐孝遠密告祖珽誅斛律明月後，矯稱敕賜其珍寶財物，亦有不雲敕而徑回取者。

translations.literal: His clerk Xu Xiaoyuan secretly reported that after Zu Ting had Hulü Mingyue executed, he falsely claimed an edict granting him precious treasures and goods, and there were also cases where he took them directly back without claiming an edict.
translations.idiomatic: His clerk Xu Xiaoyuan secretly reported that after Zu Ting had Hulü Mingyue executed, he falsely claimed an edict granting him precious treasures, and in some cases took them without any edict at all.

sentences.zh: 敕令領軍將軍侯呂芬追珽還，引入侍中省鎖禁，其事首尾，並鳳約敕責之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered General-in-Chief of the Guards Hou Lüfen to pursue Ting and bring him back, introduced him into the Palace Attendant's office and locked him up; the whole affair from beginning to end was charged to Feng by edict.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered General-in-Chief of the Guards Hou Lüfen to pursue Ting and bring him back. Ting was confined in the Palace Attendant's office, and Feng was charged by edict with the whole affair from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 進位領軍大將軍，余悉如故。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General-in-Chief of the Guards, with the rest remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Guards, with everything else unchanged.

sentences.zh: 息寶行尚公主，在晉陽賜甲第一區。

translations.literal: His son Baoxing married a princess and was granted a first-rank mansion in Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoxing married a princess and was granted a first-rank mansion in Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 其公主生男滿月，駕幸鳳宅，宴會盡日。

translations.literal: When the princess bore a son at the full month, the imperial carriage visited Feng's residence and feasted the whole day.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess's son reached his full month, the emperor visited Feng's residence and feasted all day.

sentences.zh: 每旦早參，先被敕喚顧訪，出後方引奏事官。

translations.literal: Each morning at early audience he was first summoned by edict for a private audience, and only after leaving were memorial officials introduced.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning at early audience he was first summoned for a private audience by edict; only after he left were memorial officials admitted.

sentences.zh: 若不視事，內省急速者，皆附奏聞。

translations.literal: If the emperor did not attend to affairs, urgent matters of the Inner Secretariat were all attached to memorials and reported.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor did not hold court, urgent Inner Secretariat matters were all attached to memorials and reported.

sentences.zh: 軍國要密，無不經手。

translations.literal: Military and state secrets—none did not pass through his hands.
translations.idiomatic: No military or state secret failed to pass through his hands.

sentences.zh: 東西巡幸，及山水遊戲射獵，獨在禦傍。

translations.literal: On eastern and western tours, and at mountain-and-water outings, hunting, and archery, he alone was at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: On tours east and west, and at outings, hunting, and archery, he alone stayed at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 與高阿那肱、穆提婆共處衡軸，號曰三貴。

translations.literal: Together with Gao Anagong and Mu Tipo he stood at the pivot of power and was called the Three Honored.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Gao Anagong and Mu Tipo he stood at the pivot of power and was called one of the Three Honored.

sentences.zh: 損國害政，日月滋甚。

translations.literal: Harm to the state and injury to government grew day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Harm to the state and injury to government grew worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 壽陽陷沒，鳳與穆提婆聞告敗，握槊不輟曰：「他家物，從他去。」

translations.literal: When Shouyang fell, Feng and Mu Tipo heard the report of defeat and, without stopping their pitch-pot game, said, "Another family's property—let it go.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouyang fell, Feng and Mu Tipo heard the report of defeat and, without stopping their pitch-pot game, said, "Another family's property—let it go.

sentences.zh: 後帝使于黎陽臨河築城戍，曰：「急時且守此作龜茲國子。

translations.literal: Later the emperor sent him to Liyang to build a fortified post by the river, saying, "In an emergency we can hold this and play the sons of Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor sent him to Liyang to build a fortified post by the river, saying, "In an emergency we can hold this and play at being sons of Kucha.

sentences.zh: 更可憐人生如寄，唯當行樂，何用愁為？」

translations.literal: How much more pitiable—human life is like lodging; one should only seek pleasure—why worry?"
translations.idiomatic: How pitiable—human life is but a lodging. One should only seek pleasure. Why worry?"

sentences.zh: 君臣應和若此。

translations.literal: Ruler and ministers responded to each other like this.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ministers spoke to each other like this.

sentences.zh: 鳳恆帶刀走馬，未曾安行，瞋目張拳，有啖人之勢。

translations.literal: Feng always carried a sword and rode at a gallop, never walking at ease; glaring with eyes and clenching fists, he had the air of devouring men.
translations.idiomatic: Feng always carried a sword and rode at a gallop, never walking at ease. Glaring and clenching his fists, he looked ready to devour men.

sentences.zh: 每吒曰：「恨不得剉漢狗飼馬！」

translations.literal: He often shouted, "I wish I could mince Han dogs to feed horses!
translations.idiomatic: He often shouted, "I wish I could mince Han dogs to feed horses!

sentences.zh: 又曰：「刀止可刈賊漢頭，不可刈草。」

translations.literal: He also said, "A blade should only cut off Han bandit heads—it should not cut grass."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "A blade should only cut off Han bandit heads—it should not cut grass."

sentences.zh: 其弟萬歲，及其二子寶行、寶信，並開府儀同，萬歲又拜侍中，亦處機要。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wansui, and his two sons Baoxing and Baoxin, all held the rank of General of the Opening Gate with Third Rank Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies; Wansui was further appointed Palace Attendant and also held confidential posts.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wansui and his two sons Baoxing and Baoxin all held the rank of General of the Opening Gate with Third Rank Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies. Wansui was further made Palace Attendant and also held confidential posts.

sentences.zh: 寶信尚公主，駕復幸其宅，親戚咸蒙官賞。

translations.literal: Baoxin married a princess; the imperial carriage again visited his residence, and relatives all received official rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxin married a princess. The emperor again visited his residence, and relatives all received official rewards.

sentences.zh: 鳳母鮮于，段孝言之從母子姊也，為此偏相參附，奏遣監造晉陽宮。

translations.literal: Feng's mother Xianyu was the maternal elder sister of Duan Xiaoyan's mother's younger brother, and for this reason he was especially attached and joined with him; he memorialized to send Xiaoyan to supervise construction of the Jinyang palace.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's mother Xianyu was the maternal elder sister of Duan Xiaoyan's mother's younger brother, and for this reason he was especially attached to Xiaoyan. He memorialized to send Xiaoyan to supervise construction of the Jinyang palace.

sentences.zh: 陳德信馳驛檢行，見孝言役官夫匠自營宅，即語云：「僕射為至尊起台殿未訖，何用先自營造？」

translations.literal: Chen Dexin rode post horses to inspect; seeing Xiaoyan using official laborers and craftsmen for his own residence, he immediately said, "The Vice Director is building halls and towers for His Majesty that are not yet finished—why use them first for your own construction?
translations.idiomatic: Chen Dexin rode post horses to inspect. Seeing Xiaoyan using official laborers and craftsmen for his own residence, he said at once, "The Vice Director is building halls for His Majesty that are not yet finished—why use them first for your own house?

sentences.zh: 鳳及穆提婆亦遣孝言分工匠為己造宅。

translations.literal: Feng and Mu Tipo also sent Xiaoyan to divide craftsmen to build residences for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Feng and Mu Tipo also sent Xiaoyan to divide the craftsmen and build residences for themselves.

sentences.zh: 德信還，具奏聞。

translations.literal: Dexin returned and fully reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Dexin returned and reported everything.

sentences.zh: 及幸晉陽，鳳又以官馬與他人乘騎，上因此發忿，與提婆並除名。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Jinyang, Feng again lent official horses for others to ride, and for this the emperor grew angry and removed Feng and Tipo from their names.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Jinyang, Feng again lent official horses for others to ride. The emperor grew angry and struck Feng and Tipo from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 亦不露其罪。

translations.literal: He also did not expose their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He did not expose their crimes.

sentences.zh: 仍毀其宅，公主離婚，復被遣尚鄴吏部門參。

translations.literal: He still destroyed their residences, the princesses divorced them, and they were again sent to attend at the gate of the Ministry of Personnel in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed their residences, the princesses divorced them, and they were again sent to attend at the Ministry of Personnel gate in Ye.

sentences.zh: 及後主晉陽走還，被敕喚入內，尋詔復王爵及開府、領軍大將軍，常在左右。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler fled back from Jinyang, he was summoned by edict to enter within; soon an edict restored his princely title and General of the Opening Gate and General-in-Chief of the Guards, and he was constantly at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler fled back from Jinyang, Feng was summoned by edict into the palace. Soon an edict restored his princely title, General of the Opening Gate, and General-in-Chief of the Guards, and he was constantly at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 仍從後主走度河，到青州，並為周軍所獲。

translations.literal: He still followed the Later Ruler in fleeing across the river to Qing Province, and both were captured by Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: He still followed the Later Ruler in fleeing across the river to Qing Province, and both were captured by Zhou troops.

sentences.zh: 鳳被寵要之中，尤嫉人士，朝夕宴私，唯相譖訴。

translations.literal: Among those favored and trusted, Feng especially envied gentlemen; at morning and evening private feasts he only slandered and accused others.
translations.idiomatic: Among the favored, Feng especially envied gentlemen. At morning and evening private feasts he only slandered and accused others.

sentences.zh: 崔季舒等冤酷，皆鳳所為也，每一賜與，動至千萬。

translations.literal: The cruel injustice done to Cui Jishu and others was all Feng's doing; each grant of favor often reached tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: The cruel injustice done to Cui Jishu and others was all Feng's work. Each grant of favor often reached tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 恩遇日甚，彌自驕恣，意色嚴厲，未嘗與人相承接。

translations.literal: Favor grew daily more splendid, and he became all the more arrogant and unrestrained; his expression and color were stern and harsh, and he never received people with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Favor grew daily, and he became ever more arrogant. His expression was stern and harsh, and he never received people with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 朝士諮事，莫敢仰視，動致呵叱，輒詈云：「狗漢大不可耐！

translations.literal: When court gentlemen consulted him on affairs, none dared look up; he often shouted rebukes and immediately cursed, saying, "Han dogs are utterly unbearable!
translations.idiomatic: When courtiers consulted him, none dared look up. He often shouted rebukes and cursed at once: "Han dogs are utterly unbearable!

sentences.zh: 唯須殺卻！」

translations.literal: They need only be killed!
translations.idiomatic: They need only be killed!

sentences.zh: 若見武職，雖廝養末品，亦容下之。

translations.literal: If he saw military officers, even the lowest ranks of grooms and servants, he also treated them with tolerance.
translations.idiomatic: If he saw military officers, even the lowest grooms and servants, he treated them with tolerance.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，位終於隴州刺史。

translations.literal: Serving Sui, he ended his career as Governor of Long Province.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Sui, he ended his career as Governor of Long Province.

sentences.zh: 宦者韓寶業、盧勒叉、齊紹、秦子徵並神武舊左右，唯閣內驅使，不被恩遇。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Han Baoye, Lu Lecha, Qi Shao, and Qin Zizheng were all old attendants of Shenwu, used only for inner-palace driving and service, and did not receive favor.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Han Baoye, Lu Lecha, Qi Shao, and Qin Zizheng were all old attendants of Shenwu, used only for inner-palace service, and received no special favor.

sentences.zh: 曆天保、皇建之朝，亦不至寵倖，但漸有職任。

translations.literal: Through the Tianbao and Huangjian reigns they also did not reach favored intimacy, but gradually held official posts.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Tianbao and Huangjian reigns they also won no special favor, but gradually held official posts.

sentences.zh: 寶業至長秋卿，勒叉等或為中常侍。

translations.literal: Baoye reached Director of the Long Autumn Office; Lecha and the others sometimes became Regular Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Baoye rose to Director of the Long Autumn Office; Lecha and the others sometimes became Regular Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 武成時有曹文摽、夏侯通、伊長游、魯恃伯、郭沙彌、鄧長顒及寶業輩，亦有至儀同食幹者。

translations.literal: In Wucheng's time there were Cao Wenbiao, Xiahou Tong, Yi Changyou, Lu Shibo, Guo Shami, Deng Changyi, and the group of Baoye and others; some also reached Third Rank with income from fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng's time there were Cao Wenbiao, Xiahou Tong, Yi Changyou, Lu Shibo, Guo Shami, Deng Changyi, and Baoye's group; some also reached Third Rank with income from fiefs.

sentences.zh: 唯長顒武平中任參宰相，干預朝權。

translations.literal: Only Changyi in the Wuping period served as assistant to the chancellor and interfered in court power.
translations.idiomatic: Only Changyi in the Wuping period served as assistant to the chancellor and interfered in court power.

sentences.zh: 如寶業及勒叉、齊紹、子徵後並封王，俱自收斂，不過侵暴。

translations.literal: Such as Baoye and Lecha, Qi Shao, and Zizheng—later all were enfeoffed as princes, each gathering wealth for himself, but no more than oppression and violence.
translations.idiomatic: Baoye, Lecha, Qi Shao, and Zizheng were later all enfeoffed as princes. Each gathered wealth for himself, but no more than through oppression and violence.

sentences.zh: 又有陳德信亦參時宰，與長顒並開府封王，俱為侍中、左右光祿大夫，領侍中。

translations.literal: There was also Chen Dexin who participated in governing at the time, and with Changyi both were made General of the Opening Gate and enfeoffed as princes, all becoming Palace Attendants, Left and Right Masters of Luminous Virtue, and Attending Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Chen Dexin, who participated in governing at the time. He and Changyi were both made General of the Opening Gate and enfeoffed as princes, all becoming Palace Attendants, Left and Right Masters of Luminous Virtue, and Attending Palace Attendants.

sentences.zh: 又有潘師子、崔孝禮、劉萬通、研胥光弁、劉通遠、王弘遠、王子立、王玄昌、高伯華、左君才、能純陀、宮鍾馗、趙野叉、徐世凝、苟子溢、斛子慎、宋元寶、康得汪，並於後主之朝，肆其奸佞。

translations.literal: There were also Pan Shizi, Cui Xiaoli, Liu Wantong, Yan Xu Guangbian, Liu Tongyuan, Wang Hongyuan, Wang Zili, Wang Xuanchang, Gao Bohua, Zuo Junzai, Neng Chuntuo, Palace Zhong Kui, Zhao Yecha, Xu Shining, Gou Ziyi, Huzi Shen, Song Yuanbao, Kang Dewang—all of whom in the Later Ruler's reign unleashed their wicked flattery.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Pan Shizi, Cui Xiaoli, Liu Wantong, Yan Xu Guangbian, Liu Tongyuan, Wang Hongyuan, Wang Zili, Wang Xuanchang, Gao Bohua, Zuo Junzai, Neng Chuntuo, Palace Zhong Kui, Zhao Yecha, Xu Shining, Gou Ziyi, Huzi Shen, Song Yuanbao, and Kang Dewang—all of whom in the Later Ruler's reign unleashed their wicked flattery.

sentences.zh: 敗政虐人，古今未有。

translations.literal: Ruining government and tormenting people—nothing like it in antiquity or the present.
translations.idiomatic: Ruining government and tormenting people—nothing like it in antiquity or the present.

sentences.zh: 多授開府，罕止儀同，亦有加光祿大夫，金章紫綬者。

translations.literal: Many were appointed General of the Opening Gate; few stopped at Third Rank Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies; some were also made Masters of Luminous Virtue with golden seals and purple cords.
translations.idiomatic: Many were made General of the Opening Gate; few stopped at Third Rank Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies; some were also made Masters of Luminous Virtue with golden seals and purple cords.

sentences.zh: 多帶中侍中、中常侍，此二職乃至數十人。

translations.literal: Many carried the posts of Attending Palace Attendant and Regular Palace Attendant—these two posts reached several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: Many held the posts of Attending Palace Attendant and Regular Palace Attendant—these two posts alone numbered several tens of men.

sentences.zh: 恆出入門禁，往來園苑，趨侍左右，通宵累日。

translations.literal: They constantly went in and out of the gate guards, back and forth in the gardens and parks, hurrying to attend at the emperor's side, through the whole night and for days on end.
translations.idiomatic: They constantly passed gate guards and moved through gardens and parks, hurrying to attend at the emperor's side through whole nights and days on end.

sentences.zh: 承候顏色，競進諂諛，發言動意，多會深旨。

translations.literal: Receiving and observing his expression, they vied to advance flattery; in speech and intent they mostly matched his deep purposes.
translations.idiomatic: Watching his expression, they vied to flatter him. In speech and intent they mostly matched his deepest purposes.

sentences.zh: 一戲之賞，動逾巨萬，丘山之積，貪吝無厭。

translations.literal: A single reward for one jest often exceeded tens of millions; piled like hills, their greed and stinginess knew no satiety.
translations.idiomatic: A single reward for one jest often exceeded tens of millions. Piled like hills, their greed knew no satiety.

sentences.zh: 猶以波斯狗為儀同、郡休，分其幹祿，神獸門外，有朝貴憩息之所，時人號為解卸査。

translations.literal: They even made a Persian dog General with Equal Privileges and enfeoffed Jun Xiu, dividing income from fiefs with it; outside the Divine Beast Gate there was a place where court nobles rested, and people at the time called it the Disrobing Office.
translations.idiomatic: They even made a Persian dog General with Equal Privileges and enfeoffed Jun Xiu, dividing fief income with it. Outside the Divine Beast Gate was a resting place for court nobles that people called the Disrobing Office.

sentences.zh: 諸閹或在內多日，暫放歸休，所乘之馬，牽至神獸門階，然後升騎。

translations.literal: The various eunuchs, after many days within, were temporarily released to rest; the horses they rode were led to the steps of the Divine Beast Gate, and only then did they mount.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs who had been within the palace many days were temporarily released to rest, the horses they rode were led to the steps of the Divine Beast Gate before they mounted.

sentences.zh: 飛鞭競走，十數為群，馬塵必坌諸貴，爰至唐、趙、韓、駱，皆隱査趨避，不敢為言。

translations.literal: Whipping their horses they raced in competition, ten or more in a group; horse dust was sure to cover the nobles—even Tang, Zhao, Han, and Luo all hid and hurried to avoid it, not daring to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Whipping their horses they raced in groups of ten or more; the dust was sure to cover the nobles—even Tang, Zhao, Han, and Luo all hid and hurried aside, not daring to speak.

sentences.zh: 齊、盧、陳、鄧之徒，亦意屬尚書、卿尹，宰相既不為致言，時主亦無此命。

translations.literal: The group of Qi, Lu, Chen, and Deng also aspired to posts of Director of the Imperial Secretariat and ministers; since the chancellor would not speak for them and the ruler at the time also gave no such command,
translations.idiomatic: The group of Qi, Lu, Chen, and Deng also aspired to posts of Director of the Imperial Secretariat and ministers. Since the chancellor would not speak for them and the ruler gave no such command,

sentences.zh: 唯以工巧矜功，用長顒為太府卿焉。

translations.literal: they relied solely on craftsmanship to boast of merit, and for this reason Changyi was made Director of the Grand Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: they relied solely on craftsmanship to boast of merit, and for this reason Changyi was made Director of the Grand Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 神武時有倉頭陳山提、蓋豐樂，俱以驅馳便僻，頗蒙恩遇。

translations.literal: In Shenwu's time there were household stewards Chen Shanti and Gai Fengle, both of whom, through swift service and fawning, received considerable favor.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenwu's time there were household stewards Chen Shanti and Gai Fengle, both of whom through swift service and fawning received considerable favor.

sentences.zh: 魏末，山提通州刺史，豐樂嘗食典禦。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei, Shanti reached Governor of Tong Province, and Fengle once served as Director of Palace Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wei, Shanti reached Governor of Tong Province, and Fengle once served as Director of Palace Provisions.

sentences.zh: 又有劉郁斤、趙道德、劉桃枝、梅勝郎、辛洛周、高舍洛、郭黑面、李銅鍉、王恩洛，並為神武驅使。

translations.literal: There were also Liu Yujin, Zhao Daode, Liu Taozhi, Mei Shengliang, Xin Luozhou, Gao Sheluo, Guo Heimian, Li Tongti, and Wang Enluo—all driven in service by Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Liu Yujin, Zhao Daode, Liu Taozhi, Mei Shengliang, Xin Luozhou, Gao Sheluo, Guo Heimian, Li Tongti, and Wang Enluo—all driven in service by Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 天保、大寧之朝，漸以貴盛。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao and Daning reigns they gradually became honored and powerful.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao and Daning reigns they gradually became honored and powerful.

sentences.zh: 至武平時，山提等皆以開府封王。

translations.literal: By Wuping, Shanti and the others were all made General of the Opening Gate and enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: By Wuping, Shanti and the others were all made General of the Opening Gate and enfeoffed as princes.

sentences.zh: 其不及武平者則追贈王爵。

translations.literal: Those who did not reach Wuping were posthumously enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: Those who did not live to Wuping were posthumously enfeoffed as princes.

sentences.zh: 雖賜與無貲，顧眄深重，乃至陵忽宰輔，然皆不得干預朝政。

translations.literal: Although their grants of favor were not lavish, the weight of their glances was deep, reaching even to contempt for chief ministers—yet none could interfere in court government.
translations.idiomatic: Although their grants of favor were not lavish, the weight of their glances ran deep, even to contempt for chief ministers—yet none could interfere in court government.

sentences.zh: 武平時有胡小兒，俱是康阿馱、穆叔兒等富家子弟，簡選黠慧者數十人以為左右，恩眄出處，殆與閹官相埒。

translations.literal: In the Wuping period there were Hu youths who were all wealthy household sons such as Kang A'tuo and Mu Shu'er; several tens of clever and bright ones were selected as attendants at the emperor's side, and the favor and glances they received in going out and coming in nearly equaled the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuping period there were Hu youths, all wealthy household sons such as Kang A'tuo and Mu Shu'er. Several tens of clever ones were selected as attendants at the emperor's side, and the favor they received nearly equaled the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 亦有至開府儀同者。

translations.literal: Some also reached General of the Opening Gate with Third Rank Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Some also reached General of the Opening Gate with Third Rank Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 其曹僧奴、僧奴子妙達，以能彈胡琵琶，甚被寵遇，俱開府封王。

translations.literal: Among them, Cao Sengnu and Sengnu's son Miaoda, because they could play the foreign pipa, were greatly favored and treated well, and both were made General of the Opening Gate and enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: Among them, Cao Sengnu and Sengnu's son Miaoda, because they could play the foreign pipa, were greatly favored, and both were made General of the Opening Gate and enfeoffed as princes.

sentences.zh: 又有何海及子洪珍，開府封王，尤為親要。

translations.literal: There were also He Hai and his son Hongzhen, made General of the Opening Gate and enfeoffed as princes, especially intimate and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: There were also He Hai and his son Hongzhen, made General of the Opening Gate and enfeoffed as princes, especially intimate and trusted.

sentences.zh: 洪珍侮弄權勢，鬻獄賣官。

translations.literal: Hongzhen mocked and wielded power, selling judgments and trading in offices.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhen mocked and wielded power, selling judgments and trading in offices.

sentences.zh: 其何硃弱、史醜多之徒十數人，咸以能舞工歌及善音樂者，亦至儀同開府。

translations.literal: The group of more than ten such as He Zhuoruo and Shi Chouduo—all skilled at dancing, singing, and music—also reached Third Rank Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies and General of the Opening Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The group of more than ten such as He Zhuoruo and Shi Chouduo—all skilled at dancing, singing, and music—also reached Third Rank Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies and General of the Opening Gate.

sentences.zh: 閹官猶以宮掖驅馳，便蕃左右，漸因昵狎，以至大官。
