translations.literal: Eunuchs still drove in the inner palace and attended frequently at the emperor's side; gradually through intimacy they reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs still served in the inner palace and attended frequently at the emperor's side; gradually through intimacy they reached high office.

sentences.zh: 倉頭始自家人，情寄深密，及於後主，則是先朝舊人，以勤舊之勞，致此叨竊。

translations.literal: Household stewards began as family servants, with deep and intimate attachment; by the time of the Later Ruler they were old men of the former reign, and through merit of long service reached this usurpation of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Household stewards began as family servants with deep intimate attachment. By the Later Ruler's time they were old men of the former reign, and through long service reached this usurpation of rank.

sentences.zh: 至於胡小兒等，眼鼻深險，一無可用，非理愛好，排突朝貴，尤為人士之所疾惡。

translations.literal: As for the Hu youths and the like, with deep eyes and prominent noses, wholly useless in every way, yet irrationally loved and favored, pushing aside and offending court nobles—they were especially hated and detested by gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Hu youths and the like, with deep-set eyes and prominent noses, wholly useless in every way, yet irrationally favored, pushing aside court nobles—they were especially hated by gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 其以音樂至大官者：沈過兒，官至開府儀同；

translations.literal: Those who through music reached high office: Shen Guo'er reached General of the Opening Gate with Third Rank Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies;
translations.idiomatic: Those who through music reached high office: Shen Guo'er reached General of the Opening Gate with Third Rank Equal Privileges to the Three Excellencies;

sentences.zh: 王長通，年十四五便假節、通州刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Changtong, at fourteen or fifteen, was made Acting Commissioner with Full Powers and Governor of Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Changtong, at fourteen or fifteen, was made Acting Commissioner with Full Powers and Governor of Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 時又有開府薛榮宗，常自雲能使鬼。

translations.literal: At the time there was also General of the Opening Gate Xue Rongzong, who often said himself that he could command ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was also General of the Opening Gate Xue Rongzong, who often claimed he could command ghosts.

sentences.zh: 及周兵之逼，言於後主曰：「臣已發遣斛律明月將大兵在前去。」

translations.literal: When Zhou troops pressed close, he said to the Later Ruler, "I have already dispatched Hulü Mingyue with a great army to go ahead.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou troops pressed close, he told the Later Ruler, "I have already dispatched Hulü Mingyue with a great army to go ahead.

sentences.zh: 帝信之。

translations.literal: The emperor believed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 經古塚，榮宗謂舍人元行恭：「是誰塚？」

translations.literal: Passing an ancient tomb, Rongzong said to Attendant Yuan Xinggong, "Whose tomb is this?
translations.idiomatic: Passing an ancient tomb, Rongzong asked Attendant Yuan Xinggong, "Whose tomb is this?

sentences.zh: 行恭戲之曰：「林宗塚。」

translations.literal: Xinggong joked with him, saying, "It is Linzong's tomb."
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong joked, "It is Linzong's tomb."

sentences.zh: 復問：「林宗是誰？」

translations.literal: He asked again, "Who is Linzong?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "Who is Linzong?"

sentences.zh: 行恭曰：「郭元貞父。」

translations.literal: Xinggong said, "Guo Yuanzhen's father."
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong said, "Guo Yuanzhen's father."

sentences.zh: 榮宗前奏曰：「臣向見郭林宗從塚出，著大帽、吉莫靴，棰馬鞭，問臣：'我阿貞來不？'」

translations.literal: Rongzong stepped forward and memorialized, "Your subject just now saw Guo Linzong come out of the tomb, wearing a great hat and jimo boots, wielding a horse whip, and ask your subject, 'Has my A'zhen come or not?'"
translations.idiomatic: Rongzong stepped forward and reported, "Your subject just saw Guo Linzong come out of the tomb, wearing a great hat and jimo boots, wielding a horse whip, and ask me, 'Has my A'zhen come or not?'"

sentences.zh: 是時群妄，多皆類此。

translations.literal: At that time such group delusions were mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: At that time such collective delusions were mostly of this sort.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古諺有之，「人之多幸，國之不幸。」

translations.literal: The commentary says: An old saying has it, "When men are too fortunate, the state is unfortunate.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: An old saying has it, "When men are too fortunate, the state is unfortunate.

sentences.zh: 然則寵私為害，自古忌之。

translations.literal: Thus private favor is harmful—since antiquity it has been dreaded.
translations.idiomatic: Thus private favor is harmful—it has been dreaded since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 大則傾國亡身，小則傷賢害政，率由斯也，所宜誡焉。

translations.literal: Greatly it overturns states and destroys persons; in small measure it injures the worthy and harms government—all proceed from this, and one ought to take warning from it.
translations.idiomatic: On a great scale it overturns states and destroys lives; on a small scale it injures the worthy and harms government—all proceed from this, and one ought to take warning.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「殷鑒不遠，近在夏後之世。」

translations.literal: The Odes say, "The mirror of Yin is not far off—it is in the age of the Xia successor.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "The mirror of Yin is not far off—it is in the age of the Xia successor.

sentences.zh: 觀夫魏氏以降，亦後來之殷鑒矣。

translations.literal: Observing from the Wei dynasty onward, it is likewise a mirror of Yin for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Observing from the Wei dynasty onward, it is likewise a mirror of Yin for later ages.

sentences.zh: 為國家者，可無鑒之哉？

translations.literal: For those who govern a state, can they fail to take it as a mirror?
translations.idiomatic: For those who govern a state, can they fail to take it as a mirror?
